And he preserves these for himself; he attains union with the Sun. He draws up four times; he offers twice. Thus he obtains the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ as the sacrificial rite, [as well as] the animal sacrifice (paśubandha). [The parts of the body are: the two breasts, the two testicles, the penis, and the downward breath. And he preserves these for himself; he attains union with the Sun. He draws up four times; he offers twice.

{2.3.7.4} The fuel-stick is the seventh. By this, he attains the seven-hotṛ sacrifice as a sacrificial rite, the Soma sacrifice; he preserves the seven vital breaths in his head, attains union with Āditya, pours out four times, offers twice, wipes twice, and consumes twice. By this, he attains the ten-hotṛ sacrifice as a sacrificial rite, the year; he preserves his entire self without omission, and attains union with Āditya.

Anuvāka 8 {2.3.8.1} Prajāpati desired, "May I procreate. He performed austerity. He became pregnant. He became tawny and dark-brown. Therefore, a woman who is pregnant becomes dark-brown while she is still tawny. As he was being born with the fetus, he exhausted himself. Being exhausted, he became black and dark-brown. Therefore, one who is exhausted becomes black and dark-brown. Only his breath remained alive.

{2.3.8.2} By means of that *asu*, he created the Asuras. That is the "Asura-nature" (*asuratva*) of the Asuras. He who thus knows the Asura-nature of the Asuras becomes possessed of *asu*; the Asuras do not abandon him. Having created the Asuras, he thought of himself as a father. Following that, he created the Pitṛs (Fathers). That is the "Father-nature" (*pitṛtva*) of the Pitṛs. He who thus knows the Father-nature of the Pitṛs becomes like a father to his own people.

{2.3.8.3} His fathers go to his call. Having created the fathers, he became despondent; after that, he created human beings. That is the "human-ness" (*manuṣyatva*) of human beings. He who knows thus the human-ness of human beings becomes possessed of mind; Manu does not desert him. For him, having created human beings, [the state] was "among the gods by day" (*divā devatrā*); after that, he created the gods. That is the "god-ness" (*devatva*) of the gods. He who knows thus the god-ness of the gods—

By day indeed he belongs to the gods. These, then, are the four waters: the gods, humans, the fathers, and the asuras. For one who knows this, among all these [beings] he becomes like the water in the sky. The exponents of sacred knowledge (*brahmavādinaḥ*) say: "Whoever should know this—from whence it blows, what it blows toward, and what it blows against—he shall attain a full lifespan; he shall not die before his time; he shall be rich in cattle; and he shall obtain offspring—whoever knows this. *Anuvāka 9 {2.3.9.1}* The exponents of sacred knowledge say: "Whoever should know this—from whence it blows, what it blows toward, and what it blows against—he shall attain a full lifespan; he shall not die before his time; he shall be rich in cattle; and he shall obtain offspring—whoever knows this."

{2.3.9.2} Since he purifies himself from this [world], since he purifies toward that [world], since he purifies completely toward that [world], he attains a full lifespan; he does not die before his time. He becomes possessed of cattle; he obtains offspring. He purifies himself from the waters; he purifies toward the waters; he purifies completely toward the waters.

{2.3.9.3} It purifies for her; it purifies toward her; it purifies completely toward her. It purifies from Agni; it purifies toward Agni; it purifies completely toward Agni. It purifies from the intermediate space; it purifies toward the intermediate space; it purifies completely toward the intermediate space. It purifies from Āditya.

He purifies toward Āditya; he purifies himself toward Āditya. He purifies from the sky; he purifies toward the sky; he purifies himself toward the sky. He purifies from the quarters; he purifies toward the quarters; he purifies himself toward the quarters. When he blows from the east, having become the vital breath (*prāṇa*), he blows from the east.

Therefore, when it blows from the east, all creatures rejoice, for breath is dear to creatures. He who knows this becomes as dear to creatures as breath itself. Indeed, this wind is simply breath. Now, when it blows from the south, it blows from the south having become Mātariśvan; therefore, one should know that it blows from the south. It blows toward all the quarters.

"He blows through all the quarters; he blows along all the quarters"—this indeed is Mātariśvan himself. Now, when he blows from behind, having become Pavamāna, he blows from behind. For one who knows this, they bring what is purified; they offer what is purified; he eats what is purified. This one, indeed, is Pavamāna himself.

{2.3.9.7} Now, when he blows from the north, having become Savitṛ himself, he blows from the north; he becomes like Savitṛ among his own people, for one who knows thus. Indeed, he is Savitṛ himself. Those who speak ill of him as he approaches from the east—whatever evils are his from the front, those they strike away. Other evils follow after them from the front. Then, those who speak ill of him as he approaches from the south...

{2.3.9.8} Those evils that are on his right side—those they strike away from him. Other evils follow after them on the right. Then, those who speak ill of him as he comes from behind—those evils that are behind him—those they strike away from him. Other evils follow after them behind. Then, those who speak ill of him as he comes from the north—those evils that are on his north side—those they strike away from him.

{2.3.9.9} The other evils attend from the north. Therefore, one who knows this should dance about as it were, move forward as it were, and speak with his eyes wide open as it were; he should act as if singing, as if snorting, and as if bellowing. [He should do this thinking: "May they not revile me, and may they drive away my evil. In whichever direction he intends to go for gain, when the wind blows toward that direction, then he should set out or run forward.
He who knows this—pleasure alone, when bitten and arranged, flows forth as fragrance; his fame goes before him to that region; and his subjects become desirous of giving to him.

Anuvāka 10 {2.3.10.1} Prajāpati created King Soma. The three Vedas were created after him. He placed them in his hand. Now there was Sītā Sāvitrī; she desired King Soma, and she also desired Śraddhā. She approached her father Prajāpati. He said to her: "Homage be to you, O Blessed One! I come to you."

{2.3.10.2} "I approach you; I desire King Soma, and he desires Faith. Having thus prepared for her a *sthāgara* ornament, he explains the *daśahotṛ* formula in front, the *caturhotṛ* to the south, the *pañcahotṛ* behind, the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ* to the north, and the *saptahotṛ* above; and having adorned her face with the *sambhāras* and the *patnīs*.

He went toward her half-way. Seeing her, he said, "Come back to me. She said to him, "Tell me your reward; tell me this: what is in your hand? He gave her the three Vedas. Therefore, women always seek their own enjoyment. Thus, whoever should desire, "May I be beloved," [should act accordingly].

{2.3.10.4} Or, for whomsoever he may desire, "May he become dear," for him he should fashion this *sthāgara* ornament. Having explained the *daśahotṛ* formula in the east, the *caturhotṛ* in the south, the *pañcahotṛ* in the west, the *ṣaḍḍhotṛ* in the north, and the *saptahotṛ* above; and having adorned his face with the *sambhāras* and the *patnīs*, he should go toward half of him. Verily, he becomes dear.

Anuvāka 11 {2.3.11.1} Brahmā created the Ātman-possessor (Ātmanvat). He desired: "May I be united with my own self. He called out, "Ātman! Ātman! To him, the tenth [call] responded when invoked. Thus he became Daśahūta ("the one invoked ten times"). Indeed, this is his name, Daśahūta; yet, although he is Daśahūta, they call him Daśahotṛ ("the ten-invoker") cryptically. For the gods, as it were, love the cryptic.

He called out, "Ātman! Ātman! To him, being called for the seventh time, he responded. Thus he became Saptahūta (the one called seven times). Indeed, this is his name, Saptahūta; yet, though he is Saptahūta, they call him Saptahotṛ (the seven Hotṛ-priests) cryptically, for the gods are fond of the cryptic. He called out, "Ātman! Ātman! To him, being called for the sixth time, he responded. Thus he became Ṣaḍḍhūta (the one called six times).

This one is indeed named Ṣaḍdhūta. Although he is Ṣaḍdhūta, they call him Pañcahotṛ by an indirect name, for the gods, as it were, love the indirect. He called out, "To me! To me! (ātman ātman). To him, the fifth call responded. Thus he became Pañcahūta. This one is indeed named Pañcahūta. Although he is Pañcahūta, they call him Pañcahotṛ by an indirect name.

{2.3.11.4} For the gods, as it were, prefer what is indirect. He addressed himself by his own name, "Ātman! Ātman! To him he responded when called for the fourth time. Thus he became Caturhūta (the one called four times). Indeed, this is his name, Caturhūta; yet they call him Caturhotṛ (the four-priest) by an indirect name, for the gods, as it were, prefer what is indirect. He said to him: "It was you who, being called, first responded to me most closely. Through you, these [gods] shall be revealed."

Therefore, indeed, they call these the "Four Hotṛs. Consequently, among sons, one who is obedient is most dear; he is the nearest and most dear. He who knows this becomes the nearest and most dear to Brahman.

Prapāṭhaka 4, Anuvāka 1 Pleasant as a householder, a guest in the dwelling, come to this our sacrifice, O wise one. Having struck down all assailants, O Agni, bring hither the provisions of those who act as enemies. O Agni, be strong for great good fortune; may thy splendors be most excellent. Secure for us a well-governed household lordship; trample down the powers of those who act as enemies. O Agni, that person who from around us seeks to harm us, like a wolf or a robber—[him do thou overcome].

{2.4.1.2} O slayer of Vṛtra, slay them! Bring us wealth! O Agni, whoever assails us—whether he be an equal or a stranger—let nothing of him remain, as if of fuel being consumed by fire. O Indra, you are the overcomer, the god whose prowess is well-known, the slayer of Vṛtra, the one of many insights. Drive away all our enemies, O Indra, toward the east.

{2.4.1.3} Drive away those from the west, O Overcomer; drive away those from the north, and away, O Hero, those from the south. So that we may rejoice in your protection. We incite that Indra for the slaying of the great Vṛtra. May he become the bull, the showerer of blessings. I yoke the booty-seeking chariot with the two bay steeds. Our sacred prayers have reached him who accepts them with favor. By his greatness, Indra has forced asunder the two worlds, heaven and earth, as he struck down the Vṛtras without being resisted.

{2.4.1.4} We invoke Agni Sviṣṭakṛt—the bearer of oblations, the subduer of adversaries, the slayer of demons, the victor in battles, the radiant, the shining, the wise one. We invoke him; we invoke him; we invoke him. O Agni, make that well-offered; O God, overcome all hostile armies. Shining forth, show us a wide path. Bestow upon us a life full of light and undecaying. Mortals, bearing oblations, praise you, O divine Agni.

I deem you to be Jātavedas; may you carry the oblations in due succession. O Jātavedas, carry us across all difficulties, as one crosses over a river with a boat through perils. O Agni, being praised with a mind like that of Atri, be the protector of our bodies. May Pūṣan follow after our cows; may Pūṣan protect our horses; may Pūṣan win booty for us. May Pūṣan know all these regions.

{2.4.1.6} May he lead us by the path most free from fear; may he, the giver of well-being, the passionless one, possessing all heroes, go before us, never failing, knowing the way. {F Thou} {Ānanda. Thou} {BI Thy own} {Thou}, O Agni, art far-extending; thou art the beloved, the excellent invoker. Through thee they extend the sacrifice. Agni drives away the demons; he is of bright luster, immortal, pure, purifying, and worthy of praise. O Agni, protect us from distress.

{2.4.1.7} O God, burn down those who seek to harm us with your most scorching flames; O ageless Agni, you slay the devourer as you shine among mortals in your own dwelling, O observer of pure vows. O Vāta, blow hither healing medicine; O Vāta, blow away whatever is disease, for you are the possessor of all remedies and you move as the messenger of the gods. These two winds blow here.

{2.4.1.8} From the ocean, from the far distance—may one [wind] blow strength to me; may the other blow away whatever is harmful. O Vāta, that treasure of immortality which is placed in your house yonder—from that give us life; from that grant us medicine; from that bring us great prosperity. May Vāta blow medicine upon us, bringing health and delight to our heart.

{2.4.1.9} May he prolong our lifespans. You, O Agni, are *ayās* (unwearied). Being *ayās*, you are established with a well-disposed mind; being *ayās*, you carry the oblation. As *ayās*, bestow healing upon us. Agni, sacrificed and invoked, may he, consecrated by *svāhā*, fulfill our desires. This homage is for the gods, who have gone their own way. Kāma (Desire) alone rules as sovereign over all that has been and all that is to be.

{2.4.1.10} He has spread himself out across this world; the Lord releases the seasons. At the beginning, desire arose within it—that which was the first seed of the mind. They discovered the bond of Being in Non-being, having perceived it in their hearts through inspired thought. O Manyu, together with you on the same chariot, breaking down [the enemy] in boldness, exulting, O Marut-like one, men with sharp arrows, whetting their weapons, advance like fires in form.

{2.4.1.11} Manyu is Bhaga; Manyu indeed was the god. Manyu is the Hotṛ, Varuṇa, the all-knowing. The people, seeking the gods, praise Manyu. Protect us, O Manyu, with your heat and with your toil. You, O Agni, are the pure upholder of vows. Seat the gods here for the sake of carrying the oblation, O Agni. Now, bearing the vows, the protector of vows, the undeceivable one, sacrificing to the gods, ageless and possessing excellent heroes, bestowing jewels, O Agni, you who are easy to find—protect us that we may live, O Jātavedas!

O missile of the eye! O missile of the mind! O missile of speech! O missile of the sacred word (*brahman*)! That one who, being malevolent, assails me—O Agni, make him weaponless by means of your weapon. He who, being malevolent, assails me with his eye, with his mind, with his speech, or with the sacred word—by that very weapon of yours, O Agni, make that person weaponless. Whatever he offers with his mind, whatever with his speech, with sacrifices, with *yajus*-formulas, or with oblations; [all that shall be turned against him.]

{2.4.2.2} Let Death, in agreement with Destruction, strike down his oblations before his appointed time. Let the sorcerers, Destruction, and the demon destroy him; let them slay his truth with falsehood. Impelled by Indra, let them churn away his clarified butter. May that which he does not prosper! I destroy the oblation prepared by him who has wrought terror for me. Both your arms are turned backward; I bind your mouth shut.

I unbind your arms; I unbind your mouth, by the sacred word (*brahman*) of the divine Agni. Whatever you have done, I have destroyed it all, before the *vaṣaṭ*-call of that [enemy]. Make our sacrifice among the gods; let our sacrifice be well-offered. Let not hostile powers reach us, O Agni, whether they be near or far, from the rival who seeks to harm us.

{2.4.2.4} With the *vaṣaṭ*-call as my thunderbolt, I strike down the spell that has been prepared. Whoever—by night or by day, in the evening or in the morning—seeks to consume me, him, our rival, we cause to fall today with Indra’s thunderbolt. You are the dwelling-place of Indra; I enter you, along with my cattle and my horses, together with all that is mine. I praise Agni, the wise one.

{2.4.2.5} By means of the *gir* (song), the accomplishment of the sacrifice—[the song] which is responsive and full of intent—O Agni, may we be able to master the power of the divine steed. May we cross beyond all hostilities. Protect me, you two who are of one mind, of one dwelling, of one consciousness, and of one seed. Both of you, O Jātavedas, protect me; be auspicious to us today. Creating for yourself a path that is easy to traverse and free from weariness.

The sharp-horned bull, flaming brightly, beholding his ancient dwelling place, Agni has stretched out the celestial thread. You, O Agni, are our thread and our bridge; you are the path that leads to the gods. By you, O Agni, may we ascend to the high ridge; then may we rejoice in the shared banquet with the gods. Release us from the highest bond, untie the middle bond, and loosen the lowest bonds so that we may live.

{2.4.2.7} O Soma, in your service, bearing the mind within our bodies, may we, possessing offspring, attain prosperity. The goddess Indrāṇī, fortunate and having a noble husband, won her husband by means of the *aṃśu* stalk. Thirty *yojanas* are her hips; she bears the mighty Indra in her lap. Truly, the earth is named Senā, the winner of wealth; she is the all-encompassing Aditi, whose skin is like the sun. The goddess Indrāṇī is victorious and bestowing gifts.

{2.4.2.8} May that goddess, who is easily invoked, grant us protection. I have brought you here; you have entered within. Stand firm, unshakable. Let all the people desire you. Let the kingdom not fall away from you. Firm is the sky, firm is the earth; firm is this entire world. Firm indeed are these mountains; firm is this king of the people. Be right here; do not waver.

Like a mountain, immovable; like Indra, stand firm here. Maintain the kingdom here. Overcome those who attack us. Let the enemies be beneath us. Stand like Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, conquering the waters and the fields. Indra has established him with a firm oblation. For him the gods have spoken in favor, as has this Brahmaṇaspati.

Anuvāka 3 {2.4.3.1} O men, for the pleasure of the fathers, through this sacred prayer (*brahman*), may you never harm the unaging axle. When, O Vasiṣṭhas, you bestowed vigor upon Indra with the *Śakvarī* verses and with a mighty roar; May the purifying Sarasvatī, rich in spoils and possessing strength, desire our sacrifice through her wisdom, she who is the source of wealth. O Sarasvatī, lead us toward greater prosperity; do not falter, nor fail us with your milk. Be pleased with our friendship and our service.

{2.4.3.2} May we not go from you to desolate fields. I offer the oblation with reverence; I spread the sacrificial grass for Agni. The butter-laden ladle is extended; the well-fashioned hymn has been offered. The dwelling-place on the seat of the earth has been established; the sacrifice has been fixed like the eye upon the sun. Hitherward I call Indra, for victory, to win the prize. May he be ours alone. From yonder we call Indra hitherward—he who wins cattle, wins wealth, and wins horses.

{2.4.3.3} Enjoy this sacrifice of ours at our invocation! O Lord of the Bay Steeds, we make you our ally. You are born pure from your two mothers, unsullied; you arose as the joyous sage from Vivasvat. Increasing you with clarified butter, O Agni, when you are invoked, your smoke became your banner resting in heaven. Agni was the first among the deities; of those who have come together, Viṣṇu was the highest. Having gathered the gods for the sake of the sacrificer, come to us with this oblation through consecration.

O Agni and Viṣṇu, you two possess supreme heat and great majesty. O powerful ones, do you grant [this] to the guardians of the consecration, being in harmony with all the gods worthy of sacrifice. Bestow the consecration upon this sacrificer! For that very reason, Viṣṇu is praised for his heroic power—he who, like a fearsome beast, wanders and dwells in the mountains, in whose three wide strides all the worlds abide. Now, does a mortal man not desire to gain, he who offers gifts to Viṣṇu, the wide-striding?

{2.4.3.5} He who, with a focused mind, would sacrifice—may he win over for himself such a heroic one. Viṣṇu strode across this very earth, bestowing it upon Manu for his domain. Firm are his people, the singers; he of noble birth has created a wide dwelling-place. Three times this earth, rich in light, has this god strode across by his greatness. May Viṣṇu be preeminent, stronger than the strong, for the name of this steadfast one is truly wondrous.

The Hotṛ priest of the sacrifice, whose chariot is radiant, the bright banner of every rite, the counterpart of every god by virtue of his greatness—Agni, the guest of men, come to us with all your aids, being of one mind, enjoying our prayer, O Lord of the bay horses! Turning toward us with your steadfast steeds, O fair-cheeked one, bestow upon us manly vigor, O Indra! Indra, the showerer of benefits, generating the days, has conquered the hostile armies with his eager followers, he who is the glory of the battle.

{2.4.3.7} You made the banner of days shine for Manu; you found the light for the great battle. O Aśvins, I invoke you both for protection. Come now, O sages, for the sake of the well-doer, on your well-rolling chariot yoked at dawn. Approach us with your aid, come to us! O Aśvins, favor these our prayers. May we have seed that brings offspring, free from shame. Striving for us in our children and grandchildren, may we, possessing fine jewels, go to the feast of the gods.

O Soma, through your powers of will you have become one of excellent will; through your skills you have become one of excellent skill, the knower of all. As a bull, by these greatnesses of yours, you have become a bull; through splendors, O splendorous one, you have become the beholder of men. You are the unconquerable one, the deliverer in battles and in conflicts, the winner of light, dwelling in the waters, the guardian of the enclosure, born for the fray, possessing a secure dwelling and great renown—O Soma, may we rejoice after you as you conquer. Be gracious like Mitra, anointing us with clarity, possessed of far-reaching splendor, swift-moving, and wide-extending.

{2.4.3.9} Now, O Viṣṇu, even by the wise your praise is to be perfected; the hymn of the oblation-bearer is to be brought to success. He who offers gifts to the ancient and most recent Viṣṇu, the one who possesses great majesty—he who shall proclaim the great birth of this Great One, he indeed shall surpass even his peer through his glories. O praisers, as you know him to be the ancient one, fulfill him with the oblation, the offspring of Ṛta. Knowing even his name, proclaim it aloud. O Viṣṇu, we partake in your lofty favor.

{2.4.3.10} Here are these parched grains dripping with ghee; let the two bay steeds bring Indra here upon his most comfortable chariot. This priest shall proclaim for thee in the great assembly the two bay steeds. I win for thee the desirable exhilaration, worthy of the season, from thee who art the conqueror. He who is known by the name Indra, who pours forth the lovely ghee with his bay steeds—he, the famous host, may enter into thee.

{2.4.3.11} O singer, [sing] of him who dwells in Hari-varṣa. The bull among men, the filler of the people, Indra, the much-invoked king of the tribes—he, being praised and seeking glory, comes toward me with help. Having yoked his two vigorous bay horses, come hither! When the rivers went forth according to their impulse, the waters flowed to the ocean like chariot-borne travelers. Even greater than that seat is Indra’s dwelling, when the milked stalk of Soma fills him. We call upon you, O Indra; come hither!

{ 2.4.3.12} Soma shall be sufficient for your body, O Śatakratu; rejoice in the pressed juices. Protect us in battles, protect us in the fray. For Indra, the Somas have been known since ancient times—those by which he became the skillful R̥bhu with strong-jointed limbs and vast power. Grasp them as they are being offered! O Indra, drink of the bullish juice shaken by the bull; come to the sacrifice without anger. For you the drops flow clear, the pressed juices, like cows toward their own stall, O Wielder of the Thunderbolt.

{2.4.3.13} O Indra, come first among those worthy of sacrifice! With that well-fashioned, most excellent jaw of yours, with which you ever drink the wave of the honeyed soma—drink with it! The Adhvaryu has stepped forward for you; let your thunderbolt, seeking cattle, roll forth, O Indra! Awaken the two who are yoked at dawn! O Aśvins, come hither to drink this soma! Worship the two who travel at dawn as the first! Drink before the greedy one who bestows nothing!

For at dawn the Aśvins establish the sacrifice; the sages praise them as those who receive the first portion. Worship the Aśvins at dawn and urge them forward; there is no [offering] made in the evening that is not pleasing to the gods. Moreover, another besides us sacrifices with discernment; each sacrificer who comes first is more worthy of gain.

O herb, you were born at night—Rāmā, Kṛṣṇā, and Asiknī. O Rajanī, make this turn white! Whatever is kilāsa and whatever is palita—drive away the speckled kilāsa and the palita from here! May our own natural color prevail; cast off the white patches! Black is your dwelling, black is your place of rest.

{2.4.4.2} O black herb, drive away the white spot from here! [Drive away] the leprosy born of the bone and that which is born upon the skin. By means of the *brahman*-spell, I have destroyed the white mark produced by sorcery. *Sarūpā* is your mother’s name; *Sarūpa* is your father’s name. O herb, you are *Sarūpā*; make this [skin] uniform in color.

{2.4.4.3} We invoke the auspicious Maghavan Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the winning of booty—him who hears us, the fierce one for our protection in the conflicts, who slays the Vṛtras and is the conqueror of riches. You shake the sky and the mountains to give wealth to the donor; the forests bow down before you out of fear on your march. O sons of Pṛśni, you cause the earth to tremble when you, the fierce ones, have harnessed the spotted mares for battle. They make the mountains quake and they rend asunder the lords of the forest.

O Maruts, turn away like those intoxicated with madness; O gods, [turn away] with your entire host. For you are the same in many places, the lord over all the tribes. In battles we invoke you; in battles we invoke Agni for aid, seeking booty, him who bestows wonderful wealth in the contests. Gather together, speak together; let your minds be of one accord.

{2.4.4.5} As the gods of old, being in accord, have attended to their portion; so may we be of one mind. One is the counsel, one the assembly; one is the thought, and their intention is shared. With one intent, join yourselves together! We worship you with an oblation that brings concord. One is your purpose; one are your hearts. Let your mind be one, so that there may be good harmony among you.

May there be concord for us with our own people; may there be concord with strangers. O Aśvins, you two grant concord here among us. May Bṛhaspati grant me concord; may Savitṛ bring about concord. O Aśvins, you two grant me concord here; bestow it upon me. Like [seeking] shade from the heat of the sun, we have come to your protection.

O Agni, you who shine like gold; O Savitṛ, with your unfailing and auspicious protections, guard our household today. You whose tongue is golden, for the sake of new prosperity, protect us; let no one who speaks evil against us have power over us. For at every exhilaration they have given us, as one of upright intent gives herds of cattle—gather for yourself many hundreds of treasures with both hands; sharpen us and bring us wealth.

O Siprin, Lord of spoils, O possessor of power, by your wondrous deed, do thou, O Indra, grant us a share of cattle, of horses, and of radiant treasures, O thou of abundant wealth! Whatever offense against the gods we have committed, O gods, from that, O Ādityas, release us by means of the Truth, through the Truth. O Ādityas, [release us] by means of the Truth.

O worshipful ones, release me here! O you who carry the sacrifice by means of sacrifices, we have sought to help you but were unable; though sacrificing with fat and offering clarified butter with the ladle, we, O All-Gods, though desiring it, were unable to assist you. Whether by day or by night, if one has committed a sin against you, may both the past and the future [be free] from that for me.

{ 2.4.4.43} May he release me as from a wooden post; may he release me as one released from a wooden post. Like a person who has bathed, may he cleanse us from impurity; like clarified butter purified by a strainer. May all [the gods] release me from sin. Out of the darkness, we have risen up, beholding the higher light—the god Sūrya among the gods—we have attained the supreme light.

Anuvāka 5 {2.4.5.44} This vigorous stalk flows forth, the oblation-bearing Soma, Indra’s portion, seeking the *ṛta*, possessing a hundredfold life. May he make me vigorous, a bull; beloved by the people, possessed of all heroes, and of noble heroism. With whom does the bull of the one who bestows dwell? The bull, accompanied by his team, rejoices for the slaying of Vṛtra and for the drinking of Soma. O Bull, grandson, great-grandson, you who are worthy of the *kuṇḍapāyya* sacrifice—may my mind be fixed upon you.

2.4.5.45 His aids come together; his virile powers and manly deeds, his teams, attend upon Indra. Like rivers to the ocean, our hymns—impetuous with praise—enter him who is wide-expansive. For Indra, songs flow in unceasing streams. He sent the waters forth from the depths of the sea, he who by his powers, as if with an axle for his wheels, has propped apart the earth and the sky on every side. With his might, Indra has shaken the ground and its foundation, like a wind from the ocean, through his vigorous strengths.

{2.4.5.46} He, displaying his strength, shattered the firm [fortresses] and struck down the peaks of the mountains. O Agni, with your beautiful light, grant us wealth that nourishes all life and bestow mercy so that we may live. O Soma, you bestow fortune upon the great, and you grant skill to the youth who follows the *ṛta* so that he may live. The Maruts harness their chariot for glory, making it easy to traverse like the sun; O Mitra and Varuṇa, they do so in the search for cattle.

Variegated dust-clouds move about like thundering sounds. O sovereign kings of heaven, sprinkle us with milk. O Mitra and Varuṇa, Parjanya speaks a word full of nourishment, wondrous and radiant. The Maruts clothe themselves in clouds through their great creative power; cause the ruddy, stainless sky to rain. Sūrya has yoked the seven bright mares, the daughters of his chariot; he travels by means of those self-yoked ones. With the swiftest steeds, drawing out the thread of the sacrifice, you go. (With the swiftest steeds, drawing out the thread, you go.)

{2.4.5.48} Driving away the darkness, O God, you bring forth the wealth of light; the rays of the sun shine brightly. Like a skin, they have stripped away the gloom within the waters. Sing forth to Parjanya, the bounteous son of Heaven! May he seek out pasture for us. Address the mighty one with these songs; praise Parjanya with reverence and win his favor. Bellowing like a bull, the swift-giving one shall bestow seed as a germ within the plants.

{2.4.5.49} He who produces the embryo of the plants, of the cows, and of the mares—Parjanya [is he] for the women. To him let us offer this most honey-sweet oblation in our mouth; may he grant us nourishment (*iḍā*) in abundance. When, O Agni, the pure ones with clarified butter served you, the pure one, for three autumns, they assumed even names worthy of sacrifice; the well-born ones brought their bodies to perfection.

{2.4.5.50} And Indra and Śunāsīra, sprinkle this sacrifice for us! Bestow the germ [of life] for our well-being! You two, into whom this entire world has entered, in whom joy and greatness are established—O Śunāsīra, in harmony with the seasons and accompanied by Indra, may you both enjoy this oblation {this offering} with a willing heart! Those who kindle the fire and spread the sacrificial grass in due order, whose friend is the youthful Indra—O Agni and Indra, acting in concert!

2. You two, irresistible, [have struck down] the Vṛtras. 3. For you two are the greatest slayers of Vṛtra. 4. By whom they won the light of heaven in the very beginning. 5. You two who have taken your stand in the midst of the world. 6. O bulls, leaders of men, with thunderbolts in your arms. 7. O Agni and Indra, slayers of Vṛtra, I invoke you both.

And may Sarasvatī, who is dear among the dear, the seven-sistered, and well-beloved, become worthy of our praise. These offerings, accompanied by salutations, are presented from you; O Sarasvatī, accept this hymn of praise. Placing ourselves within your most beloved protection, may we take refuge in you as if under a tree. Viṣṇu, the inviolable guardian, strode forth three steps; from thence he established the sacred laws.

May I attain that beloved domain of his, where the god-seeking men rejoice; for such is the kinship of Viṣṇu of the wide stride: in his highest step is the fountain of honey. By his wisdom he has become the most excellent giver. Today, O you of beautiful splendor, the mortal has approached you with hymns of praise. O you who are borne by prayer, these prayers are dear to you; sit upon the sacred grass. Enjoy the sacrificial cake, O Hero.

{2.4.6.53} May the sons who are the singers of the *ṛta* hear our songs; may they be gracious toward us. O God Savitar, bestow upon us today prosperity accompanied by progeny. Drive away ill dreams and evil sleep. O God Savitar, drive away all misfortunes; send what is auspicious to me. [I praise] the pure Bṛhaspati with hymns.

2.4.6.54 In the sacrifices, pay homage! He who is unbending desires strength. Those gods who, highly skilled, supported the two parents of skill (Dakṣapitarau) for the sake of divine power with great majesty—he indeed dwells well-established in his own abode; for him Iḍā swells at all times; to him the subjects bow down of their own accord, that king in whose presence the Brahman goes first. O Indra, [grant] the impulse, the shaking, the shaking from the thighs, the shaking from the hips.

From the *kana* bring to us the *kābhā*. Like one about to urinate, [extend] the two thighs. O Indra, strike away our enemies. Like one digging with a small spade, causing them to flow away, lead us toward excellent praise. Prajāpati placed glory in the woman; he placed the testicles, the satisfaction of desire, and bliss therein. O Agni, grant me a share of that here: joy, rapture, and bliss.

The sap deposited in the two testicles—may I satisfy myself with it like one who has run his course. In the acceptance of sacrificial gifts, may we attain the intention of the mind, the truth of speech, the form of cattle, and the essence of food; may glory and prosperity rest upon me. Just as I have been satisfied by this woman as a man, and just as a woman is satisfied by her beloved husband, even so may I be satisfied by Bhaga.

The beloved desire of the sacrifice is Agni; he says, "I give. Vāyu says, "So be it. The Moon says, "Hanta! (Come!). The Sun is the Truth, "Om. The Waters brought that truth—the glory of the sacrifice and the sacrificial fee—with the prayer: "May this desire of mine be fulfilled. For they found no other guide than him, the Vaiśvānara Agni, the one who goes before.

{2.4.6.58} Then the wise gods churned out the nectar, Vaiśvānara, for the conquest of the field. Those whose ancient tracks were here, whose many dwellings were established without pillars—those people, O Vaiśvānara, driven away by you, have taken their stand upon another earth. I invoke the great mother earth, the mid-air, and the lofty heaven for our protection. The earth sustains everything. {The blissful earth...}

The intermediate space has spread out wide; the vast heaven milks forth its milk. These [cows] are never lost, nor does a thief harm them; no enemy or distress can assail them. With those [cows] by which one worships the gods and gives gifts, the lord of cattle dwells together with them for a long time. No steed with dust-stained hooves overtakes them, nor do they ever go toward a place of slaughter. Following after those cows of the mortal sacrificer, they roam through the wide-striding, fearless realm.

Night has shone forth as she approaches, in many places with her divine eyes; she has put on all her splendors. I have driven the cows toward you; choose them, O Daughter of Heaven, O Night, like one who has won the hymn of praise. The gods generated the goddess Speech; animals of every form speak her. May that cow, Speech, yielding us joy, refreshment, and vigor, come to us well-praised.

{2.4.6.61} What the voice speaks when it is unconscious—the joyous Queen of the gods has sat down. She has milked out fourfold nourishment and waters. Where indeed has her highest part gone? The Gaurī has lowed, fashioning the flowing waters. She became one-footed, two-footed, four-footed, eight-footed, nine-footed, and thousand-syllabled in the highest heaven. Upon her the oceans flow; by that the four quarters of space live.

Then the imperishable flows forth; upon that the entire universe depends for life. May Indra, the Sun, the All-Creator, arise, accompanied by the Maruts, by his hosts, and by his kinsmen. Let his daughters-in-law, with their minds, attend to the command of this father-in-law and to the voice of his rivals. Indra, the Sun, has crossed the regions; let the daughter-in-law and the rival be under this father-in-law. May he, exulting, conquer his enemies; may he win the prize in the contest for booty.

1. Agni, the upholder of the kṣatra, possesses unassailable vigor; may he shine forth with a thousandfold radiance, never failing. 2. Blazing brightly, kindled and fierce, he has ascended the mid-air and reached the heavens.

Anuvāka 7 {2.4.7.63} Thou art the bull; thy stalk is taken for the bull. This one is fierce, for the observer of men. Celestial, fit for action, established, the great-named one. That which is the hump of the bull—let it be the central point, O Viṣṇu. This one who is mine, the bull—likewise like Indra among the gods, let him speak out among the people. Long-lived, full of splendor, and moreover the overlord of the clans.

Overseer of this earth, O Indra, make him a bull, he who is well-horned, a true bull, auspicious, and placed within the wooden trough. With the lowing of the plowman’s bull, we sacrifice with the bull; sacrificing with the bull, as if with unctuous clarified butter, we conquer all adversaries and hostile armies through Indra.

{2.4.7.65} He for whom this bull is the oblation is led forth for Indra. He shall conquer the approaching enemy; moreover, he slays those who attack us. May he be the leader of men; may he be the one who breaks through at the front. O Indra, stir up vigor within our bodies. Trample down all hostile powers beneath you. Strike down whatever affliction assails us. O Giver of Life, make wide space for us.

Come forth! Come forward! Strike out! Overpower! Do not be dejected; make yourself heard among the people. O Bull, being praised, stand up with your might! O Indra, fight our enemies in the front lines! O Agni, you are the victor; conquer the enemies with your force and power! Drive away the enemies, drive away the mockers! I, the inspired singer, have fashioned this hymn for you, O many-born one, as a skillful craftsman fashions a chariot. If you, O God Agni, should take pleasure in it.

May we win these waters rich in gold, which have been consecrated with ghee. O Indra, you were born for victory; as such, carry us across in battles and in the overcoming of hostile armies. Indra has conquered the earth, the mid-air, and the great heaven—the slayer of Vṛtra, the one of many insights. Indra has conquered by force all forces; Indra has conquered all hostile armies.

Indra, once born, shattered the fortresses; may he, our protector from afar, grant us wide space. This Soma is the doer, ungrasped, the all-conquering, the piercer; he is the seer and the inspired sage through his poetic wisdom. Vāyu goes first, the lover of sacrifice; may he go with the mind to the sacrifice, auspicious with his auspicious teams. O Vāyu, the bright [Soma] is offered to you—the first of the honeyed draughts at the rites for heaven.

{2.4.7.69} Come for the drinking of the Soma, O God who mounts thy chariot by thy own power, with thy team of horses! O Indra, cause this man to prosper among the Kṣatriyas; let him be the lord of the people and their king. O Indra, bestow great splendors upon him; deprive his enemy of luster. Grant him a share in the village, in horses, and in cattle; exclude from these that one who is his enemy. Rest upon the height of the realm, at its summit; then, as a mighty one, distribute wealth to us.

O Heaven and Earth, milk for us abundant wealth, like a cow that yields the warm oblation. May this king be dear to Indra; may he be dear to the cattle, to the plants, and to the waters. I yoke for you Indra, the superior one, by whom you shall conquer and not be defeated. He has made you the sole bull among your own people, and thus, O King, the highest among men. You are superior; your rivals are beneath you. As the sole bull, a friend of Indra, you have emerged victorious.

Conquering all the quarters and the hostile armies, overcome those who act as enemies; subdue them! To you, O youngest one, the peoples bring tribute, O Agni—both from nearby and from afar. Take notice of the favor of him who praises you most excellently. Great and auspicious is your mighty protection, O Agni, you who paralyzed the divine powers with your deadly weapons, and who made the Dawns have noble lords. That youthful Agni, having hemmed in the Nahuṣas, by his might made the clans payers of tribute.

{2.4.7.72} O Agni, you shall instantly surpass others for whomever you have become more manifest and beautiful. Another [god] is praised as wondrous and resplendent; he is the beloved guest of human clans. Heroic powers have been gathered with the *brahman* as the foremost. The *brahman* extended the sky as the first and highest. The *brahman* was born as the first of the cosmic order (*ṛta*). Who is worthy to rival that *brahman*? The ladles filled with clarified butter are the *brahman*; by the *brahman* were the sacrificial posts measured out.

The threads of the Brahman-sacrifice are the officiating priests who prepare the oblations. Like the horns of horned animals, they appear clearly; the sacrificial posts stand upon the earth with their cross-pieces. These divine sacrificial posts stand firm; homage to my friends—do not strike down me who am already bowed. Agni, the conqueror, has crossed the realms, having struck down the rivals and the hostile armies, the glorious one. Accepting my offering, do not neglect me; slaying our enemies, grant us wide space.

1. I praise you, O Agni, the lord of beings, the glory of all worlds, the wide-maker, the possessor of noble heroes. 2. Rejoicing in the oblation, you are the conqueror of rivals. 3. Slay the enemies; drive away the adversaries.

As of old, with your newest splendor, O Agni, joined together, expand greatly with your light. Now I have generated a new hymn for Agni, for the falcon of heaven; will he not surely grant us wealth? He who is self-arisen, whose glories are visible to behold, like the riches of a hero—O Agni, mindful at the forefront of the sacrifice, you are the invincible leader.

Agni belongs to the human clans; he is the swift chariot, ever new. For Soma, the prize-winner, new clarified butter has been produced from milk—a cherished treasure, most pure. O Soma, enjoy our new [offering]; satisfy yourself here with the cream of the milk. We, who are your portion by Right, we, O Soma, choose for ourselves the favor of you, the new one.

{2.4.8.76} Grant us thousands; enjoy our new oblation, O Soma, you who are most perfect through the seasons. Therefore, truly, take pleasure in this of ours. O King Soma, for our well-being, present this new hymn and new oblation to Indra and Agni. May they, being of one mind, accept it. O Indra and Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, may you today graciously accept this pure hymn newly born.

For I invoke both of you, who are easy to call upon; may you two bestow strength immediately upon the one who desires it. May Agni and Indra be satisfied with this our new oblation. O two gods, thousandfold, come here to our sacrifice—wealthy and finders of heaven. May they be satisfied with this our new oblation: Agni and Indra. Satisfy all the gods.

Of this our new oblation—verily they were born as finders of the light. Hither to this well-spread sacred grass with the new [offering]! This sacrifice is the portion of the sacrificer; this has become the embryo of the world. O All-Gods, come most readily to this today! These two, Heaven and Earth, joined together, are stretching out the sacrifice, richly adorned with wisdom. May they both bestow upon him all beings: offspring, prosperity, and immortality through the new [offering].

These two milch-cows yield the nectar of immortality; may nourishment, rich in milk, come to the higher realm. Delighting in this sacrifice with the new [offering], may Heaven and Earth, joined together and dripping with clarity, be present. O Agni, youngest carrier of oblations, you of wondrous luster, fed by clarity, newly born, you shine forth. Such is your greatness, O Agni! You, O divine Agni, are not diminished in your portion among the deities.

Knowing this, you shall sacrifice with these. Accept our new hymn of praise. Let Agni be the first to eat, for he knows how the oblation is. May he make the plants auspicious for us, he who belongs to all people. O gods, you have led us to a fortunate prosperity; through you as our wealth, may we attain you. As such, O food, enter us as a source of bliss—be a comfort to our children and a blessing to our bodies. This very barley, mixed with honey—
They ploughed over the mind of Sarasvatī; Indra, the lord of a hundred powers, was the master of the plough; the bounteous Maruts were the ploughmen.

Prapāṭhaka 5, Anuvāka 1 The vital breath (*prāṇa*) protects all that moves; having become active and manifold, it has entered into many things. He alone has pervaded everything—he who is the pervasive deity among the gods, dwelling within. The protector, the one who rises up from the womb, the master of the field and the traveler, the bull—attend upon that very *prāṇa* with your mind. Let this our oblation be the foremost of the gods. This is the thought of the mind; the past and the future are protected by it, for that indeed is preeminent among the gods.

{2.5.1.2} May she who goes before us come to this invocation together with the gods, placing the lord of the sacrifice in ever more excellent action—may my speech take pleasure in this oblation. The goddess Virāj is our high priest; she is the bearer of the oblation, never-failing, by whom the gods proclaim manifold forms and beautiful ornaments in the highest birthplace. May that Virāj, never shrinking away, [be ours].

{2.5.1.3} May the Goddess of Speech enjoy this oblation. The eye of the gods, the light hidden in immortality, is established in many ways for its discernment. May we attain its favor; may it not abandon us, the far-seeing one. May our life-span be extended; may we, unblinded by the eye, live on and attain the light. May we attain the light of heaven and immortality. With the ear, they hear what is auspicious and the truth; with the ear, the speech uttered in many ways.

2. Through the ear, joy and greatness are heard. 3. Through the ear, I hear all the quarters. 4. By which [the quarters] from the east and the south, 5. And from the western quarter, they hear from the north. 6. That very ear, being raised up in many ways, 7. Has encompassed everything, as the felly encompasses the spokes.

Anuvāka 2 {2.5.2.4} Arise, O vigorous one; you are within the waters. Enter this kingdom, which is full of truth and joy. May he who, as Rohita, brought forth this entire universe, establish us securely in our kingdoms. Rohita has ascended higher and higher; through his offspring, he has ascended to the expanse of all beings. Grasped by them, he found the six wide worlds; beholding a path, he has brought the kingdom here. Rohita has brought the kingdom here; he has cast away our enemies. May there be safety for us.

{2.5.2.5} May Heaven and Earth yield for us sovereignty with powerful verses and with wealth here. Rohita, the omniform, has touched [all things], encompassing both the upward-growing and the downward-growing plants. Having ascended to heaven with his great majesty, may he moisten our kingdom with his own milk. Those subjects of yours who have been brought together through austerity—they have come following the Gāyatra-calf; may they enter you with their own greatness. May the mother and the son, Rohita, come together.

{2.5.2.6} You, O fierce Maruts, sons of Pṛśni, together with Indra as your ally, crush the enemies. Rohita heard you, O sky-piercing Maruts, you who are thrice-seven in number and possess sweet delights. Rohita brought forth heaven and earth; upon him Parameṣṭhin stretched the thread. Upon him Aja Ekapāt took his stand. He made heaven and earth firm by his strength; Rohita made heaven and earth firm. By him the sun was supported, by him the firmament.

He is the measurer of the mid-air, the realm of dust; through him the gods found the heavenly light. O Jātavedas, may the radiant beams of light, all together, offer oblations unto you who shine so auspiciously. They sprinkle you, the vigorous one, with clarified butter. O Agni, you gather for yourself all enjoyments. O Agni, be strong for great good fortune; may your splendors be most excellent. Establish for us a household that is well-governed, and trample down the powers of those who act as enemies.

May Indra Maghavan give to us again; may Śakra, the giver of wealth, the bestower of riches, grant us treasures. May he turn his mind toward us when entreated, enjoying our oblation with readiness. O Hero, those riches which you took from us in your wrath—O Indra, find them for us again through this oblation. May Indra bring safety from all directions.

The conqueror of enemies, the all-beholding one; for your intention (*ākūti*), for your desire (*kāma*), for your prosperity (*samṛdh*), I place you before me for immortality and life. May his intention be for his protection; may his desire be for his fulfillment. The thoughts of Indra are yoked; I place the divine intention before my mind. May she, the mother of sacrifice, be easy for me to invoke. Whatever I desire with my mind, may I obtain that wish with my heart fixed upon it.

This Agni surpasses all other fires, where the vigorous son, with firm hands, meets the imperishable syllables that have a thousand paths. To you, the guardians of the quarters—from the four immortal ones—overseers of what has come to be, we offer this oblation. I mingle all the quarters with honey; may the waters and the plants be free from disease. May this sacrificer cast away his enemies.

{2.5.3.11} May all cattle be unseized: Agni, Soma, Varuṇa, Mitra, Indra, Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ who is thousandfold, Pūṣan with his protection for our cattle, and Sarasvatī. May Tvaṣṭṛ adorn forms with sacrifices (the sacrifice is bliss). Sarasvatī bestows forms, Pūṣan, Bhaga, and Savitṛ shall grant us fortune; Bṛhaspati and Indra shall grant a thousand; Mitra, Varuṇa, Soma, and Agni are the givers.

Anuvāka 4 {2.5.4.12} Bring us glorious fortune, O Indra! May we take possession of the abundance of your gift. Our desire has spread out like the wide expanse; fulfill it, O Lord of Wealth, for you are the master of riches. Satisfy this longing with cattle and horses, and extend it with splendid bounty. Seeking the light of heaven, the wise Kuśikas have fashioned hymns for you, Indra, as their vehicle. Now I shall proclaim the heroic deeds of Indra, those which the wielder of the thunderbolt performed for the first time.

{2.5.4.13} He slew the serpent; he pierced through the waters. He split open the bellies of the mountains. He slew the serpent as he lay coiled upon the mountain. Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for him the resounding thunderbolt. Like lowing cows, the flowing waters went straight down to the ocean. Acting like a bull, he chose the Soma; at the Trikadruka rites, he drank of the pressed juice. Maghavan took up his missile, the thunderbolt; he slew this first-born of the serpents.

{2.5.4.14} When you, O Indra, slew the first-born of the serpents, and then destroyed the magic powers of the deceivers; when you generated the sun, the sky, and the dawn—by such deeds you truly found no enemies. Indra slew Vṛtra, the worst of Vṛtras, the shoulderless one, with his great bolt as a weapon of slaughter. Like tree trunks hewn down by an axe, the serpent lies prostrate, pressed close against the earth. For he, like an invincible and intoxicated warrior, challenged the great hero, the crusher, the drinker of the dregs.

He did not survive the onset of his weapons; he was shattered. Indra’s foe was ground to powder. He, the all-pervading messenger, the Vasu, has taken [the prize] in his right hand. Like one who crosses over, he has not relaxed; through the desire for glory, he has not relaxed. For every supplicant you bring forth [the gift]; you carry the oblation among the gods. For every doer of good, he opens the door of treasure; Agni opens wide the doors.

Rising up, impelling our desire, filling all beings as of old, well-kindled with his banner, the most excellent sacrificer—O Agni, look graciously upon our desire from every direction; enjoying the oblation among the immortals, [warding off] those of evil intent, bestow upon us abundant wealth and food rich in cattle, while performing sacrifice and adorning himself among the immortals. O Aśvins, performers of many wonders, come to the sacrifice of the donor! May Pūṣan protect our wealth!

{2.5.4.17} O Aśvins, strengthening this sacrifice, bestow wealth upon the sacrificer; may you two protect our cattle on every side. May Pūṣan protect us always, never failing. To thee, O great Sarasvatī, O fortunate one, rich in prizes, who art true of speech, I offer my prayer. This oblation, rich in ghee, is for thee, O Sarasvatī; we bring these offerings to thee, who art true of speech. These are thy auspicious blessings against misfortune; through them, may we be well-fortuned.

The sacrifice is the lord of riches; the sacrifice rules over treasures. The sacrifice is the master of crops and of secure dwellings. May the sacrifice, when offered, bestow foresight. May the sacrifice, accompanied by sacred prayer (*brahman*), go unto the gods. May this sacrifice increase with cattle and horses; may this altar be rich in offspring and heroic sons. May this sacrificial grass surpass all other grass. May all the gods protect this sacrifice. O gods, let Bhaga alone be the possessor of fortune; through him, may we become possessed of fortune.

{2.5.5.19} As such, O Bhaga, everyone invokes you repeatedly. O Bhaga, be our leader here. O Bhaga, leader; O Bhaga, whose gifts are true; O Bhaga, favor this prayer of ours. O Bhaga, further us with cattle and horses; O Bhaga, may we be rich in men through our men. Constant years pass away; constant years flow on like waters. Having sacrificed with the eternal oblation of the many passing years—sacrifice performed and merit earned—he ascended to the infinite, supreme world.

This is indeed she who first shone forth; as a goddess, she assumes five forms. Two sisters weave this eternal web, extended with six threads. One lets down some threads while the other lays others down; they do not fall away, nor do they reach an end. May your water-bearers come here today—those Maruts who all impel the rain. O Maruts, this fire has been kindled; take pleasure in it, O youthful seers.

{2.5.5.21} The Maruts, pourers of rain, bold in their might, are like terrifying wild beasts with their powerful waves; like fires blazing forth, they are the drinkers of the *ṛjīṣa*. Blowing forth smoke, they have covered the cows. The God has stepped out thrice. Seat Bṛhaspati—the ordainer, blue-backed, and vast—upon his seat. Let us honor him who is seated in his own womb, shining within the house, golden-hued and ruddy. For he is pure, possessed of a hundred feathers, and he is radiant.

{2.5.5.22} Bṛhaspati, with his golden axe, vigorous and bestowing fair rain, is the one who enters us well and is exalted. He is the most effective in providing nourishment for his friends, O Pūṣan; under your protection, may we never come to harm. We here are your praisers. O Pūṣan, those golden ships of yours which travel within the ocean and through the mid-air—those by which you go on the mission of Sūrya, driven by desire and seeking renown.

{2.5.5.23} O Forest, O Forest, you there! You who seem to vanish away—why do you not ask the way to the village? Does fear not seize you? When the cicada (*ciccika*) chirps in response to the loud cry of the bull-frog, the Forest exults as if running with clashing cymbals. And it is like grazing cattle; and it appears like a house.

{2.5.5.24} And so, Araṇyānī at evening lets loose [the cattle] like wagons. Truly, he calls the cow; truly, he has driven up the wood. Dwelling in the forest at evening, he thinks, "It has bellowed. But Araṇyānī does not kill, nor does anyone else come near her. Having eaten sweet fruit, one lies down wherever one desires. I have praised Araṇyānī, the mother of wild beasts—she who is fragrant with the scent of ointment, sweet-smelling, rich in food, and requiring no plowing.

For the slaying of Vṛtra, for strength, and for the conquest of armies—O Indra, we turn you hither, the one accompanied by the holy word (*brahman*), possessed of heroes, the great, the wide, the deep, the broad-based Indra, the famous seer, the fierce, the overcomer of adversaries. Grant us wonderful, virile wealth! For the field-disease, for thee; for Nirṛti, for thee. I release [thee] from malice, from the noose of Varuṇa. I make thee sinless before the *brahman*.

May both these, Heaven and Earth, be auspicious for you, O Śiva. May Agni together with the waters be auspicious for you. May the four quarters be auspicious for you—those four divine quarters which the Sun gazes upon as having the Wind as their lord. From them I place you into old age; let consumption go far away to Destruction (Nirṛti). You have been released from consumption, from misfortune, and from the power of decay.

{2.5.6.27} From the snares of malice, from Destruction (Nirṛti), he has been released. He has found the day, the pleasant freedom from distress. He has entered the auspicious world of the well-doer. Just as the gods released the Sun, the Truth, from the grasp of darkness and set him free from sin, even so do I release this man from the kinship-curse of *kṣetriya*, from malice, and from the snare of Varuṇa. O Bṛhaspati and Indra, you two are the lords of celestial and earthly wealth.
Bestow riches upon the singer, even upon the humble one.

{2.5.6.28} May you protect us always with blessings, O gods, as we invoke Indra, the wielder of weapons, who increases all things—those whom he protects, by whom [the enemies] were slain and went along the long path, returning from their endless purpose. O well-born Sībalā, that medicine of yours which is in the Himālayas, which is blissful and most auspicious for the heart—from that, grant it to us. When you run forth from those mountains, O radiant one, shining like a maiden.

{2.5.6.29} The Mudgalas strengthen you with oblations; as such, O Sibali, grant us wealth here. The gods of the past looked upon those of the future through their births; they know the births of others to be inferior. "The gods know me: 'This one am I,'" [he says]. Having left behind the body at the end of old age—having left behind out-breath and in-breath, sight and hearing, and speech gathered within the mind—having left behind the body at the end of old age, may we attain every prosperity.
1. These indeed are those dawns which first shone forth. 2. Those goddesses assume five forms. 3. Everlasting, they do not abandon us. 4. They do not go to an end.

With the study of the Vasus, with the wave of the Rudras, with the splendor of the Ādityas, with the will of the Viśvedevas, and with the speed of the Maruts, I offer thee, Svāhā! I have come as the conqueror, the friend of Indra, well-armed. Sit thou, invincible, within the quarters. This luster given by Agni has arrived—glory, radiance, endurance, vigor, and strength.

For long life, for a hundred autumns; I accept [this] for great heroic power. You are life, you are all-encompassing life; you are complete life, you are total life. May my life be complete; may I attain a full span of life. Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ! Agni, by his law, is the eater of food; Death, by his law, is the lord of food. Brahman, Kṣatra—svāhā!

Prajāpati is the leader; Bṛhaspati is the forerunner; Yama is the path; the Moon is the restorer of life—svāhā! Agni is the eater of food, the lord of food; may he grant the enjoyment of food to the sacrificer at this sacrifice—svāhā! Soma is the king, the lord of kings; may he grant sovereignty to the sacrificer at this sacrifice—svāhā! Varuṇa is the sovereign, the lord of sovereigns; may he grant imperial rule to the sacrificer at this sacrifice—svāhā!

Mitra is the lord of the kṣatra; may he grant the kṣatra to the sacrificer at this sacrifice—svāhā! Indra is the lord of strength; may he grant strength to the sacrificer at this sacrifice—svāhā! Bṛhaspati is the lord of the sacred word (brahman); may he grant the sacred word to the sacrificer at this sacrifice—svāhā! Savitṛ is the lord of the kingdom; may he grant the kingdom to the sacrificer at this sacrifice—svāhā!

May Pūṣan, the lord of the people, grant the people to the sacrificer at this sacrifice; svāhā! (0) Sarasvatī is nourishment, the mistress of nourishment; may she grant nourishment to the sacrificer at this sacrifice; svāhā! (1–2) Tvaṣṭṛ is the maker of forms, the lord of forms of animals that come in pairs; may he grant animals with their forms to the sacrificer at this sacrifice; svāhā! (3)

Anuvāka 8 {2.5.8.34} Protect him, he who is the consumer of the *ṛjīṣa*, the deliverer; he who is powerful, the bull among hymns; he who is the breaker of enclosures, the wielder of the thunderbolt, who stands upon his two bay horses. May that Indra pierce through for us wondrous spoils of war. O Bull, let your impetuous strength come from behind; let it come from above, from below, and from the front. Let it come from every side toward us. O Indra, bestow upon us celestial splendor. Sing forth a song of power for this Indra, whose chariot is foremost.

Even in the encounter, he is the maker of space; in the clash of battles, he is the slayer of Vṛtra. Be our inspirer! Let the bowstrings of our enemies snap upon their bows! We invoke Indra Śunāsīra at this sacrifice; may he come to us with strengths. To Indra Śunāsīra, offer our oblation with the ladle!

{2.5.8.36} May the wise one accept [the offerings] in return! Let the oblations rich in clarified butter be presented to him, to the Lord of the bay horses, who is the sustainer and acts in harmony. Indra, increasing through the sacred word (*brahman*) and the seasons, enjoy this oblation of Śunāsīra! The birds with beautiful wings, the Priyamedha seers, have approached Indra with their supplications. Dispel the darkness; fill our vision! Release us like those bound in a snare! Sing a great song for Indra!

O Maruts, [bring] the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, by whom the upholders of Ṛta generated light—the god who is watchful for the sake of the gods. Who are these solitary ones here? Who are these winged birds? The offspring of Manthāla, the *kulis*, fly all around me. May the gods blow them away so that they do not return. May I obtain with my body the vision of the eagle. Thus, O Varuṇa, praise the great one; pay homage to the wise guardian of immortality. May he grant us a triple-layered protection.

{2.5.8.38} Do you protect us always with blessings! When they beheld you with longing hearts as you flew toward the vault of heaven like a fair-winged bird—golden-winged, the messenger of Varuṇa, a swift-moving bird in the womb of Yama. May the divine Waters be for our aid; may they be for our drinking. May they flow toward us with health and prosperity, they who are the lords of desirable things and the rulers of all people.

I beg the waters for medicine; Soma has told me that within the waters are all medicines, as well as Agni, the source of universal welfare, and the waters themselves, which possess all healing powers. O Sarasvatī, whatever sweetness is in the waters, in the cows, and in the horses—with that, O lady of plenty, anoint my face, O Sarasvatī! May she who is Sarasvatī, the bringer of universal prosperity—

{2.5.8.40} Grant me a share of her; may I partake of her; may we become the greatest sharers of her. I am yours, you are mine; this is so. You are my source, I am your source. Being as one of mine, O Agni, carry the oblations; like a son who makes the world for his father, O Jātavedas. Being right here, I sustain you, O Agni, who are there, with breath, speech, and mind. May life not abandon me while I am hidden away.

{2.5.8.41} With the Vaiśvānara light, I worship thee. This is thy seasonal womb, from which, once born, thou didst shine. Knowing it, O Agni, ascend it; then increase our wealth. O Agni, with that body of thine which is worthy of sacrifice, come hither—be radiant—ascend; ascend thy own self. Bringing many manly riches to us, come toward us.
Becoming the sacrifice, enter the sacrifice as your own womb; O Jātavedas, being born from the earth, come to your dwelling. Descend again, O Jātavedas!

Carry our oblation to the gods, knowing them well; bestow upon us long life, progeny, and wealth. Shine unceasingly within our home. I call aloud upon that Indra, the bounteous and fierce, who bestows strength continuously and is irresistible in his powers. May he, the most generous and worthy of sacrifice, turn toward us through our hymns. May the wielder of the thunderbolt make all paths easy for us to attain prosperity. At the Trikadruka sacrifices, the mighty and very vigorous one drank his fill of the barley-mixture.
He drank the Soma pressed by Viṣṇu as he desired; it exhilarated him, the great and wide one, for the performance of mighty deeds.

{2.5.8.43} May she, the goddess, attend upon this god; the true Indu [is attended] by the true Indra. When Saramā found the cleft of the mountain, she, uniting with them, reached the great, ancient path. She of the good feet led them to the summit of the flowing waters. Knowing it well, she went first toward the roar. Saramā found the firm, wide stall of cattle, by which the human clan is nourished. They who have made all things their own offspring, creating a path toward immortality—O Lord of Men, you [are there] among the men at the invocation of the gods.

Having chosen many [battles], O Lord of the bay horses, you slay the greedy Cumuri; and for Dabhīti, you sent Dhuni to sleep, easy to kill. Thus protect us as of old; let [the Soma] exhilarate you. Hear our prayer, grow strong through our songs. Make the sun manifest, cause the nourishments to swell. Slay the enemies, O Indra; pierce through to the cattle. O Agni, drive away the adversaries, push them aside. Banish sickness and ward off the demons.
From this great ocean, from the high heaven, [bring us aid].

Release upon us here an abundance of waters. O Sacrifice, be established in our benevolence—most gracious, full of bliss, most gracious!—may riches enter into you in many ways. Bestowing long life upon the sacrificer, anoint the singer with immortality, O Indra; Indra spreads the furrow with the ploughshare.

This is the image of the year; that indeed was the preeminent light of the sun. May this plow bring us prosperity for a year; it is Indra’s bounty, offered forth by himself in abundance. That form of the sun moves on, measuring out the year; thereon the bull stands firm upon the twelve-spoked wheel. Desiring horses, desiring cattle, desiring booty, we invoke you, that you may come to us. Adorning ourselves, we seek you in your new favor; O Indra, we would call upon you for our welfare.

Prapāṭhaka 6, Anuvāka 1 I mingle you, who are sweet, with what is sweet; you, who are strong, with what is strong; you, who are immortal, with what is immortal; you, who are honey-sweet, with what is honey-sweet—I mingle you with Soma. You are Soma; be prepared for the Aśvins; be prepared for Sarasvatī; be prepared for Indra the Good Protector. Pour out the pressed juice on all sides—Soma, who is the supreme oblation.

{2.6.1.2} He who, manly, has flowed within the waters, has pressed the Soma with the stones. May the daughter of the Sun purify for you the flowing Soma, with the eternal fleece as a means. Purified by the filter, Vāyu; the Soma has sped forward.

{2.6.1.3} The worthy companion and friend of Indra; the *brahman* and *kṣatra*, the brilliance and the power of the senses, flow forth. The pressed Soma, mixed with *surā*, is effused for exhilaration. O God, satisfy the deities with your bright [light]; bestow nourishment with its essence upon the sacrificer. Just as those possessing barley reap the barley, threshing it out in due order, so here provide food for those who have not come to the ritual cutting of the sacred grass (*barhis*) with their homage. You are taken with a support; I take you, acceptable to the Aśvins.

{2.6.1.4} For Sarasvatī; for Indra the Good Protector. This is your womb: for brilliance you, for heroism you, for strength you. You are brilliance; bestow brilliance upon me. You are heroism; bestow heroism upon me. You are strength; bestow strength upon me. For separate indeed have your seats been established by the gods. Do not mingle in the highest heaven. You are the spirited Surā; this is Soma. Do not harm me as you enter your own womb.

{2.6.1.5} You are taken with a support; you are the brilliance of the Aśvins, the vigor of Sarasvatī, the strength of Indra. This is your womb: for joy you, for bliss you, for greatness you. You are force; bestow force upon me. You are fury; bestow fury upon me. You are majesty; bestow majesty upon me. You are power; bestow power upon me. That [power] which protects the tiger from the cholera-disease, both the wolf and the hawk, the winged bird and the lion—may it protect this man from distress.
4. You are mingling; O *dyumān* (shining ones), you are mingling. Unite me with what is auspicious. 5. You are separating; O *dyumān*, you are separating.

Separate me from evil. Anuvāka 2: King Soma, the pressed, is immortality. By means of the *ṛjīṣa* (the dregs), he abandoned death. Through the *ṛta* (cosmic order), [he attained] truth and sensory power (*indriya*). The bright drinking of the juice—the sensory power of Indra. This milk is immortality, honey. He drank the Soma apart from the waters. By means of the *chandas* (meter), the swan dwelling in purity. Through the *ṛta*, [he attained] truth and sensory power. From the waters, he drank forth the milk.

The curlew of the Aṅgirasas [obtained] through inspired thought; by means of cosmic order (*ṛta*), he drank the truth, the power of the senses, the essence from the flowing food. By means of sacred formulation (*brahman*), he drank the ruling power (*kṣatra*); by means of cosmic order, the truth, the power of the senses. He casts off the seed as urine; the power of the senses enters the womb. The embryo, enveloped by the fetal membrane, casts off the chorion at birth. By means of cosmic order, the truth, the power of the senses.

{2.6.2.8} By means of the *veda*, Prajāpati differentiated the two forms: the existent and the non-existent. By means of the *ṛta*, he drank the true power (*indriya*) with Soma; Prajāpati drank the pressed and the unpressed Soma. By means of the *ṛta*, he drank the true power. Having seen the two forms, Prajāpati differentiated them: truth and falsehood. He placed lack of faith in falsehood; Prajāpati placed faith in truth. By means of the *ṛta*, [he drank] the true power. Having seen the essence of the flowing libation, he drank the bright with the bright.

4. Milk is Soma; Prajāpati. 5. Through the cosmic order (ṛta), the power (indriya) of truth. 6. The drinking of the bright essence of the plant-juice. 7. The power of Indra. 8. This milk is nectar, honey.

Anuvāka 3 {2.6.3.9} {a} With reverence, the mighty ones send forth the sacrifice, rich in Soma, seated upon the sacred grass, abounding in heroes; placing Soma among the gods in heaven, may we, the sacrificers with beautiful hymns, rejoice in Indra. {b} That essence of yours which is gathered in the plants, the vigor of Soma pressed with *surā*—with that exhilaration, quicken the sacrificer, Sarasvatī, the two Aśvins, Indra, and Agni. {c} That [essence] which the two Aśvins and Sarasvatī extracted from the Asura Namuci for the sake of power...

{2.6.3.10} Here I consume this bright, honeyed, exhilarating King Soma. {d} Whatever of the flavorful pressed juice remains smeared here, which Indra drank with his powers—that of his I consume here as King Soma, with a gracious mind. {e} To the fathers who partake of the *svadhā* offering, *svadhā*! Adoration! To the grandfathers who partake of the *svadhā* offering, *svadhā*! Adoration! To the great-grandfathers who partake of the *svadhā* offering, *svadhā*! Adoration! The fathers have eaten.

{2.6.3.11} The fathers have rejoiced; the fathers have been satisfied; the fathers have purified themselves. O fathers, be pure! {f} May the Soma-loving fathers purify me; may the grandfathers purify me; may the great-grandfathers purify me with the filter that grants a hundred-year life. {g} May the grandfathers purify me; may the great-grandfathers purify me.

{2.6.3.12} By means of the purifier that bestows a hundredfold life, may I attain full span of life. {h} O Agni, you purify lives; {i} O Agni, purify yourself. {j} Purifying, belonging to the world of light; {k} May the divine folk purify me. {l} O Jātavedas, [you who possess] the purifier; {m} that purifier of yours which is in your flame. {n} With both [purifiers], O God Savitṛ; {o} the purifying one belonging to all the gods. {p} Those who are equal and of one mind, the fathers in the realm of Yama—may their world be [granted]; *svadhā*, obeisance! May the sacrifice be perfected among the gods.

{2.6.3.13} {q} Those who are my kinsmen, of one mind, living among the living—may their prosperity be ordained for me in this world for a hundred years. {r} I have heard of two paths of the fathers: that of the gods and that of mortals; by these two paths all that moves in this universe comes together, which lies between the father and the mother. {s} May this oblation be productive for me, bringing ten heroes and a full company for my well-being.

1. Gaining for oneself, gaining offspring; 2. gaining cattle, gaining fearlessness, gaining the world; 3. May Agni make my offspring abundant; 4. Bestow upon us food, milk, and seed; 5. May he maintain for us the increase of wealth, nourishment, and vigor—svāhā!

Anuvāka 4 {2.6.4.14} {a} With lead as the warp, the wise weave with their mind; the seers weave with woolen thread—the Aśvins, Savitṛ, and Sarasvatī, while Varuṇa heals the form of Indra. {b} That immortal form of his, the three deities, acting in harmony, established by their powers: the hair [was made] from young grass, manifoldly from sprouts; his skin became flesh, and the parched grains were not [the flesh]. {c} That [work], O Aśvins, the physicians who travel on the paths of Rudra...
Sarasvatī weaves her form within the radiant interior.

{2.6.4.15} With morsels of meat, they provide bone and marrow; with the *kārotara* strainer, they place [the mixture] upon the hide of cows. Sarasvatī, with her mind, weaves a delicate treasure—a beautiful form—for the two Nāsatyas. Like a red horse with foaming drink, the wise *nagnahu* weaver weaves the warp like a loom. With milk, they produce the bright, immortal generative seed; with wine, from urine, they produce semen. Driving away lack of understanding and ill-will, they cast far away the raw entrails, the wind, and the froth.

{2.6.4.16} {f} Indra, the good protector, [produced] truth with his heart; Savitṛ generated [him] with the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*). Varuṇa, healing the liver and the lungs—[the Ṛgveda says] "healing with joys"—does not diminish the kidneys with the Vāyavya cups, nor the bile. {g} The entrails are the cooking pot, overflowing with honey; the bowels are the vessels, like a cow that is easy to milk. The spleen, by its powers, is like the wing of a hawk; the navel is the throne-seat, the belly like a mother. {h} The rectum is the cauldron, the progenitor by its powers, in which, at the beginning, the embryo was within the womb.

The bladder is manifest as a fountain with a hundred streams; like a jar, it milks the *svadhā* offering for the fathers. His mouth is the seat, his head is the seat; by means of the seat [is he established]. The tongue is the strainer; the Aśvins and Sarasvatī are united therein. His tail is the protector, the physician; his hair is the bladder, vigorous with heat. From the two Aśvins comes the immortal eye through the two cups; brilliance from the goat and the cooked oblation. The eyelashes are woven with wheat and *kvala*-berries. Like a form, they clothe themselves in white and black.

{k} Like a ram for strength in its nostrils, the immortal path of breath is through the two cups. Sarasvatī, with her invocations, produced the out-breath (*vyāna*) and the nasal passages, along with the sacrificial grass and jujube fruits. {l} The bull is the form of Indra for his power; from his two ears comes the immortal hearing through the two cups. Like barley on the sacrificial grass, the beard-hair is on his brows; the *karkandhu* fruit was born from his mouth as honey from the bee. {m} On his body and in his lap is not the hair of a wolf; on his face are whiskers, not the fur of a tiger.

{2.6.4.19} The hair on the head is for glory; the crest is for splendor. The lion’s fur is brilliance and the senses. The Aśvins, the physicians, restored the limbs to the self. Sarasvatī joined the self together with the limbs. The form of Indra is a hundredfold life. Bestowing immortal light through the moon, {o} Sarasvatī, as a wife with the Aśvins, bears the well-fashioned embryo within the womb. Varuṇa [restores it] with the essence of the waters, as with a *sāman* chant.

Indra, the king in the waters, generating glory; the brilliance of cattle, the powerful oblation; the honeyed mead from the bee, with milk and the *parisrut* liquor; milked by the two physicians, the Aśvins, and by Sarasvatī—the immortal Soma-drop, pressed and unpressed.
