Anuvāka 5 {2.6.5.20} {a} You are Mitra; you are Varuṇa. {b} I am united with all the gods. {c} You are the navel of sovereignty; you are the womb of sovereignty. {d} Sit upon the pleasant [seat]; sit upon the comfortable [seat]. {e} Let it not harm you; let me not be harmed. {f} Varuṇa, whose law is firm, has sat down in his dwellings.

{2.6.5.21} For universal sovereignty, he of good resolve. {g} At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, with the healing power of the Aśvins, I consecrate you for splendor and for the luster of sacred knowledge. {h} At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, with the healing power of Sarasvatī.

{2.6.5.22} For valor, for the eating of food, I consecrate you. {i} At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, with the power of Indra, I consecrate you for prosperity, glory, and strength. {j} Who are you? Which one are you? For whom are you? To whom are you? {k} O you of fair renown! O you of fair renown! O you of auspiciousness! O you of auspiciousness! O King of Truth! {l} Prosperity is my head.

Glory is my face; brilliance is my hair and beard. The King is my breath, the immortal. The Sovereign is my sight; the Far-Shining is my hearing. My tongue is auspiciousness; my speech is greatness. My mind is wrath; the Self-Ruler is my passion. Joy and delight are my fingers and my limbs.

My mind is strength; my arms are power and sensory vigor; my hands are action and heroism; my self is the ruling power, my chest is the breastplate; my ribs are the kingdom, my belly is the domain; my shoulders, neck, and hips; my thighs, forearms, and knees; the common people are all my limbs; my navel is consciousness and discernment; my anus is honor and the perineum.

{2.6.5.25} Joy and delight are my testicles; fortune and good luck are my thighs. {m} Through my shanks and feet, I am Dharma; I am established as king among the people. {n} He is established in the sovereign power, established in the kingdom. I am established in horses, established in cattle; I am established in the limbs, established in the self; I am established in the vital breaths, established in nourishment; I am established in heaven and earth; I am established in the sacrifice.

{2.6.5.26} {o} The thirty-three gods, the eleven triads, the bounteous ones, who have Bṛhaspati as their domestic priest—by the impulse of the god Savitṛ, may the gods protect me with the gods: the first with the second, the second with the third, the third with truth, truth with sacrifice, and sacrifice with the Yajus formulas.

{2.6.5.27} May the *yajus* verses fulfill my desires through the *sāman* chants; may the *sāmans* fulfill them through the *ṛc* verses; may the *ṛcs* fulfill them through the *yājyā* offerings; may the *yājyās* fulfill them through the *vaṣaṭ* calls; may the *vaṣaṭ* calls fulfill them through the oblations (*āhuti*). May the oblations fulfill my desires! *Bhūḥ svāhā!* My hair is *prayati*; my skin is *ānati*, my arrival. My flesh is *upanati*, my wealth; my bone is [the same]; my marrow is *ānati*.

{a} O Gods, whatever offense against the gods we have committed, O divine ones, may Agni release me from that sin and from all distress. {b} Whether by day or by night we have committed sins, O Vāyu, may you release me from that sin and from all distress. {c} Whether waking or sleeping we have committed sins—

May Sūrya release me from that sin, from all distress. Whatever sin we have committed in the village, whatever in the forest, whatever in the assembly, whatever in our sensory faculties, whatever toward a Śūdra, whatever toward an Ārya, whatever sin we have committed under the law of one [person], for that you are the expiation. When we swear by the waters, by the inviolable ones, or by Varuṇa—therefrom, O Varuṇa, release us.

{2.6.6.30} {f} O Avabhṛtha, O Nicaṅkuṇa, you are the gliding one, O Nicaṅkuṇa! Through the gods, you have expiated the sin committed against the gods; through mortals, that committed against mortals. O God, protect us from wide-reaching harm! {g} May the waters and the plants be friendly to us; may they be unfriendly to him who hates us and whom we hate. {h} As one released from a wooden stake, as one bathed free from impurity after sweating.

{2.6.6.31} Purified like clarified butter by a strainer—may the waters cleanse me from sin. {i} Out of the darkness we have risen, beholding the higher light, the god Sūrya among the gods; we have reached the highest light. {j} Loosed is the bond of Varuṇa; cast off is the bond of Varuṇa. {k} Fuel art thou; may we prosper. Thou art kindling.

{2.6.6.32} You are brilliance; bestow brilliance upon me. I have followed after the waters; we have united with their essence. Rich in milk, O Agni, I have come; unite me with splendor, with progeny, and with wealth. The earth turns toward me; so does the dawn, so does the sun, and so does this entire living world. May I become the light of Vaiśvānara; may I attain my pervasive desire. *Bhūḥ*! *Svāhā!*

Anuvāka 7 {2.6.7.33} {a} Let the Hotṛ worship Indra with the kindling-stick at the place of libation, upon the navel of the earth. He is kindled at the height of heaven, the most powerful subduer of the peoples. Let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {b} Let the Hotṛ worship Tanūnapāt—the protector with his aids, the conqueror, the unconquered, the god Indra who finds the light of heaven—by means of the paths most rich in sweetness, together with the Narāśaṃsa-splendor.

{2.6.7.34} Let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {c} Let the Hotṛ worship Indra, who is praised with invocations (*iḍā*), the immortal one being summoned. The god, together with the gods, possessing heroic power, thunderbolt in hand, the destroyer of forts—let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {d} Let the Hotṛ worship Indra, seated upon the sacred grass (*barhis*), the bull whose deeds are for men, who sits upon the *barhis* in company with the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas.

{2.6.7.35} Let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {e} Let the Hotṛ worship: Might, vigor, and conquering power—the Doors have strengthened Indra. May the Doors, easy of access and increasing the Truth, open wide for the bounteous Indra. Let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {f} Let the Hotṛ worship: The two Dawns, Indra’s milch-cows, the well-yielding mothers, the great ones, the twin sisters—like two splendors, they have strengthened Indra, their calf.

{2.6.7.36} "O Hotṛ, sacrifice the two [deities] who have partaken of the clarified butter. {g} Let the Hotṛ worship the two divine Hotṛs, the physicians, the friends; they heal Indra with the oblation—[they are] the two seers, the gods, the wise ones. Bestow vital power upon Indra. O Hotṛ, sacrifice the two who have partaken of the clarified butter. {h} Let the Hotṛ worship the three goddesses, the three active ones of triple nature: Iḍā, Sarasvatī, and Bhāratī.

{2.6.7.37} May the wives of Mahīndra, rich in oblations, come; O Hotṛ, sacrifice the clarified butter! Let the Hotṛ worship Tvaṣṭṛ, the divine Indra, the physician, the well-sacrificing, the one adorned with ghee, the multiform, the of excellent seed, the bountiful. May Tvaṣṭṛ bestow powers upon Indra; let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Vanaspati, the immolator, the lord of a hundred powers, the lover of devotion, the divine power.

{2.6.7.38} Anointing with honey along easy paths, he makes the oblation savory with honey and ghee. Let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! The Hotṛ shall sacrifice to Indra: Svāhā to the clarified butter! Svāhā to the fat! Svāhā to the drops! Svāhā to the utterances of Svāhā! Svāhā to the hymns of the oblation! Svāhā to the gods who drink the clarified butter! Svāhā—Indra, being pleased by the Hotṛ’s [offering]! 1. May Indra enjoy the clarified butter! May Indra enjoy the clarified butter! 2. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

{a} Kindled at the face of the dawns, Indra, the doer of ancient deeds, has grown strong with the *puroruḳ* hymn. With the thirty-three gods, he of the thunderbolt-arm struck down Vṛtra and threw open the doors. {b} Narāśaṃsa, the hero who measures out [the sacrifice], Tanūnapāt, who conforms to the station of the sacrifice—the wise one, rich in fatness, anointing himself with milk and honey, bright with gold, performs the worship. {c} Praised by the gods, the lord of bay horses, the helper, being invoked with the oblation and exulting, [advances].

{2.6.8.40} Purandara, Maghavan, with the thunderbolt in his arm—may he come to our sacrifice, graciously accepting it. {d} May Indra, the Lord of Bay Steeds, graciously accepting the sacrificial grass, sit down facing the east upon the earth’s surface, spreading himself out on the wide-extending, pleasant seat, in harmony with the Ādityas and the Vasus. {e} May the swift-running, cleft-mouthed doors, like wives with noble husbands, hasten toward the Bull Indra; may the divine Doors open themselves wide on all sides, providing noble heroes, as they expand with their greatness toward the Hero.

{2.6.8.41} {f} Dawn and Night, the two vast ones, [serve] the vast Indra, the hero; they are rich in milk, yielding well, and adorned with beauty, weaving together with the thread, worshipping the God among the gods, O you of beautiful gold. {g} Measuring out in many places with the divine mind, the two first Hotṛ-priests with fair voices, placing [Indra] at the head of the sacrifice with honey, increase the eastern light with the oblation. {h} The three goddesses, increasing through the oblation, delighting in Indra, the bull, like wives [delight in their husband].

Sarasvatī with her milk [maintains] the unsevered thread; the goddess Iḍā, Bhāratī, she who overcomes all. Tvaṣṭṛ, bestowing vigor upon Indra—[he who is] far-reaching, radiant, for the sake of glory, performing many [deeds]—the bull, sacrificing, rich in seed, shall anoint the gods at the head of the sacrifice. Vanaspati, released as if from bonds, anointing himself by his own power like the divine slaughterer, filling Indra’s belly with oblations.

May he consume the oblation with honey and clarified butter. Indra, the hero, is the drop of the drops; acting as a bull, the bull, the subduer of the swift; moistening the oblation with honey that drips with clarity; may he enjoy it at the head of the sacrifice—svāhā!

Anuvāka 9 {2.6.9.43} {a} O filler of the peoples! {b} Since he has entered me. {c} Toward him, the converging [streams]. {d} This is indeed the truth: there is no other like you; Indra, neither god nor mortal, is greater. You slew the dragon who lay encompassing the flood; you released the waters toward the ocean. {e} O much-invoked one, you have overcome the enemies. Let your might be supreme; let your bounty be here. O Indra, bring us riches with your right hand. You are the lord of the wealthy rivers.

1. Place upon us that auspicious glory; 2. O Indra, great dominion, victorious over men, and powerful strength. 3. Protect our patrons and guard the wise leaders. 4. And bestow upon us wealth and food accompanied by noble offspring.

Anuvāka 10 {2.6.10.44} {a} The divine sacrificial grass (*barhis*), well-divine with the gods, has strengthened Indra as it was spread upon the altar, strewn heroically. Mown at dawn, gathered before the breaking of day, it has surpassed those who possess the sacrificial grass through wealth. For the winning of goods, for the granting of treasure, let him enjoy it; sacrifice! {b} The divine doors, in their gathering, have strengthened Indra on his journey—those that are wide-opening. Enclosed by the young calf and the child, let them drive away the backward-turning horse, the dust-stirring one.
For the winning of goods, for the granting of treasure, let them partake; sacrifice!

{2.6.10.45} {c} The two goddesses, Dawn and Night, have invoked Indra as the sacrifice proceeds. The divine clans have set forth. They have become well-pleased and well-disposed. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, may they partake; sacrifice! {d} The two goddesses, the Delighters, the repositories of wealth, have caused the god Indra to grow strong. One has driven away all enmities and hostilities; the other has brought hither desirable riches for the sacrificer, being well-skilled in bestowing them.

{2.6.10.46} May they partake of the gift of wealth from the treasury of wealth; perform the sacrifice! O two divine offerings of strength (*ūrjāhuti*), you who are well-milking cows, you have caused Indra to grow with milk. One has brought hither nourishment and strength; the other, the shared meal and the shared drink. Bestowing the old upon the new, and the new upon the old, the two offerings of strength have established strength and desirable riches for the sacrificer, being well-trained. May they partake of the gift of wealth from the treasury of wealth; perform the sacrifice!

{2.6.10.47} {f} The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the gods, have strengthened the divine Indra. Having struck down the malevolent, they have brought hither desirable riches for the sacrificer, being well-disposed toward him. For the winning of wealth, partake of the gift of wealth; sacrifice! {g} The three goddesses—the three goddesses—have strengthened their husband, Indra. Bhāratī has touched the sky; Sarasvatī, with the Rudras, [has strengthened] the sacrifice; and Iḷā, rich in cattle, [has strengthened] the household.

{2.6.10.48} May they partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of the bestowal of wealth; perform the sacrifice! O God Indra, Narāśaṃsa—having threefold protection and a triple-seated chariot—he has magnified the divine Indra. He is established with a hundred white-backed [cattle] and proceeds with a thousand. Mitra and Varuṇa are worthy of his office of Hotṛ; Bṛhaspati is the Stotra; the Aśvins are the Adhvaryus. May he partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of the bestowal of wealth; perform the sacrifice!

{2.6.10.49} {i} The divine Indra is the lord of the forest (vanaspati), golden-leaved, honey-sweet of branch, and rich in fine fruit. He caused the divine Indra to grow; with his top he reached the sky, he steadied the mid-air and the earth. For the sake of wealth, for the bestowal of wealth, let him partake; sacrifice! {j} The divine sacrificial grass (barhis) of the waters has caused the divine Indra to grow. It provides a good seat, joined with Indra; it has surpassed all other sacrificial grasses. For the sake of wealth, for the bestowal of wealth, let it partake; sacrifice!

2. Agni Sviṣṭakṛt is the god. 3. He has caused the god Indra to prosper. 4. Performing the well-offered sacrifice, he is Sviṣṭakṛt. 5. May he perform for us today the well-offered sacrifice. 6. For the winning of wealth, may he partake of the gift of wealth; sacrifice! Conquer!

Anuvāka 11 {2.6.11.50} {a} Let the Hotṛ worship Agni with the kindling-stick at the place of the libation (iḍā). [He worships] the Aśvins and Indra, and Sarasvatī. The goat is the smoke; with wheat and *kvala*-berries there is healing medicine. With young grass-shoots, honey, vigor, and sensory power. With milk, Soma, foaming liquor, ghee, and honey—let them partake of the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {b} Let the Hotṛ worship Tanūnapāt and Sarasvatī. The ram and the ewe are the healing medicine. Bringing it by the honeyed path, the Aśvins [bring] heroic power for Indra.

{2.6.11.51} With jujube fruits, with upavākā-herbs, with young sprouts—there is milk, Soma, foaming liquor, ghee, and honey. Let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! The Hotṛ shall worship Narāśaṃsa, who is not naked, the lord of Surā, the remedy. The ram is the physician Sarasvatī; the omentum of the Aśvins is like a chariot shining with moonlight, the heroic power of Indra. With jujube fruits, with upavākā-herbs, with young sprouts—there is milk, Soma, foaming liquor, ghee, and honey. Let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

{2.6.11.52} {d} Let the Hotṛ worship Sarasvatī, who is praised with the *iḍā* invocation and into whom oblations are poured; let him worship Indra, increasing his strength with a bull, his sensory power (*indriya*) with a cow, and heroic vigor for Indra with the Aśvins. With barley, jujubes, honey, and parched grains, as well as *māsara*, milk, Soma, foaming liquor, ghee, and honey—let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {e} Let the Hotṛ worship the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), which is well-spread and soft as wool; let him worship the two physicians, the Nāsatyas.

The two Aśvins are the physicians; the mare is pregnant. Sarasvatī is the physician, the milch-cow; she yields medicine for Indra. Milk, Soma, fermenting liquor, ghee, and honey—let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship the Doors, the Quarters, which are wide-expanding like caves. To the Aśvins belong the Doors, the Quarters; like Indra, they milk the two worlds (Heaven and Earth). Sarasvatī milks out all desires.

O Aśvins, [bring] a remedy for Indra; a bright light, vital power, milk, Soma, foaming liquor, ghee, and honey. Let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship the well-adorned Dawn and Night, the two Aśvins who are in harmony, who are united with Sarasvatī. Like a falcon through the mid-air, they have brought splendor and a remedy to Indra, with their heart. Milk, Soma, foaming liquor, ghee, and honey.

{2.6.11.55} Let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {h} Let the Hotṛ worship the two divine Hotṛs, the physicians Aśvins, who, like Indra, are watchful by day and by night with their remedies. Sarasvatī, the physician, [provides] strength; with lead she milks out power (*indriya*). Milk, Soma, foaming liquor, ghee, and honey—let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {i} Let the Hotṛ worship the three goddesses for the remedy; the three, the triple-natured, the active ones. The golden form is in Indra.

The Aśvins, Iḍā, and Bhāratī—Sarasvatī with her speech—have bestowed great vital power upon Indra: milk, Soma, foaming liquor, ghee, and honey. Let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Tvaṣṭṛ, Indra, and the Aśvins, and Sarasvatī as our healer. Might, speed, and sensory power—like a fierce and impetuous wolf is the physician; glory and medicine through the *surā* liquor.

{2.6.11.57} As for the *māsara* with *śrī*, [there are] milk, *soma*, *parisrut*, ghee, and honey. Let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! The Hotṛ shall worship Vanaspati, the immolator, the Lord of a hundred powers, the King who is like terrible wrath, the tiger. With reverence, [he worships] the Aśvins, the fury of Sarasvatī the physician. For Indra, they milk out power (*indriya*): milk, *soma*, *parisrut*, ghee, and honey. Let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

{2.6.11.58} Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Agni: Svāhā! for the drops of clarified butter; Svāhā! separately for the pieces of fat; Svāhā! the goat for the Aśvins; Svāhā! the ram for Sarasvatī; Svāhā! the bull for Indra, the lion, for power through force; Svāhā! Agni as the medicine; Svāhā! Soma as the power; Svāhā! Indra the Good Protector, Savitṛ, Varuṇa, the Lord of Physicians; Svāhā! Vanaspati, the beloved, as the path and the medicine; Svāhā! the gods who drink the clarified butter.

Svāhā! May Agni accept the oblation from the Hotṛ; may Agni, enjoying it, grant healing. Milk, Soma, foaming liquor, ghee, and honey—may they partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship the Aśvins, Sarasvatī, and Indra the Good Protector. These Somas are well-blended with spirituous liquor, pressed out with goats, rams, and bulls; with young grass and sprouts, with parched grains, and full of splendor. They are exhilarating, adorned with *māsara* liquor, bright, milky, and immortal.

1. These [soma juices] set forth for you, dripping with sweetness; may the Aśvins, Sarasvatī, and Indra the good protector, the slayer of Vṛtra, [accept them]. 2. May they enjoy the sweet soma. 3. Let them drink, let them rejoice, let them partake of the soma. 4. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Anuvāka 12 {2.6.12.60} {a} Kindled is Agni, O Aśvins; the Gharma is heated, the Virāj is pressed. Sarasvatī, the cow, yields here the bright Soma, the power of Indra. {b} The two physicians, the Aśvins, and Sarasvatī—protectors of the body at the pressing—shall carry the sweet Soma, the power of Indra, through the regions for Indra by their paths. For Indra, Sarasvatī [carries] the Indu; with Narāśaṃsa, the Nagnahu [is offered]. (Note: *nagnahu* is glossed as *dyumaun ta nagnahum*).

The Aśvins, the two physicians, poured forth honey as a healing medicine into the pressed [soma]. Sarasvatī, being invoked, [bestowed] powers and vigor upon Indra. With the *iḍā*-offerings, the Aśvins [and] Dyumna bestowed nourishment, strength, and wealth. The Aśvins [took] the pressed juice of Namuci; Sarasvatī brought that bright soma, mixed with the *parisrut* liquor, along with the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) for Indra to drink.

{2.6.12.62} {f} Like wide-opening doors, the quarters are spacious; like the two Aśvins, the quarters are for the sake of the Aśvins. Like Indra, he milks the two worlds; Sarasvatī milks all desires. {g} Dawn and Night, the two Aśvins, by day and by evening with their powers, are for the sake of Indra. Being of one mind and well-adorned, they anoint themselves together with Sarasvatī. {h} O Aśvins, protect us by day; O Sarasvatī, protect us by night.

{2.6.12.63} The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the physicians, protect Indra together at the pressed juice. {i} Sarasvatī is threefold in three ways: the Aśvins, Bhāratī, and Iḍā. They have well-pressed for Indra the sharp Soma with the *parisrut* ferment, a source of exhilaration. {j} O Aśvins, [the Aśvins]—the honey is a medicine; Sarasvatī is our medicine. Tvaṣṭṛ has bestowed upon Indra glory, splendor, and every form at the pressed juice. {k} Indra, the Lord of the Forest, according to the seasons, exerts himself with the *parisrut*.

3. The thick liquid, honey for the Aśvins. 4. Sarasvatī, the cow, yields [it]. 5. Like Soma with milk, O Aśvins. 6. Adorned with *māsara* [grain-beer], [the] *parisrut* [fermented liquor]. 7. They have united it with Sarasvatī. 8. *Svāhā!* To Indra, the pressed honey.

Anuvāka 13 {2.6.13.64} {a} The Aśvins [brought] the invigorating oblation; Sarasvatī, through inspired thought, [brought] from the Asura Namuci the bright wealth, the bounty for Indra. {b} Him whom the Aśvins and Sarasvatī strengthened with the oblation—Indra—he shattered the strength and the bounty (magha) [or, according to Ḍyumoṇṭa, the sacrifice (makha)] along with the Asura Namuci. {c} To that Indra, the cattle, the two Aśvins, and Sarasvatī were joined.

Bestowing [power], they have shouted in praise for the Indra-like sacrifice with the oblation. Those who bestowed Indra-power—Savitṛ, Varuṇa, and Bhaga—he, the good protector and lord of the oblation, attends to the sacrificer. Savitṛ and Varuṇa bestow [gifts] upon the sacrificing donor; the good protector took away the wealth and the power of Namuci.

Varuṇa [bestowed] sovereignty and power; Savitṛ, with Bhaga, [bestowed] splendor; Sutrāman, with glory, [bestowed] strength. Bestowing these, they attained the sacrifice; they sat down in bliss. The Aśvins, with cattle, [bestowed] power; with horses, heroism and strength; with the oblation, Sarasvatī and Indra increased the sacrificer. Those two Nāsatyas, well-adorned, O heroes whose paths are golden, and Sarasvatī, rich in oblations—O Indra, protect us in our rites!

3. Those two are physicians of skillful deeds. 4. She is Sarasvatī, the one who yields milk easily. 5. He is the slayer of Vṛtra, the lord of a hundred powers. 6. For Indra they have established vital power (*indriya*). {a} The divine sacrificial grass (*barhis*), Sarasvatī, and the Aśvins—these three, together with Indra, have placed brilliance like sight within the two eyes; through the sacrificial grass they have established vital power. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, may they partake; sacrifice! {b} The divine Doors, the Aśvins, and Sarasvatī the physician—these have placed breath and vigor within the nose; through the Doors they have established vital power. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, may they partake; sacrifice!

{2.6.14.68} {c} The goddesses Dawn and Night, the Aśvins, and Sarasvatī the physician—[these] have placed strength and speech in our mouth, and sensory power from the two Dawns. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, may they partake; perform the sacrifice! {d} The goddesses Joṣṭrī, the Aśvins, and Indrāṇī, the good protectress, and Sarasvatī—[these] have placed hearing and glory in our ears, and sensory power from the two Joṣṭris. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, may they partake; perform the sacrifice!

{2.6.14.69} {e} O Goddess Ūrjāhuti, you who are easy to milk, yield your milk; with that milk, O Sarasvatī and the two physicians, the Aśvins, protect Indra. Place bright light and vital power within our breasts as an oblation. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, may they partake; perform the sacrifice! {f} The gods, the physicians of the gods—the two Hotṛ-priests and the Aśvins, along with Sarasvatī through their *vaṣaṭ*-cries—have placed brilliance in the heart and mental power, as well as vital strength, by means of the two Hotṛs. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, may they partake; perform the sacrifice!

{2.6.14.70} {g} Three goddesses, the three goddesses—Sarasvatī, the two Aśvins, Bhāratī, and Iḍā—have placed vital strength and manly power in the center, in the navel, for Indra. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of wealth, may they partake; sacrifice! {h} O divine Indra Narāśaṃsa, the chariot with its triple protection, drawn by Sarasvatī and the two Aśvins, moves along. Like seed, like immortal form, like a source of birth, Tvaṣṭṛ has bestowed manly powers upon Indra. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of wealth, may they partake; sacrifice!

{2.6.14.71} {i} The divine Indra is the lord of the forest (vanaspati). With golden leaves for the Aśvins, and with well-ripened fruit for Sarasvatī—{ḍyumoṇṭa for Sarasvatī}—it ripens its honey for Indra. Like vigor, like speed; like a bull, like brilliance—may the lord of the forest bestow upon us powers of the senses. For the winning of wealth, may they partake of the gift of wealth; sacrifice! {j} The divine sacrificial grass (barhis) of the waters, strewn at the rite for the Aśvins, soft as wool for Sarasvatī.

{2.6.14.72} O Indra, your seat is pleasant. For the sake of sovereignty, they have established King Manyu with the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) as a source of power. For the winning of wealth and the granting of riches, may they partake; sacrifice! The divine Agni Sviṣṭakṛt shall sacrifice to the gods in due order: to Indra and the two Aśvins as the two Hotṛ-priests; to Sarasvatī with speech for Speech; to Agni and Soma as Sviṣṭakṛt. Indra is well-sacrificed, the good protector; Savitṛ and Varuṇa are the physicians. The god Vanaspati is sacrificed to. The gods who drink the clarified butter (*ājya*) are well-sacrificed.

Agni has been sacrificed with Agni; the Hotṛ has been sacrificed for the Hotṛ as the Sviṣṭakṛt. Bestowing glory and sensory power, strength, honor, and the *svadhā*-offering, may they partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth—sacrifice!

Anuvāka 15 {2.6.15.73} {a} Today he has chosen Agni as the Hotṛ-priest—this sacrificer who has pressed the Soma, cooking the cooked offerings, cooking the sacrificial cakes (puroḍāśas), drawing the cups (grahas), and binding a goat for the Aśvins and Sarasvatī, and binding a ram for Sarasvatī and the Aśvins, and binding a bull for Indra, the Aśvins, and Sarasvatī. {b} Today the divine Vanaspati has become well-established—for the Aśvins with the goat, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra.

{2.6.15.74} For Sarasvatī with a ram; for Indra and the Aśvins [with a ram]. For Indra with a bull; for the Aśvins and Sarasvatī [with a bull]. {c} They cooked those [animals] from the fat, desiring to take the first portions. They strengthened themselves with draughts. The Aśvins, Sarasvatī, and Indra Sutrāman, the slayer of Vṛtra, drank the *surāmaṇ* soma. The hymns and shouts of joy—{ḍyumoṇṭa: the hymns and shouts of joy}—the Vimadas ate. They strengthened themselves with songs of praise.

{d} Today, O Ṛṣi, descendant of Ṛṣis, grandson of Ṛṣis, this sacrificer, having pressed the Soma, has chosen you from among many who have assembled, thinking: "He shall offer to me among the gods wealth that is desirable. {e} Those gifts which the gods gave as divine gifts—declare them to us, proclaim them, and urge them forward! O Hotṛ, being impelled for the auspicious recitation and sent by man, speak the hymns for the *sūktavāka*.

Anuvāka 16 {2.6.16.75} {a} We invoke you, desiring [you]. {b} O Agni, come to us with fair splendor. {c} O Soma, you are great fortune. {d} O Soma, you have perceived through our inspired thought. {e} For by you, O Soma, were our ancient fathers [sustained]. {f} O Soma, being in harmony with the fathers. {g} O fathers who sit upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). {h} I have summoned the fathers. {i} The fathers are invited. {j} The fathers who are consumed by the fire (*agniṣvātta*). {k} We invoke the fire-consumed fathers who follow the seasons.

Those who are swift, who have attained the drinking of Soma at the Narāśaṃsa rite—may they, as our coursers, be easy to invoke; may they be auspicious to us, auspicious to our bipeds, and auspicious to our quadrupeds. Those who are consumed by the Agniṣvātta fire and those who are not consumed by the Agniṣvātta fire...

{2.6.16.76} The Fathers who release from distress, worthy of Soma—those who exist as immortals, both higher and lower—let them speak for us; let them protect us. {m} Rejoicing in the groats-mash (*karambha*) milked from Vānyā, rising up, both the lower and the higher ones—the Agniṣvāttas, in harmony with the seasons, accompanied by Indra—let them enjoy this oblation. {n} O Agni, Kavyavāhana... {o} Thou, O Agni Jātavedas, being praised... {p} Mātali with the Kavyas.

Those who have satisfied [the gods] among the gods, striving with zeal; who increase the *hotṛ*-priesthood, fashioning hymns with their chants—O Agni, come hither with those well-disposed ones, with the true *kavya* fathers who sit at the *gharma* vessel. Worshipping Agni—the bearer of oblations, ageless, and much-beloved—with clarified butter as an offering, [I approach] him who sits near, the carrier of *kavya* for the fathers. May he provide us with offspring rich in heroes.

Anuvāka 17 {2.6.17.77} {a} Let the Hotṛ worship at the place of *iḍ* the kindled one, the great glory, the well-kindled, the excellent Agni, who is Indra, the bestower of vital strength; [bestowing] the Gāyatrī metre, sensory power, and a three-year-old cow as vital strength—let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {b} Let the Hotṛ worship Tanūnapāt, whose vows are pure, the piercer, whom Aditi bore as her embryo.

{2.6.17.78} To pure Indra, the bestower of vital strength; to the *uṣṇih* metre, the power of the senses; to the *dityavāh* ox, bestowing vital strength—let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! The Hotṛ shall worship the one worthy of praise, the most excellent slayer of Vṛtra, the might that is to be praised with invocations (*iḍā*s); to Soma, to Indra, the bestower of vital strength; to the *anuṣṭubh* metre, the power of the senses; to the three-year-old ox, bestowing vital strength.

{2.6.17.79} Let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {d} Let the Hotṛ worship the immortal one who sits upon the excellent sacrificial grass, accompanied by Pūṣan, seated upon the beloved sacrificial grass—the immortal Indra, the bestower of vigor. Bestowing the *bṛhatī* metre, sensory power, and the five-striped cow as vital strength, let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {e} Let the Hotṛ worship the eloquent ones, easy of access, the increasers of cosmic order (*ṛta*).

The divine doors are golden; they bring the Brahman, the radiant Indra, the bestower of vital strength. May the *paṅkti* metre here bestow sensory power and a four-year-old ox that grants vitality. Let it partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship the two well-formed, well-crafted, lofty ones, Night and Dawn, who are beautiful to behold like two jewels. They bring all-encompassing Indra, the bestower of vital strength. May the *triṣṭubh* metre here bestow sensory power.

{2.6.17.81} May the beast of burden, the ox, bestowing vigor, partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {g} Let the two wise Hotṛs, the supreme glory of the gods, the two divine seers joined together, [invoke] Indra, the bestower of vigor, the Jagatī meter, and sensory power here; may the ox, bestowing vigor, partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {h} Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to the beautiful ones.

{2.6.17.82} Three golden goddesses—Bhāratī, Bṛhatī, and Mahī—bestow upon Indra, the lord who grants vital strength, the Virāj meter as his power here; like a milch-cow, they bestow life-sustaining vigor. Let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! {i} Let the Hotṛ worship Tvaṣṭṛ, the one of excellent seed, the increaser of prosperity, who bears various forms separately, who bestows nourishment and vital strength upon Indra.

The two-footed metre is here the sense-power; bestowing vigor like a bull, a cow—let it partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship the Lord of a Hundred Powers (Indra), who has golden wings, who is praised with hymns, who bears the reins, the subduer, Bhaga, Indra, the bestower of vigor. The *kakubh* metre is here the sense-power; bestowing vigor like a barren cow and a cow that miscarries—let it partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

1. Let the Hotṛ sacrifice the Svāhā-offerings. 2. [He sacrifices] to Agni Gṛhapati individually. 3. To Varuṇa the healer, the seer. 4. To Indra, the lordly power who bestows vigor. 5. To the Aticchandas metre, the sensory power. 6. Bestowing the great bull and the cow as vigor. 7. Let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Anuvāka 18 {2.6.18.84} {a} Agni, kindled with fuel, well-kindled, most excellent; the Gāyatrī metre and sensory power; the three-year-old bull—these have bestowed vital strength. {b} Tanūnapāt of pure vows, and Sarasvatī, O Tanūnapāt; the Uṣṇih metre and sensory power; the two-year-old bull—these have bestowed vital strength. {c} Agni is to be praised with invocations; Soma is the immortal god.

The *anuṣṭubh* metre is the faculty; the three-year-old steer bestowed vital power. Agni, accompanied by Pūṣan, is the one with excellent sacrificial grass; the immortal one for whom the grass is strewn. The *bṛhatī* metre is the faculty; the five-year-old steer bestowed vital power. The divine doors, the great quarters, and the god Brahmā, Bṛhaspati—the *paṅkti* metre is the faculty here; the four-year-old steer bestowed vital power.

{2.6.18.86} {f} O Dawn, the two youthful and well-adorned ones; all the immortal gods; the *triṣṭubh* metre; the sense-power (*indriya*); the four-year-old ox—the bull has bestowed vitality. {g} The two divine invokers (the two invokers of bliss), the two physicians, joined with Indra as their companion; the *jagatī* metre; the sense-power here; the draft-ox—the bull has bestowed vitality. {h} The three—*iḍā*, Sarasvatī, and Bhāratī; the Maruts, the clans.

The *virāj* meter has bestowed sensory power here; the milch-cow, the bull—these have bestowed vital strength. Tvaṣṭṛ, the wondrous impeller, and Indra-Agni, the increasers of prosperity, have bestowed it. The *dvipād* meter has bestowed sensory power here; the draft-ox, the bull—these have bestowed vital strength. The Vanaspati is our pacifier; Savitṛ, impelling, bestows fortune. The *kakubh* meter has bestowed sensory power here; the barren cow, the cow that miscarries—these have bestowed vital strength. *Svāhā*! Varuṇa [sanctifies] the sacrifice.
May Sukṣatra provide healing. The Aticchandas meter is power. 3. The Bṛhat [sāman], the bull, and the cow have bestowed vigor.

Anuvāka 19 {2.6.19.88} {a} With the spring season, the gods, the Vasus, with the Trivṛt [stoma]—the chant, with the Rathantara [sāman] and with brilliance—they have placed the oblation and vigor in Indra. {b} With the summer season, the gods, the Rudras, with the Pañcadaśa [stoma]—the chant, with the Bṛhat [sāman] and with glory—they have placed the oblation and vigor in Indra. {c} With the rainy season, the Ādityas, with the Saptadaśa [stoma]—the chant.

{2.6.19.89} With the Vairūpa [Sāman], with the Viś [deities], and with vigor, they have placed the oblation and vital strength in Indra. {s} With the autumnal season, the gods, the Ekaviṃśa [Stoma], and the Ṛbhus have praised the glory with the Vairāja [Sāman]; they have placed the oblation and vital strength in Indra. {e} With the winter season, the gods, the Maruts, and the Triṇava [Stoma] have praised the power with the Śakvarī verses; they have placed the oblation and vital strength in Indra. 1 {f} With the dewy season, the gods, the Trayastriṃśa [Stoma], and the nectar have praised it;
3 with truth, the Revatī verses, and the Kṣatra [power], 4 they have placed the oblation and vital strength in Indra.

Anuvāka 20 {2.6.20.90} {a} The divine sacrificial grass (*barhis*), divine, has magnified the divine Indra, the bestower of vitality. Through the *gāyatrī* meter, it has bestowed sensory power, brilliance, and vitality upon Indra. For the winning of wealth, let it partake of the gift of wealth; sacrifice! {b} The divine doors, divine, have magnified the divine Indra, the bestower of vitality. Through the *uṣṇih* meter, they have bestowed sensory power and vital breath upon Indra. For the winning of wealth, let them partake of the gift of wealth; sacrifice!

{2.6.20.91} {c} The two goddesses, Dawn and Night, have magnified the god Indra, the bestower of vital strength. Through the *anuṣṭubh* metre, they have bestowed sensory power and speech upon Indra. For the winning of wealth and the granting of treasure, let them partake; sacrifice! {d} The two goddesses, the lovers (*joṣṭrī*), have magnified the god Indra, the bestower of vital strength—the goddesses have magnified the god. Through the *bṛhatī* metre, they have bestowed sensory power and hearing upon Indra. For the winning of wealth and the granting of treasure, let them partake; sacrifice!

{2.6.20.92} {e} The two goddesses, Ūrjā and Āhutī, have caused the god Indra, the bestower of vitality, to grow; they, as goddesses, have caused the god to grow. Through the *paṅkti* metre, they have bestowed sensory power (*indriya*) and bright vitality upon Indra. For the sake of wealth and the granting of riches, accept [the offering] and sacrifice! {f} The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the gods, have caused the god Indra, the bestower of vitality, to grow; they, as gods, have caused the god to grow. Through the *triṣṭubh* metre, they have bestowed sensory power and brilliance upon Indra. For the sake of wealth and the granting of riches, accept [the offering] and sacrifice!

{2.6.20.93} {g} Three goddesses—three goddesses—increased Indra, the husband who bestows vital strength. Through the *jagatī* meter, they bestowed sensory power, strength, and vitality upon Indra. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of wealth, let them partake; sacrifice! {h} The god Narāśaṃsa increased the god Indra, the bestower of vital strength. The god increased the god through the *virāj* meter, bestowing semen and vitality upon Indra. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of wealth, let him partake; sacrifice!

{2.6.20.94} {i} The divine Vanaspati has caused the divine Indra, the bestower of vital strength, to grow; the divine [one] has caused the divine [Indra] to grow by means of the *dvipadā* metre, bestowing sensory power (*indriya*) and fortune (*bhaga*), and placing vital strength (*vayaḥ*) in Indra. For the winning of wealth, let him partake of the gift of wealth; sacrifice! {j} The divine Barhis, the lord of the waters, has caused the divine Indra, the bestower of vital strength, to grow; the divine [Barhis] has caused the divine [Indra] to grow by means of the *kakubh* metre, bestowing glory (*yaśas*) and vital strength (*vayaḥ*) in Indra.

0. May he partake of the gift of wealth from the treasury of wealth; perform the sacrifice! 1. The divine Agni Sviṣṭakṛt has caused the divine Indra, the bestower of vitality, to prosper. 2. The god has magnified the god. 3. By means of the Atichandas metre, he has bestowed sensory power. 4. Bestowing the ruling power and vitality upon Indra, may he partake of the gift of wealth from the treasury of wealth; perform the sacrifice!

Prapāṭhaka 7, Anuvāka 1. The *trivṛt* stoma is employed. The *trivṛt* is indeed spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*); verily, he wins spiritual luster. The Soma sacrifice is an *agniṣṭoma*. The *agniṣṭoma* is indeed spiritual luster; verily, he wins spiritual luster. The *rathaṃtara* Sāman is employed. The *rathaṃtara* is indeed spiritual luster; verily, he wins spiritual luster. The Hotṛ priest wears a wreath.

{2.7.1.2} Aruṇa, Mirmira, Triśukra—this indeed is the form of spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*). By means of this very form, he wins spiritual luster. Bṛhaspati desired, "May I attain the position of domestic priest among the gods. He saw this Bṛhaspatisava sacrifice; he performed it; with it he sacrificed. Thereupon, he indeed attained the position of domestic priest among the gods. Whoever should desire the position of domestic priest, he should sacrifice with the Bṛhaspatisava.

{2.7.1.3} He goes to the office of the domestic priest (*purodhā*). At his morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*), when the *nārāśaṃsa* cups have been set down, eleven sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇā*) are led forth. Eleven at the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina-savana*), when the *nārāśaṃsa* cups have been set down; eleven at the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*), when the *nārāśaṃsa* cups have been set down. They amount to thirty-three. There are indeed thirty-three deities; thus he wins the deities themselves. The horse is the thirty-fourth. Now, the horse belongs to Prajāpati.

Prajāpati is the thirty-fourth among the deities. As many deities as there are, those very ones he wins. He sprinkles him on a black antelope skin; for the black antelope skin is the form of the Brahman. He thus endows him with the splendor of the Brahman. He sprinkles him with clarified butter; for clarified butter is brilliance. He thus bestows brilliance upon him.

As for the fact that there is an offering to Agni: prosperity indeed has Agni as its mouth. Now, as for the offering to Pūṣan: Pūṣan is indeed nourishment; nourishment belongs to the Vaiśya; verily, he wins nourishment. The offering to Savitṛ is for instigation. Now, as for the offering to Tvaṣṭṛ: for Tvaṣṭṛ fashions forms. The offering to Varuṇa is for the sake of release from Varuṇa’s noose.

{2.7.2.6} Furthermore, whoever is one who is envious (sūyate) is indeed related to Varuṇa. Now, as for that which belongs to the Viśvedevas: the Vaiśya is indeed related to the Viśvedevas. And as for that which belongs to the Maruts: the Vaiśya is indeed related to the Maruts. There are these seven oblations; the Maruts consist of seven groups. A speckled four-year-old cow is offered to the Maruts. The Maruts are indeed the common people (viś); thus, he is consecrated from the midst of the common people. Therefore, he is dear to the common people.

3 For he is consecrated from the midst of the people. 4 He consecrates him upon the hide of a bull; 5 for that is the procreator. 6 He consecrates him with curds; 7 for curds are strength and the means of eating food. 8 Verily, by means of strength and the means of eating food, he causes him to prosper.

As for the fact that there is an offering to Agni: the Brāhmaṇa is indeed related to Agni. And as for the one to Soma: the Brāhmaṇa is indeed related to Soma. The one to Savitṛ is for the sake of impulsion. And as for the one to Bṛhaspati: this indeed is the domain of speech for the Brāhmaṇa. And as for the one to Agni-Soma: the Brāhmaṇa is indeed related to Agni; when those two (Agni and Soma) come together, [the Brāhmaṇa partakes in both].

{2.7.3.8} Now he becomes more vigorous. Now, as for the offering to Sarasvatī: this is indeed the manifest power of speech belonging to the Brāhmaṇa. The offering to Varuṇa is for the sake of freedom from Varuṇa’s noose; moreover, whoever is accused, he is indeed subject to Varuṇa. Now, as for the offering to Heaven and Earth: when Indra raised his thunderbolt against Vṛtra, Heaven and Earth did not approve of it. They approved of it only through this very portion.

{2.7.3.9} This [offering] is for the authorization of the *vajra*. [The intention is: "May he be consecrated with the *vajra* authorized. There are these eight oblations. The *gāyatrī* consists of eight syllables; the *gāyatrī* is spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*). Through the *gāyatrī*, he indeed acquires spiritual luster. He purifies the clarified butter with gold for the sake of splendor and radiance. He sprinkles [the sacrificer] upon a black antelope skin. For this black antelope skin is the form of the *ṛc* and *sāman* of the Brahman. That which is the black antelope skin is indeed that.
2. Verily, he consecrates him over the *ṛc* and the *sāman*. 3. He consecrates him with clarified butter. 4. Thus he becomes more powerful.

There is no pressing of Soma with Soma; for this [Soma] has already been pressed, for it has already been extracted. Indeed, that which is already pressed is not pressed again. He offers a cow in milk to Soma (*saumī sūtavaśā*). Soma is indeed the depositor of seed; thus he deposits seed. He consecrates him with a verse addressed to Soma; for she (the cow) is a depositor of seed, and Soma is seed; thus he places seed within him. Whatever belongs to the Rājasūya except for the Soma sacrifice—all that is now accomplished.

O Soma, may we rejoice after you—the invincible one who carries us across in battles and conflicts, the showerer of rain, the lord of the waters, the protector of the stronghold, born for the fray, possessing secure dwellings and great renown, the ever-victorious one.

He who is consecrated by means of Soma is a divine consecration (*devasava*). He who is consecrated by means of an animal sacrifice is a divine consecration. He who is consecrated by means of an *iṣṭi* sacrifice is a human consecration (*manuṣyasava*). Indeed, the gods bestowed this [consecration] upon Pṛthu; from that time on, he was able to procreate even wild animals. Of whatever offspring speak speech, however many there may be—of them all he is consecrated.

{2.7.5.12} Whoever performs this sacrifice, and whoever knows it thus—he consecrates [the sacrificer] with a verse addressed to Narāśaṃsa. For Narāśaṃsa is indeed men. Having thus concealed [the act], he then consecrates him. Whatever belongs to the Rājasūya that does not require a high altar (*uttaravedī*), all that is included here. [The verses are: 0. "They who have given me fifty horses—this is the joint praise. 1. "O Agni, grant us brilliant and great glory. 2. "Make it vast for our patrons (*maghavan*). 3. "O Immortal One, grant it like that of men, for the sake of men."

This is the Gosava sacrifice. It is a thirty-six-fold Ukthya with the Bṛhat-sāman; during the Pavamāna chant, the Kaṇva-rathaṃtara is employed. That which is the Vājapeya is the Samrāṭ-sava; that which is the Rājasūya is the Varuṇasava. Prajāpati is self-sovereignty (svārājya) as the Supreme Lord (parameṣṭhī); the cow indeed is self-sovereignty. One becomes like a cow.

{2.7.6.14} He who sacrifices with this [rite], and he who knows it thus—both the *bṛhat* and the *rathaṃtara* [sāmans] are employed; for that is self-sovereignty (*svārājya*). Ten thousand cows are the sacrificial fees; for that is self-sovereignty. He consecrates him with curdled milk; for that is self-sovereignty. On ground not yet dug up for the altar, to the south of the *āhavanīya* fire, he consecrates him in response to the *bṛhat* chant. This earth, indeed, is the *rathaṃtara*.

"That one is the Bṛhat. He thus consecrates him with these two [verses] without any interval. This [rite] is indeed a Paśustoma; by it, it is a Gosava. It is the thirty-sixfold [stoma] in its entirety. "Born wealthy, increased by power, the best sustainer of dominion among dominions, the bestower of vigor—great, established in greatness, be watchful over the dominion and the kingdom! "I consecrate you with the self-sovereignty of Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin," he says. He thus causes him to attain self-sovereignty.

The splendor that is in the lion, in the tiger, and in the adder; that which is in the fire, in the Brahmin, and in the sun; the auspicious goddess who gave birth to Indra—that goddess has come to us, united with splendor. The splendor that is in the royal drum when it is struck, in the neighing of the horse, and in the power of man; the auspicious goddess who gave birth to Indra—that goddess has come to us, united with splendor. The splendor that is in the elephant, in the leopard, and in gold; that which is in horses, in men, and in cattle—[that splendor has come to us].

{2.7.7.2} The fortunate goddess who gave birth to Indra—may she come to us, in harmony with our splendor, in the axle-pins of the chariot, in the vigor of the bull, in the wind, in Parjanya, and in the breath of Varuṇa. The fortunate goddess who gave birth to Indra—may she come to us, in harmony with our splendor. You are the sovereign; you are the far-ruling; you are the universal ruler; you are the self-ruling. For Indra, the radiant one, I prepare you, the radiant. For Indra, the powerful one, I prepare you, the powerful.

{2.7.7.3} For Indra, the possessor of milk, I mix you, who possess milk. For Indra, the possessor of life, I mix you, who possess life. You are brilliance; I bestow that upon you. May my mouth be brilliant; may my head be brilliant. Brilliant on every side, face me with brilliance; endow me with brilliance. You are vigor; I bestow that upon you.

{2.7.7.4} May my face be full of vigor; may my head be full of vigor. May I be full of vigor from every side. Sustain me with vigor! You are milk; I bestow that upon you. May my face be full of milk; may my head be full of milk. May I be full of milk from every side. Sustain me with milk!

{2.7.7.5} You are life. That I bestow upon you. May my face be endowed with life; may my head be endowed with life; may I be full of life, facing in every direction. Sate me with life! O Agni, make this child long-lived and radiant. O King Varuṇa and Soma, grant him dear progeny. O Aditi, like a mother, grant him protection. O All-Gods, so that he may reach old age.

{2.7.7.6} You are life; you are all-encompassing life; you are total life; you are every life. From whence the wind is swift as thought, from whence the rivers flow—by the splendor of all those [waters], I consecrate you with luster. Like the ocean, you are deep in majesty; like Soma, you are inviolable; like Agni, you face in every direction; like the sun, you are pervasive with light.

{2.7.7.7} That essence which is in the flowing of the waters—that I take for this man, the son of such-a-man, for the sake of splendor and the luster of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcasa*). That essence which is in the wave of the waters—that I take for this man, the son of such-a-man, for the sake of might and heroic power. That essence which is in the midst of the waters—that I take for this man, the son of such-a-man, for the sake of nourishment and procreation. That essence of the waters which is worthy of sacrifice—that I take for this man, the son of such-a-man, for the sake of life and long-livedness.

Advance, display your heroism! You are fierce, a watcher, a slayer of rivals. Ascend, O increaser of friends! For you the gods have spoken. O slayer of Vṛtra, mount the chariot on both sides with Aṅka and Nyaṅka. As he mounts, all have adorned him. Clothed in glory, he moves, self-luminous. Great is that name of this Asura; the multiform one has taken his stand upon the immortal realms. May Indra rejoice after you, may Bṛhaspati rejoice after you.

{2.7.8.2} May Soma favor you; may Agni favor you. May all the gods favor you. May the seven kings who have been consecrated favor you. May Mitra and Varuṇa favor you here. May Heaven and Earth, the source of universal well-being, favor you. May Sūrya with his days favor you; may the Moon with the constellations favor you. May both Heaven and Earth, the wise ones, and may the bright, vast sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) fulfill you. May *Svadhā*, Soma, and Agni take notice of you. May this one fill the two regions (*rajasī*), the seat of bliss.

Prajāpati created offspring. Once created, they went away from him. Prajāpati saw this rice-porridge (odana). Having become food, he stood firm. Not finding sustenance elsewhere, the offspring returned to Prajāpati. Verily, the offspring return to him who performs this sacrifice and who knows it thus, seeing him as having become food itself. All kinds of food come to be his.

{2.7.9.2} All men; he wins all kinds of food and all men. "Thou art a sovereign (rāḍ), thou art a universal ruler (virāḍ)," he says; verily, he causes him to attain self-sovereignty (svārājya). In that he gives gold, by that he wins luster. In that [he gives] a bow with three arrows, by that he wins vigor. In that [he gives] a goad...

Through that [water], he obtains nourishment; through that which is the water-pot, he obtains life-span. When he fastens the gold, since gold is indeed light, he thereby places light within him. Moreover, since gold is brilliance, he thereby bestows brilliance upon himself. When he eats the cooked rice, he thereby secures all of this.

{2.7.9.4} That [sacrifice] was performed by him in a single way. It should be performed under Rohiṇī; for Rohiṇī is indeed the Brāhmaṇa, and therefore it is from that very source. Moreover, he thereby makes him the pre-eminent one among his equals. It should be performed when the sun has risen; for all creatures rejoice at the rising of this [sun]. He who knows thus becomes desirable to behold and beautiful to look upon. The exponents of the Veda say:

{2.7.9.5} "Is it to be entered, or is it the *avabhṛtha*? When he purifies [him] with bunches of *darbha*-grass, is it that he thereby enters, or is it that he does not enter? He purifies him with three [stalks]. These worlds are three; verily, by means of these worlds he purifies him. Moreover, the *darbha*-grass is indeed the brilliance and luster of the waters. In that he purifies him with bunches of *darbha*-grass, he consecrates him with the brilliance and luster of the waters.

Anuvāka 10 {2.7.10.1}. Prajāpati desired, "May I become more than much. He saw this Pañcaśāradīya sacrifice; he took it up; with it he sacrificed. Thereupon, indeed, he became more than much. He who should desire, "May I become more than much," let him sacrifice with the Pañcaśāradīya; he becomes more than much. This is indeed the Marutstoma, for the Maruts are the most numerous among the gods.

He becomes manifold who sacrifices with this [rite], and he who knows it thus. It is the Pañcaśāradīya sacrifice. There are five seasons in a year; verily, he finds firm support in the seasons, in the year. Moreover, the *paṅkti* meter has five syllables; the sacrifice is fivefold; verily, he wins the sacrifice itself. The seventeen-fold hymn-form (*saptadaśa-stoma*) does not exceed it; Prajāpati is seventeenfold; [it serves] for the attainment of Prajāpati.

Anuvāka 11 {2.7.11.11}: Agastya sprinkled bulls for the Maruts. Indra seized them. They approached him, raising their thunderbolt. Agastya and Indra pacified them with the *Kayāśubhīya* hymn. He called upon them once they were pacified. Because there is the *Kayāśubhīya*, it serves for pacification. Therefore, these bulls dedicated to Indra and the Maruts become the *savanīya* offerings. Three are sacrificed on the first day; likewise on the second; likewise on the third.

{2.7.11.2} Thus on the fourth day. On the final day, five [animals] are sacrificed; for this day is, as it were, the highest. He who sacrifices with this [rite], and he who knows it thus, becomes the highest among his equals. This sacrifice is indeed self-sovereignty (*svārājya*). By means of this, Ekayāvan Kāndama attained self-sovereignty. He who sacrifices with this attains self-sovereignty.

And he who knows this thus: This Stoma belongs to the Maruts. By means of it, the Maruts became the most numerous among the gods. He becomes the most numerous among his peers who performs this sacrifice, and he who knows it thus. This sacrifice is indeed the Pañcaśāradīya. It consumes food up to the fifth generation of descendants for him who performs this sacrifice, and he who knows it thus. The Stomas do not exceed the seventeenfold; Prajāpati is seventeenfold. Thus, one does not depart from Prajāpati.

Anuvāka 12 {2.7.12.1} His are the ageless guardians of the house, the purifying fires with glowing smoke. Brightly shining, strengthening, and active, they rest in the woods like winds or Soma-draughts. Sacrifice for us to Mitra and Varuṇa; sacrifice to the gods and the lofty *Ṛta*. O Agni, sacrifice in your own home. O Aśvins, drink the pressed juice—you two who shine with fire, whose vows are pure, who bring the sacrifice according to the season.

{2.7.12.2} Two of different forms move about, moving toward their own purpose; each suckles her calf in turn. In one, he becomes tawny, self-sustaining; in the other, he is seen bright and full of splendor. These two move in succession by means of their creative power (*māyā*); like two playing children, they go around the sacrifice. One looks upon all beings; the other, ordaining the seasons, is born again. Three hundred and three thousand gods, together with thirty-nine, have worshipped Agni.

{2.7.12.3} They sprinkled him with clarified butter and spread the sacrificial grass for him; then they established him as the Hotṛ priest. Agni is kindled by Agni—the sage, the master of the house, the youth, the bearer of oblations, whose mouth is the ladle. Agni is the belly of the gods; he of purified strength and wise intellect, the god has come with the gods. The Maruts, adorned with splendor, belong to all peoples; we implore their fierce and mighty protection.

{2.7.12.4} They are the lords, the sons of Rudra, clothed in rain; like lions, they are of roaring will and bounteous givers. Whether you are in the highest, the middle, or even the lowest heaven, O fortunate Maruts—O Rudras, take notice of this our oblation which we sacrifice here, or whatever else belongs to us. I praise Agni, the one of good help, with prostrations; may he, having entered here, discern what has been done for us. Like chariots with swift-footed horses, I offer my praise; may I successfully accomplish the hymn of the Maruts, moving in a clockwise direction.

Hear us, O Agni, you with ears that hear, together with the gods who are the carriers [of the sacrifice] and your companions. Let Mitra, Varuṇa, and Aryaman sit upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). They are the ones who come early to the rite. Aditi is the mother of all those worthy of sacrifice; Agni is the guest of all human beings. May Agni, choosing the protection of the gods, be gracious to us—he who possesses all knowledge. O Agni, we beg for favor from you.

{2.7.12.6} The worshipful ones have established glory in heaven; they have made Night and Dawn of different forms. They have joined together the dark color and the ruddy. O Agni, the Ādityas have made you their mouth; the pure ones have made you their tongue, O Sage. Those who bestow gifts attend upon you at the sacrifices; in you the gods eat the offered oblation. We establish you, O Agni, as the accomplisher of the sacrifice, the Hotṛ priest, the officiating minister—O God, we choose you, the wise, the swift, the immortal messenger.

Anuvāka 13 {2.7.13.1} Mount your two bay horses; come, yoked to the chariot! Like Vāyu with his teams, come toward us. Drink the soma-juice, being poured out for us; O Indra, svāhā, we have offered it to you for your exhilaration. With whose pressed juice does the bull, the lord of teams, rejoice? The slayer of Vṛtra comes for the drinking of the soma. We invoke Indra in the great battle; we invoke Indra in the small one—the wielder of the thunderbolt, our ally against the obstructors.

{2.7.13.2} He who is doubly the greatest slayer of Vṛtra, Indra, the lord of a hundred powers, has been found. With his bay steeds, he comes to our pressed juice. That hero, generating light, [invokes] Indra. By this prayer, the one who overcomes obstacles and is vast as a mountain, the mighty one, honored with hymns according to the Eternal Law (*ṛta*), has shattered the obstructing cloud with his thunderbolt. And that wealth of horses, O Indra, which was among the Nahuṣa clans, you made manifest at the beginning for the tribes.

In battles we invoke Indra, who is easy to call upon, the divine folk who release from distress and perform good deeds—Agni, Mitra, Varuṇa, and Bhaga—for our gain; and Heaven and Earth and the Maruts for our well-being. Having found a vast domain, full of light, he has brought together for his friends a chariot from the beginning. Indra, shining forth, generated with the heroes the sun, the dawn, the path, and Agni. O Knower, lead us toward a wide space, the light of heaven, fearlessness, and prosperity.

Lofty are your arms, O Indra, you the steadfast; may we seek refuge in them, the great ones. Come to us with all your aids, being well-disposed, O Lord of the bay horses, accepting our prayer. Turning toward us, O fair-cheeked one, with your steadfast steeds, bestow upon us manly vigor, O Indra. For Indra the wielder of the thunderbolt, the cows have yielded the milk-mixture, the honey-sweetness, which he found in the secret place. May those milch-cows of yours, O wielder of the thunderbolt, bring us prosperity.

The arms, the teams, and all-desired riches, day after day increasing and ever more abundant—O Indra, these are full of food and nourishment. This great hymn I offer to you, the Great One, since my inspired thought has been polished for your praise. At every festival and at every impulse, the gods have rejoiced in Indra, the conqueror, because of his power.

Prajāpati created cattle. Once created, they went away from him. He did not recover them by means of the Agniṣṭoma; he did not recover them by means of the Ukthya; he did not recover them by means of the Ṣoḍaśin; he did not recover them by means of the Rātri; he did not recover them by means of the Sandhi. He said to Agni, "Seek these for me. Agni did not recover them by means of the Trivṛt Stoma.

He said to Indra, "Desire these for me. [The text reads: "Desire the joys for me. Indra did not obtain them with the fifteenfold hymn-form (*pañcadaśa-stoma*). He said to the All-Gods (*viśve devāḥ*), "Desire these for me. The All-Gods did not obtain them with the seventeenfold hymn-form (*saptadaśa-stoma*). He said to Viṣṇu, "Desire these for me. Viṣṇu obtained them with the twenty-onefold hymn-form (*ekaviṃśa-stoma*) and secured them with the *vāravantīya* chant.

With the verse, "Viṣṇu strode through this," he strode forth. Because cattle might otherwise tend to fall away, one should sacrifice with this [rite]. That which he obtained is the reason for the Aptoryāma's name, its "attainment" (āptoryāma). By means of this, the gods, having won the victories to be won, obtained whatever desire they desired. Whatever desire one desires, that one obtains by means of this.

This tiger moves about, having entered into the fire. He is the son of the seers, the protector against curses. With reverence, with homage, I offer to you. Do not falsely perform the portion of the gods. O God Savitṛ, impel us toward our father for procreation. Grant him height; grant him breadth. And then, O Savitṛ, grant us fullness in all things. Day by day, impel us toward many cattle. Having come into being, he moves about, having entered into beings. He has become the overlord of beings.

{2.7.15.2} He performs the Rājasūya at his death. May that king grant his approval for this sovereignty. With those crafts by which he made the earth expand and firm, with which Prajāpati anointed the sky, and with which he wove together speech of every form—with that splendor, O Agni, anoint him here. With those brilliant rays by which Āditya shines, by which the sun of manifold luster became visible, and by which he wove speech through the lotus-like [vessels]—with that splendor, O Agni, anoint him here.

{2.7.15.3} May he come hither, shining with power over the five peoples; may he be preeminent like Indra, possessed of progeny. May there be for him abundant, wondrous radiance. May he fill both worlds and the intermediate space. O Kaśyapa, that craft of yours which is luminous, powerful, abundant, and of wondrous radiance—in which the seven suns are fixed together—upon that place set this king. You are heaven; you are earth. Upon the tiger-skin, you are a tiger.

{2.7.15.4} Ascend to the great quarters; let all the subjects desire you. Let not the kingdom fall away from you. With the splendor of all those waters—those celestial ones that have come together with milk, those that are in the intermediate space, and those that are on earth—with the luster of them all, I sprinkle you with glory. I sprinkle you with divine glory, together with milk, so that you may be the increaser of the kingdom.

{2.7.15.5} So may Savitṛ fashion you. All [the gods] have strengthened Indra, whose expanse is like the ocean, with their songs—he who is the best of chariot-warriors among chariot-warriors, the true lord and master of spoils. May the Vasus sprinkle you from the east with the Gāyatrī metre; may the Rudras sprinkle you from the south with the Triṣṭubh metre; may the Ādityas sprinkle you from the west with the Jagatī metre.
May all the gods sprinkle you from the north with the Ānuṣṭubh metre; may Bṛhaspati sprinkle you from above with the Paṅkti metre.

Thee, the ruddy, the fierce wolf, the stirrer of the fray, shining at the head of the Maruts’ flames—the Sūryavat, the Maghavan, the all-conquering Indra, most worthy of invocation in our hymns—we shall call upon. Stretch forth your arms that we may live; sprinkle our pastures with ghee. O youthful ones, make us renowned among the people. Hear these my invocations, O Mitra and Varuṇa! I draw down the two arms of thee, Indra, the doer of heroic deeds.

Go forth, display your heroism! You are fierce, a watcher, a slayer of rivals. Ascend, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra; the gods have spoken in favor of you. The two hooks, Aṅka and Nyaṅka, who are on both sides of the chariot, moving along the darkness at the edge of the wind—the far-shooting, powerful, winged one: may those fires of ours, being full, carry us across. Homage to you, O Seer, speak! For the sake of non-distress (or joy), for the sake of self-sustenance, I address you.

{2.7.16.2} O Indra, may we, unharmed, be on every side near you, O Sublime One. Thus, O Brahman, let this be yours alone. Mount upon the chariot when you hold the thunderbolt in your hand; as one with noble horses, O God, you grasp the reins. Ascend, O Slayer of Vṛtra; ascend him who is ascending around you. Let Indra rejoice after you, let Mitra and Varuṇa rejoice after you. May both Heaven and Earth, the wise ones, favor you. May the bright, vast sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) carry you across. May Svadhā, Soma, and Agni take notice of you; may Savitṛ favor you with his impulse.

All songs have magnified Indra, who is as vast as the ocean; the best of chariot-warriors among chariot-warriors, the true lord and master of spoils. May the clamors of the armies, eager for the bowstrings, spare me here. May the swelling stakes enter into me, the lord of cattle. May Anumati grant her approval to this; may Mother Earth and Father Heaven do so as well.

{2.7.16.4} Therefore, O pressing-stones, you who press the Soma and bring delight; therefore, O Aśvins, you who possess good fortune, hear this! Release the highest wrath for our protection! Embracing the tiger, they urge on the lion for great good fortune. Like the ocean, easy to invoke, standing firm within the waters, they groom the leopard. May that Sun rise up; may this word of mine rise up. Rise up, O divine Sun, together with my voice!

I am the one who causes speech to be spoken. May speech abide in me as a sustainer. May the rivers flow; may the rain-clouds pour forth. May the plants bear good fruit. May I become the king of these: of those possessing food, of those possessing boiled rice, and of those possessing curd-mixture.

Anuvāka 17 {2.7.17.1} Those Keśins who were the first to sit for the sacrificial session (sattra), by whom this world which shines forth was brought into being—to them I offer oblations in many ways with clarified butter. With the increase of wealth, endow this man with splendor. There is no release from the sacred word (brahman) and from austerity (tapas). The initiation (dīkṣā) is double-named, for it is both self-controlled and fierce. The hair grows forth and becomes tufted; over its shaving, the sacred word alone has mastery, and none other. Ascend the couch, overcome your enemies; the initiation has flowed away, for it is self-controlled and fierce.

{2.7.17.2} Bestow the sacrificial fee; may you live on in response. Now be released from the noose of Varuṇa. With that razor wherewith Savitṛ, the knower, shaved King Soma and Varuṇa—with that, O Brahmins, shave this [hair] of his. Endow him with vigor, with wealth, and with splendor. Let not this splendor follow after your hair; may Dhātṛ ordain it for you thus. May Indra, Bṛhaspati, and Savitṛ bestow splendor upon you.

{2.7.17.3} From them they sought a storehouse in many ways: between heaven and earth, in the waters, and in the light of heaven. Having deposited it in a clump of *darbha* grass, which has been made potent, unite this man with manly vigor and splendor. May Savitṛ bestow strength upon your two arms; may Soma anoint you with milk and ghee. O Aśvins, deposit this beauty in women. Unite this man with manly vigor and splendor. That which the comb has marked as your parting line—

Or rather, when you shaved with a razor, O Aśvins, deposit this beauty in women; unite this man with manly power and vigor. Anuvāka 18 {2.7.18.1} The Maruts, his own people, did not show respect to Indra. Being disrespected, he perceived this *vighana* (cleaving) sacrifice. He took it up and performed it. By means of it, he shattered that resistance of theirs. Because he shattered it (*vyahan*), that is the reason for the name of the *vighana*. He who performs this sacrifice, and he who knows it thus, shatters evil and the rival.

{2.7.18.2} A king whom the subjects do not honor, or a Brāhmaṇa who is shrouded by darkness and evil—such a person should sacrifice with this [rite]. Having struck it down by means of the *vighana* (the "shatterer"), he attains sovereignty over the subjects. For him, there are two twelve-fold hymns and two twenty-four-fold hymns; that is indeed the "breaking forth" (*audbhidya*). This is the breaking forth of the ruling power: namely, that his own subjects bring him tribute.

The people bring tribute to him; it comes to him unopposed—he who knows thus. In the beginning, the ruling powers (kṣatrāṇi) strove together side by side. Indra seized their ruling powers, thinking, "These shall no longer be ruling powers. That is the origin of the name of the constellations (nakṣatra). He who sacrifices with this [rite], and he who knows it thus, takes away the splendor and power of his superior rival.

Just as two side-horses might be harnessed alongside a pair of draft-oxen, so are these two even-numbered *stomas*. They are performed during the odd-numbered *stomas* for the sake of striking away evil; he who performs this sacrifice and he who knows it thus strikes away evil and the rival. Just as there are charioteers and village headmen, so are the *chandas* (metres). Upon them that sun has mounted—the *bṛhatīs* [have mounted]. (Ānandāśrama ed.: *abhyūḍhaḥ*).

They chant on *satobṛhatī* verses; [the result is] "May I be great with offspring and cattle"—thus indeed. They chant with interwoven verses. The ruling power (*kṣatra*) is indeed interwoven with the common people (*viś*). Verily, he interweaves him with the ruling power by means of the common people. They chant with interwoven verses. The village headman is indeed interwoven with his kinsmen. Verily, he interweaves him with his kinsmen. They chant with interwoven verses. A man is indeed interwoven with evils. By means of the interwoven verses, he drives away his evils.

Prapāṭhaka 8, Anuvāka 1 The wise one, increasing wealth, follows the white steed who possesses plump food and is the glory of his teams. They have stood forth with one mind for Vāyu; all these men have performed noble deeds. Both worlds brought him forth for the sake of wealth; the divine Dhiṣaṇā establishes the god for the sake of wealth. Now his own teams attend upon Vāyu, and the white one, the bestower of riches, in his preeminence. (c) O Vāyu! (d) With those [teams] by which... (d) Toward Vāyu, the lofty hymn of praise.

{2.8.1.2} Possessing great wealth, possessing all desirable things, {O Dyumanta, possessor of all desirable things}, you who fill the chariot; whose path is radiant, you who rule over the teams of horses—O Sage, worthy of sacrifice, you seek the Sage. With your hundreds of teams, with your thousands of teams, come to our ritual, come to our sacrifice! O Vāyu, rejoice in this oblation! Do you all protect us always with blessings! O Prajāpati, none other than you has encompassed all these created beings. Whatever desire we have in sacrificing to you, may that be ours.

{2.8.1.3} May we be masters of riches! We worship the lord of riches, the adorable, the great, the most heroic in this battle for the winning of booty—Prajāpati, the first-born of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*). Let us worship the god; may he speak in our favor. O Prajāpati, you are the ancient guardian of the treasure, the father of the gods, the progenitor of creatures, the lord of the entire moving world, the protector from afar. O God, enjoy our oblation at our invocation! These worlds, the intermediate directions, and the cardinal points are yours.

{2.8.1.4} From the distant realms, from the hollows and the heights—O Prajāpati, creator of all, source of life, O God, graciously accept this our oblation! Worship Prajāpati first among those worthy of sacrifice; worship him who is to be honored at the head of the gods. May he grant us wealth and heroic vigor; may he release upon us the increase of riches for our kin. He who rules over wealth, the giver of hundreds, worthy of praise; he who is the guardian of cattle scattered abroad; Prajāpati, the first-born of Cosmic Order (Ṛta).

{2.8.1.5} May he of a thousand abodes enjoy our oblation! O Soma and Pūṣan—these two gods! O Soma and Pūṣan, the measurer of the mid-region, [you mount] the seven-wheeled chariot that moves through all, which turns in every direction and is yoked by the mind. O bulls, you quicken that [chariot] which has five reins. One of you made his seat high in heaven; the other [is] upon the earth and in the intermediate space. May those two release for us an abundance of many boons and much food, and the increase of wealth as our central point.

{2.8.1.6} May Pūṣan, the all-enlivener, quicken our intellect; may Soma, the lord of wealth, bestow riches upon us. May the divine Aditi, who is free from enemies, protect us. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly. One [of the two] has brought forth all beings; the other moves along beholding everything. O Soma and Pūṣan, favor my prayer; through you two may we conquer all hostile armies. Varuṇa has propped up the highest heaven.

Whatever this may be—O gamblers! Away with your wrath; that I implore of you. Through the favor of the Ādityas, the sacrificial fee is not [to be withheld]. The Ādityas, upholding the three earths, uphold the pure sacrifice of the gods, the waters.

Anuvāka 2 {2.8.2.7} They, the bright, pure, and radiant ones, the Ādityas, sit upon the beloved sacrificial grass. May the gods come from heaven on a single chariot to our sacrifice, being well-pleased with us. May those sons of Aditi swell the fatness of the food and the clarified butter, they who are born of Truth and delight in it. May the worshipful Ādityas extend their favor toward the sacrificer; may the Ādityas grant us a nourishment full of desire. May the sons of Aditi come to our sacrifice, the Ādityas, by the paths traveled by the gods.

{2.8.2.2} Bending toward us, may they grant the desire of the donor; may they enjoy the cake mixed with ghee. May they hold back Destruction and drive away Misfortune. Striving with their rays, unyielding, O Ādityas, accept our offered oblation and the *vaṣaṭ*-call according to our desire, O worshipful ones! We invoke the Ādityas for protection according to our desire—those who, creating all beings, have spread them abroad. May the sons of Aditi sit upon the strewn sacrificial grass to consume the oblation, O gods.

{2.8.2.3} Sit upon this strewn sacrificial grass at this sacrifice, O Adityas, driving away the stingy one who follows evil ways. O sons of Aditi, grant us your favor, you Ādityas, graciously accepting this oblation. O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth, O God, you who know all ways. Keep far from us the sin that leads astray; we shall offer to you the most abundant speech of homage. Bring forth for Agni, for his bright luster, an offering and a most purified hymn.

{2.8.2.4} He who, through his wisdom, moves between all divine and human births; toward him go our songs and god-seeking thoughts, seeking to obtain wealth. Agni, who is beautiful to behold, fair of countenance, swift-moving, the bearer of oblations, and the steward of men—O Agni, do thou drive away from us all maladies. Those who offer no fire-sacrifice oppress the people; O God, for our well-being, protect the earth with all thy imperishable powers, O Worthy of Worship.

{2.8.2.5} O Agni, you, as a new protector, carry us across all difficulties with blessings. Be for us a broad, vast, and wide fortress; be a source of peace and well-being for our children and descendants. O poets, being inspired by your thoughts, you who seek the gods lead the sacrificial ladle toward the gods. Carrying oblations for Agni, the ladle, full of ghee, moves forward, rich in strength and turned toward the right. The men have yoked the chariot for Indra. We have grasped your right hand, O Indra.

{2.8.2.6} O Lord of treasures, we seek after treasures; for we know you, O Hero, as the master of cattle. Grant us wonderful, bull-like wealth.
