To Prajāpati! *Svāhā* to Agni and Soma! *Svāhā* to Indra and Agni! *Svāhā* to Indra! *Svāhā* to Mahendra! *Svāhā* to the gods who drink the clarified butter! *Svāhā* to Agni, enjoying [the offering] from the *hotṛ*’s office! May [the deities] partake of the clarified butter, O Agni!

Anuvāka 6 {3.5.6.1} May Agni strike down the Vṛtras, seeking wealth through inspired praise—kindled, bright, and invoked with oblations. May Agni, taking pleasure, partake of the clarified butter. O Soma, you are the lord of the good; you are the king and the slayer of Vṛtra; you are the auspicious power of will. May Soma, taking pleasure, partake of the clarified butter and the oblation. Agni, beautifying his own body according to his ancient birth, the sage has grown great through the inspired singer. May Agni, taking pleasure, partake of the clarified butter.
O Soma, we who are skilled in speech magnify you with our songs; enter us with great kindness. May Soma, being pleased, partake of the offering of clarified butter.

Anuvāka 7 {3.5.7.1} Agni is the head of heaven, the summit; he is the lord of this earth. He quickens the seeds of the waters. He is the leader of the sacrifice and of the mid-world (*rajas*). Wherever you accompany with your auspicious teams of horses, you place your sun-bright head in heaven. O Agni, you have made your tongue the bearer of the oblation. Prajāpati—none other than you has encompassed all these created beings. Whatever desire we offer to you, may that be ours.

{3.5.7.2} May we be masters of riches! He knows his father, he knows his mother; he becomes a son, he becomes one who possesses wealth again. He has opened up the sky, the mid-air, and the heavens; he has become all worlds, he has come into being. O Agni and Soma, you who possess common knowledge, invoked together, accept our songs! You have established yourselves among the gods. O Agni and Soma, acting with a single will, you two have placed these luminous realms in the sky.

You two, O Agni and Soma, have released the rivers from reproach and from disgrace when they were seized. O Indra and Agni, you adorn the luminous realms of heaven in the contests for booty. This heroic deed of yours is well known: he who strikes down Vṛtra wins the prize. He who honors Indra and Agni, the two victorious ones, shall rule over abundant wealth; they are most powerful through their might, seeking strength. O Indra, [bring] winning wealth.

Bring hither for our protection the ever-conquering, most exalted one who has won all battles. O you invoked by many, you have utterly subdued your enemies; let your supreme strength be here, and let there be bounty for us. O Indra, bring us riches with your right hand; you are the lord of the wealthy rivers. Great is Indra through his might, like Parjanya rich in rain; he has grown strong through the hymns of Vatsa. Great is Indra, manly, filling the people.

And he, of double strength, undiminished by his powers, has grown for us toward heroic might. Vast, wide, and well-fashioned by the makers, he has become so. Satisfy the longing gods, O youngest one; knowing the seasons, O Lord of Seasons, sacrifice here. With those who are the divine officiating priests, O Agni—you among the hotṛ-priests are the most skilled at sacrifice. To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt: Agni has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Agni; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Soma.

He has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Agni; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Prajāpati; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Agni and Soma; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Indra and Agni; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Indra; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Mahendra; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of the gods who drink the clarified butter. May he sacrifice to the dear abodes of Agni, the Hotṛ; may he sacrifice to his own greatness. May they offer the desirable nourishments; may Jātavedas perform these sacrifices.

May he enjoy the oblation! O Agni, Hotṛ of the sacrifice, you who purify with your flame, come today to the people; for you are the sacrificer. Sacrifice according to the *ṛta*, since you have spread yourself out with greatness. O youngest one, carry the offerings that belong to you today.

Section 8 {3.5.8.1} The Rathantara has been invoked together with the Earth; may the Rathantara together with the Earth invoke me! The Vāmadevya has been invoked together with the Intermediate Space; may the Vāmadevya together with the Intermediate Space invoke me! The Bṛhat has been invoked together with the Sky; may the Bṛhat together with the Sky invoke me! The seven Hotṛ-priests have been invoked; may the seven Hotṛ-priests invoke me! The milch-cow has been invoked together with the bull; may the milch-cow together with the bull invoke me!

The portion is invited; it is my friend. May the portion, my friend, invite me. Invited! Ho! Iḍā is invited. Iḍā is invited. May Iḍā invite us. Iḍā is invited. Iḍā, the daughter of Manu, whose foot is in ghee, who belongs to Mitra and Varuṇa, is invited. The sacred formulation (brahman) created by the gods is invited.

{3.5.8.3} The divine *adhvaryu*s are invited; the human ones are invited—those who have protected this sacrifice, those who shall increase the lord of the sacrifice. Heaven and Earth are invited—the two born of old, observers of *ṛta*, goddesses whose sons are gods. This sacrificer is invited; he is invited for the subsequent sacrifice to the gods; he is invited for the greater performance of the oblation; he is invited to the celestial station. "May the gods enjoy this my oblation"—invited is he in that [thought]. Invited is all that is dear to him; invited is he by all that is dear which has been invited.

Anuvāka 9 {3.5.9.1} May the divine *barhis* (sacrificial grass) partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of bestowing wealth. May the divine *narāśaṃsa* partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of bestowing wealth. May the divine Agni Sviṣṭakṛt—the joyous sage of excellent riches, the priest whose thoughts are true, the invoker who is more skilled at sacrifice than any other invoker—partake. O Agni, those gods whom you have sacrificed to, those whom you have gladdened, and those who have rejoiced in your office as invoker: send this sacrifice, which has attained its goal and goes to the gods, to the gods in heaven.
And you, O Agni, having been the invoker Sviṣṭakṛt, accept the invocation of reverence for the sake of bestowing wealth for the gift of wealth.

Anuvāka 10 {3.5.10.1} This has become auspicious for Heaven and Earth. We have attained the *sūktavāka* and the *namovāka*. May we succeed in the recitation of the hymn, O Agni; you are the speaker of the hymn. You have taken refuge in Heaven and Earth. May Heaven and Earth be full of protection for you, O sacrificer, at this sacrifice—granting bliss, giving life-sustaining gifts, free from fear, beyond reproach, providing wide pastures, and creating security.

{3.5.10.2} Vṛṣṭidyāvā and Rītyāpā; the two who are auspicious and the two who are blissful; the two who are full of vigor and full of milk; the two who are easy to approach and the two who are good to dwell with. Through their knowledge: Agni has enjoyed this oblation; he has grown strong; he has made it greater. Soma has enjoyed this oblation; he has grown strong; he has made it greater. Agni has enjoyed this oblation.

{3.5.10.3} He has grown strong; he has made it greater. Prajāpati has enjoyed this oblation; he has grown strong; he has made it greater. Agni and Soma have enjoyed this oblation; they have grown strong; they have made it greater. Indra and Agni have enjoyed this oblation; they have grown strong; they have made it greater. Indra has enjoyed this oblation; he has grown strong; he has made it greater. Mahendra has enjoyed this oblation.

{3.5.10.4} They have grown strong; they have made it greater. The gods who drink the clarified butter have enjoyed the clarified butter; they have grown strong; they have made it greater; [they have made] joy. Agni, by means of the office of the *hotṛ*, has enjoyed this oblation; he has grown strong; he has made it greater. In this successful office of the *hotṛ* that leads to the gods, this sacrificer, so-and-so, makes his aspiration: he aspires for long life; he aspires for good offspring; he aspires for companionship with his kinsmen.

He prays for a higher sacrifice to the gods; he prays for a greater offering; he prays for the celestial abode; he prays for all that is dear. Whatever he prays for with this oblation—may he attain it, may he prosper in it; may the gods grant it to him. May the god Agni win that from the gods, and we, the men, [win] it from Agni: both the sacrificed and the enjoyed. May both Heaven and Earth protect us from distress. Here is your path, and here is this [offering]. Homage to the gods!

Section 11 {3.5.11.1} We choose that auspiciousness (śaṃyoḥ), a path for the sacrifice, a path for the lord of the sacrifice. May there be divine well-being for us; may there be well-being for human beings. May the healing medicine rise upward. May it be well with our bipeds; may it be well with our quadrupeds.

Anuvāka 12 {3.5.12.1} Swell up; may [the Soma] be gathered unto thee. Here [I invoke] Tvaṣṭṛ, the foremost; may that be our virile seed. May the longing wives of the gods protect us; may they assist us for the winning of offspring and the acquisition of booty. Those who belong to the earth and those who are in the domain of the waters—may those goddesses, who are easily invoked, grant us protection. And let the divine dames, the wives of the gods, come forth: Indrāṇī, Agnāyī, Aśvinī, and Rāṭ. May Rodasī and Varuṇānī hear us; may the goddesses come forth, they who are the seasons of women.

Agni is the Hotṛ, the lord of the household, he is the king. Jātavedas knows all births; he who belongs both to the gods and to mortals, he is the most excellent sacrificer among those who offer sacrifice, the upholder of Ṛta. O Agni, lord of the households of men, we have made thee great with fuel. May our household duties not be deficient; sharpen us with thy keen splendor.

The Rathantara has been invoked together with the Earth; may the Rathantara invoke me together with the Earth. The Vāmadevya has been invoked together with the Atmosphere; may the Vāmadevya invoke me together with the Atmosphere. The Bṛhat has been invoked together with the Sky; may the Bṛhat invoke me together with the Sky. The seven Hotṛ-priests have been invoked; may the seven Hotṛ-priests invoke me. The milch-cow has been invoked together with the bull; may the milch-cow invoke me together with the bull.

The portion is invited; the friend is invited. May the portion, the friend, invite me. "Invited!"—O! The *iḍā* is invited; the *iḍā* is invited. May the *iḍā* invite us. The *iḍā* is invited; the *iḍā* is invited. The daughter of Manu, whose foot is in ghee, belonging to Mitra and Varuṇa—the sacred formulation (*brahman*) created by the gods is invited.

The divine Adhvaryus are invited; the human ones are invited—those who have protected this sacrifice and those who shall prosper the wife of the sacrificer. Heaven and Earth are invited, the first-born, observers of cosmic order (*ṛta*), goddesses whose sons are gods. This sacrificer is invited, like Indrāṇī who is not widowed, like Aditi who has noble sons. She is invited to the higher worship of the gods; she is invited to the performance of abundant oblations; she is invited to the celestial abode.
"May the gods enjoy this oblation of mine"—thus they are invited therein. "Her entire beloved [portion] is invited; she is invited as the beloved of everything that is invited."

Prapāṭhaka 6, Anuvāka 1 The seekers of the gods anoint you, O Lord of the Forest, with divine honey at the sacrifice. If you stand upright, bestow wealth here; or if you dwell in the lap of this mother earth. Rise up, O Lord of the Forest, upon the height of the earth! Being measured with perfect skill, bestow splendor upon the one who carries the sacrifice. Being placed in front of the kindled fire, winning for yourself the imperishable prayer and heroic strength.

Driving far away from us all lack of understanding, rise up for our great good fortune! Stand upright like the god Savitṛ for our protection. Standing upright, you are the winner of booty when we, with our anointed priests, call upon you from every side. Standing upright, protect us from distress with your guidance; burn up every devouring fiend. Raise us up for the chariot, for movement, and for life; find favor for us among the gods.

Born, he is born on the auspiciousness of days; he, the mortal, [is] the resplendent one, increasing in the assembly. The wise, skillful ones purify him with their inspired thought. The sage, seeking the gods, raises his voice. Young, well-attired, and enveloped, he has come; he becomes even more excellent as he is being born. The wise poets, devout in mind, lead him upward. Broad-chested, immortal, clothed in clarity, well-invoked with *svāhā*.

Agni is the carrier of oblations for the sacrifice. Him, the pressers of Soma with uplifted ladles—truly, with such devotion, possessing the sacrifice—have brought near for protection. You, O Agni, are Varuṇa and Mitra; the Vasiṣṭhas magnify you with their hymns. In you let there be riches easily won. Do you all protect us evermore with blessings.

Anuvāka 2 {3.6.2.1} Let the Hotṛ worship Agni, kindled with a good kindling, well-kindled at the navel of the earth, in the gathering place of wealth, at the height of heaven, in the station of *iḍ*. Let him enjoy the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Tanūnapāt, the offspring of Aditi, the guardian of the world. Today let the god anoint the god-faring paths for the gods with honey; let him enjoy the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Narāśaṃsa, whose weapon is manly, the leader of men.

May he who possesses cattle be rich in fatness; may he who possesses heroes be powerful; may he who possesses chariots be the first to arrive; may he who possesses gold be radiant. Let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Agni. Praised with the *iḍā*-invocation, may the god, the messenger, the bearer of oblations, the unerring one, bring the gods hither. May he favor this sacrifice and this divine invocation of the gods. Let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). Well-spread and soft as wool, may it expand wide and far in this sacrifice, providing a comfortable seat for the gods.
May the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas sit upon this seat today; may it be dear to Indra; let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

{3.6.2.2} Let the Hotṛ worship the lofty, hollowed doors that do not hold back the waters; let them open upward with their frames and lean apart with their panels. Easy of access at this sacrifice, let them, the increasers of *ṛta*, lean apart; let them partake of the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Dawn and Night, the two great and well-adorned ones, who prepare a womb for men as wives; smiling together with Indra and the gods, let them sit upon this sacred grass (*barhis*) and enjoy the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ worship the two divine Hotṛs, the delightful ones, the two Potṛs, the sages, the wise ones. May one of them today perform the well-offered sacrifice with food, and may the other, with strength and great power, perform it with approval. May these two place this sacrifice among the gods in heaven; let them partake of the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, worship!

{3.6.2.3} Let the Hotṛ worship the three goddesses, the most skillful of workers; may they today extend this flawless work. O Hotṛ, let the goddesses go toward the divine waters; sacrifice for the clarified butter. Let the Hotṛ worship Tvaṣṭṛ, the most brilliant, the one who does not turn away, the bestower of seed, the far-famed, the bestower of glory, the multiform, who does not weary those who desire him. May he be well-nourished with nourishments, and rich in heroes through his heroes. Let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice.

Let the Hotṛ worship Vanaspati; for he has released his prayers. May the men, seeking to please him, perform the service. May the axe prepare [the wood] at the proper time today, as the god who carries the oblations to the gods. Let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Agni: Svāhā to the clarified butter, Svāhā to the fat, Svāhā to the drops, Svāhā to the consecrated offerings, Svāhā to the hymns of praise for the oblation! Svāhā to the gods who drink the clarified butter, Svāhā to Agni from the Hotṛ-offering! May they, being pleased, enjoy the clarified butter, O Agni! O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Kindled today in the dwelling of man, O Jātavedas, you, a god, worship the gods. Bring them hither, O you who are rich in friends and full of wisdom; for you are the messenger, the seer, and the perceptive one. O Tanūnapāt, anointing the paths that lead along the way of Truth with honey, make them sweet, O fair-tongued one! Accomplishing our prayers through our thoughts and the sacrifice, perform our ritual for the gods. We shall praise the greatness of Narāśaṃsa, the worshipful one, with these sacrifices.

{3.6.3.2} May those gods of pure intent, the purifiers who sustain the prayer, relish both kinds of oblations. Being invoked, worthy of praise, and worthy of worship, come, O Agni, in harmony with the Vasus! You are the youthful Hotṛ of the gods; as such, being impelled, sacrifice for them, you who are most skilled in sacrifice. The sacred grass is strewn eastward according to the direction of the earth; at the break of this day, it is gathered at the beginning of the days. It spreads itself out further and wider, a pleasant seat for the gods and for Aditi.

Let the spacious ones open wide, like wives adorning themselves for their husbands. O divine, lofty, all-impelling doors, become easy of access for the gods. Let the two holy ones, Dawn and Night, who bring forth abundance, sit down together in their place, near at hand. The two celestial maidens, lofty and adorned with bright ornaments, bestowing splendor and radiant beauty. Let the two divine Hotṛ-priests, the first and eloquent, fashioning the sacrifice for man to worship.

{3.6.3.4} Impelling [the singers] at the assemblies, the two poets pointing toward the ancient light with their direction; let Bhāratī come quickly to our sacrifice, and Iḍā, manifesting here like Manu. Let the three goddesses—Sarasvatī and the others—skilled in their work, sit upon this pleasant sacrificial grass. He who, as the progenitor, adorned these two, Heaven and Earth, and all beings with their forms—O Hotṛ, being impelled today, do you, the more skilled sacrificer, worship that god Tvaṣṭṛ here, you who are wise.

He has released [the victim] by himself, anointing it, for the path of the gods, the oblations according to the seasons. Vanaspati is the immolator, Agni is the god; let them sweeten the offering with honey and ghee. As soon as he was born, he measured out the sacrifice; Agni became the leader of the gods. At the command of this Hotṛ, in the speech of Truth (ṛta), let the gods eat the oblation consecrated with Svāhā!

Anuvāka 4 {3.6.4.1} Agni, our Hotṛ at the sacrifice, being a prize-winning steed, is led around—the god worthy of worship among the gods. Three times Agni goes around the sacrifice like a charioteer, bestowing refreshment upon the gods. Agni, the sage and lord of the prize, has stepped around the oblations—he has stepped toward the oblations—bestowing jewels upon the donor.

Agni has conquered; he has won the prize. As a god, he carries the oblations to the gods. Being urged forward by the *prāñjas* and being prepared with the *dhenās*, extending the life of the sacrifice—O Hotṛ, give the command for the offerings to the gods!

O divine immolators and you who are human, take hold! Lead him toward the sacrificial doors. Desiring the sacrifice for the two lords of the sacrifice, bring the fire forward for him; spread the sacrificial grass. Let his mother give her consent, let his father give his consent, let his brother from the same womb give his consent, and let his friend from the same herd give his consent. Place his feet toward the north.

Let him lead the eye to the sun; let him release the breath after the wind; the quarters of space his hearing; the intermediate region his life-breath; the earth his body. Let him flay off his skin in one piece; let him extract the omentum from above the navel before it is torn; let him keep the internal heat within; let him make his breast like a falcon’s; let him fashion his arms with the carving-knife.

The two shoulder-blades are the shoulders; the two collarbones are like Kaśyapa’s; the two hips are without flaw; the two thighs are hollow; the two knee-caps are like the leaves of a ladle. There are twenty-six ribs in him; pull them out one by one. Make every limb of his complete. Dig a pit for the earth to hide the undigested food (the *ūvadhyagūha*). Unite the *rakṣas* with the blood. Do not crack its rectum.

{3.6.6.4} Thinking [the victim] to be a fox—do not cry out against us regarding our children or descendants! O slaughterers, let the one who cries out be silent! O Adhrigu, perform the sacrifice well! Perform it as a good sacrifice! Perform the sacrifice, O Adhrigu! Both the Adhrigu and the Apāpa are the two slaughterers of the gods; may those two, being wise, cook this animal victim, in whatever manner its cooking is required.

Accept this most expansive word, most delightful to the gods, as you offer the oblations into your mouth. Place this sacrifice of ours among the immortals; accept these oblations, O Jātavedas. O Agni, accept the drops of fat and ghee; O Hotṛ, sit down first and partake. O Purifier, for thee there are the ghee-rich drops; the drops of fat drip down according to thy own law for the feast of the gods.

Bestow upon us the most excellent treasure. For you, O Agni, the wise and truthful one, drip the drops of ghee. You are kindled as the best of seers; be the protector of the sacrifice. For you, O irresistible and powerful Agni, drip the drops of fat and ghee. Praised by the sages, you have come with great radiance; accept our offerings, O wise one. The strongest fat has been extracted from the midst for you; we present it to you. O Vasu, the drops drip upon your skin; partake of them, O God, according to their respective shares.

Anuvāka 8 {3.6.8.1} O you two slayers of Vṛtra, come hither with your Vṛtra-slaying powers, O Indra, and with our prostrations, O Agni! May you two, Indra and Agni, be with us with your ungrudging gifts that are most excellent. Let the Hotṛ worship Indra and Agni. May they enjoy the fatness of the goat’s omentum and the oblation. Hotṛ, sacrifice! For with their mind they have looked out, seeking what is better—Indra and Agni, [seeking] kinsmen or even brothers.

{3.6.8.2} No other youthful wisdom exists for me; I have fashioned this hymn for you two that seeks the prize. Let the Hotṛ worship Indra and Agni; may they enjoy the oblation of the sacrificial cake. O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Men, possessing oblations, ever invoke you, the swift one, for the office of messenger. O Agni, upon whose sacred grass you sit with the gods—may his days be auspicious. Let the Hotṛ worship Agni; may he enjoy the oblation of the sacrificial cake. O Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Seeking wisdom through his hymns, the inspired singer implores for glorious wealth that brings precedence. O Indra and Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, wielders of the fair thunderbolt, further us with new gifts. Praying, "May we not sever the cords," and following the powers of the Fathers, the vigorous ones rejoice in Indra and Agni; for those two are the stones in the lap of the Dhiṣaṇā. Praising Agni, the beautiful-shining and fair-to-behold—
We pay homage to you, O Jātavedas, who are worthy of praise; the gods have made you their messenger, their steward, and the bearer of oblations—the navel of immortality.

Anuvāka 10 {3.6.10.1} For you, O Agni, were the first inventor of this prayer, the wondrous invoker. You, O bull, made it invincible; you brought forth conquering power to overcome all that must be overcome. Then you sat down as the most excellent sacrificer at the place of the *iḍā*-offering, seeking to nourish, worthy of praise as you are. Toward you, the first one, men seeking the gods and longing for great wealth have followed in pursuit. As you went with many riches like a chosen host, they, remaining ever-watchful, followed after you for wealth.

The brilliant, visible, and vast Agni, possessed of fatness and shining forever—we approach his station with homage, seeking glory; we have attained unimpaired glory. They have even assumed names worthy of sacrifice; they rejoice in your auspicious appearance. The peoples on earth increase you; you belong to the wealth of both kinds of people. You have become the renowned savior in our crossing, the father and the mother of mortals forever.

He is to be honored; he, the radiant Agni, is to be revered among the people. As the beloved, joyous invoker, he has sat down as the most excellent sacrificer. To you, who shine within our home, we would sit with reverence, bowing our knees. To you, O Agni, we of pure intellect, seeking favor and longing for the gods, approach as your new [worshipers]. You, O Agni, have led the clans, shining with the great light of heaven. You are the sage of the eternal clans, the lord of the people, the subduer, the bull of men.

{3.6.10.4} To Agni, the purifier, who seeks out the deceased and impels them forward; to him who rules as the worshipful lord of riches—to that Agni, the mortal has sacrificed and labored, he who has reached you with fuel and the offering of oblations. He who understands the oblation with prostrations, being protected by you, gains all desirable things. For him, O great one, let us perform great service for you with prostrations, O Agni, with fuel, and with offerings; on the altar, O Son of Strength, with songs and hymns. May we strive to abide in your auspicious favor.

{3.6.10.5} O Agni, you who have extended across the two worlds with your radiance, and with your glories, you are the seeker of renown, the deliverer; shine forth far and wide for us with great, enduring, and wealthy spoils. O Vasu, grant us evermore the strength of men; grant abundant cattle for our children and descendants. May there be ample, vast, and high nourishments, and may misfortunes be driven far away. May auspicious glories of renown belong to us. O King Agni, through my devotion to you, may I obtain many treasures in manifold ways, for by your very nature you are the possessor of wealth. For indeed, O Agni, many riches are found within you, the king who bestows wealth upon the one who serves you.

Bring it, bestow it, O you whose arms wield the thunderbolt! O Indra and Agni, protect us with your powers! These indeed are the rays of the sun, by which our fathers went to the company of the gods. Let the Hotṛ priest worship Indra and Agni; let them partake today of the goat-oblation, of the fat extracted from the midst, before the onset of hatreds, before the seizure of men. Let them now devour it!

{3.6.11.2} From the fodder of the pastures, from the first-fruits of the grass, from those that flow with abundance, from the hundredfold Rudra-offerings, from the Agniṣvātta-fires, from those clothed in fatness—from the ribs, from the haunches, from the shoulders, from the marrow, from every single limb, from those portions cut out—may Indra and Agni indeed prepare them; may they enjoy the oblation. O Hotṛ, sacrifice! O Vanaspati, for the gods are the oblations; O golden-leaved one, your purpose is from of old.

Moving clockwise, having fastened it with a girdle, carry [the offering] along the straightest paths of *ṛta*. Let the Hotṛ worship Vanaspati, for he has been bound with a most finely ground and strongest girdle. [Carry him] to where are the dear abodes of the goat-offering for Indra and Agni; where are the dear paths of Vanaspati; where are the dear abodes of the gods who drink the clarified butter (*ājyapāḥ*); and where are the dear abodes of Agni the Hotṛ.

Having introduced this [deity] there, as it were, having praised him, as it were, he shall offer [the oblation]. Making him, as it were, most eager: "May the divine Vanaspati thus grant [it]; may he enjoy the offering. O Hotṛ, sacrifice! O youngest one, satisfy the desiring gods. Knowing the seasons, O Lord of Seasons, sacrifice here. With those who are the divine officiating priests, O Agni—you among the Hotṛs are the most skilled at sacrificing. Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt. Agni has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Indra and Agni regarding the offering of the goat; he has sacrificed to the dear paths of Vanaspati."

He has sacrificed to the beloved abodes of the gods who drink the clarified butter. May he sacrifice to the beloved abodes of Agni the Hotṛ; may he sacrifice to his own greatness. May they perform the sacrifices and the offerings. May Jātavedas make these rites successful. May he enjoy the oblation. Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Anuvāka 12 {3.6.12.1} When the prize-winning ones have come to the assembly, the inspired singers seeking favor with their songs—like racing steeds reaching the goal—those men call aloud upon Indra and Agni. O Lord of the Forest, having bound [the victim] with a cord, you who know the sacred ways, carry the most finely ground oblations to the gods; and proclaim the giver among the immortals. Agni Sviṣṭakṛt has offered the dear abodes of the goat-oblation for Indra and Agni.

He has sacrificed to the beloved dwellings of Vanaspati; he has sacrificed to the beloved abodes of the gods who drink the clarified butter. May he sacrifice to the beloved abodes of Agni, the Hotṛ; may he sacrifice to his own majesty. May they offer the desirable nourishments; may Jātavedas perform these rites. May he enjoy the oblation. O Agni, Hotṛ of the people’s rite, O you of purifying luster, you indeed are the sacrificer; you shall sacrifice according to the Truth when you have expanded in greatness. Carry the offerings that are yours today, O youngest one.

May the divine sacrificial grass (*barhis*), well-favored by the gods, be accompanied by the gods; may it be rich in heroes through the heroes. May it be strewn at dawn and gathered at nightfall; may it surpass others in wealth. May we rejoice, possessing the sacrificial grass, in the winning of wealth and the granting of treasures. Perform the sacrifice! O divine doors, you who are joined together, all-knowing in your movement, unshakable and firm at the invocation of the gods—may a young calf measure its way toward them, or a newborn boy; may a swift horse or a dust-raising steed fill them. May they open wide for the winning of wealth and the granting of treasures. Perform the sacrifice!

The two goddesses, Dawn and Night, have been invoked today as this sacrifice proceeds; may they now surely come, along with the divine hosts, well-pleased and well-disposed, to partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of the winner of wealth—sacrifice!

The two divine ones who take pleasure, the bestowers of wealth, of whom one drives away evil hatreds and the other brings desirable riches to the sacrificer—may they both enjoy the offering at the distribution of wealth; sacrifice! The two divine ones, the offerings of strength (*ūrjāhuti*), may one bring food and strength, and the other bring shared eating and drinking. May we be favored by the new through the old, and by the old through the new. Those two offerings of strength, increasing our vigor, have bestowed that strength upon us. May they both enjoy the offering at the distribution of wealth; sacrifice!

The divine ones, the two divine *hotṛ*s, the *neṣṭṛ*, the *potṛ*, the destroyers of the evil-speaker, the bringers of wealth—enjoy the offering at the winning of wealth, for the bestowal of wealth; sacrifice! The three goddesses—the three goddesses *iḍā*, *sarasvatī*, and *bhāratī*—*bhāratī* has touched the sky with the Ādityas; *sarasvatī* has protected this sacrifice here with the Rudras. May we rejoice here in the shared feast with *iḍā* who is rich in wealth, at the winning of wealth, for the bestowal of wealth; may they partake; sacrifice!

The god Narāśaṃsa has three heads and six eyes; a hundred speckled-backed ones support him, and a thousand carry him forward. Mitra and Varuṇa are worthy of his office of Hotṛ, Bṛhaspati of his Stotra, and the Aśvins of his Adhvaryu-work. May he partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of winning wealth: sacrifice! The god Vanaspati, the rain-protector, clothed in clarity, has touched the sky with his top, filled the mid-air with his middle, and made firm the earth with his base. May he partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of winning wealth: sacrifice!

The divine *barhis* of the water-bringers has been placed; it is established as the unshakable foundation for those who have fallen away, the sustainer of all desires, much-longed-for, glorious. With this *barhis*, may we surpass all other *barhis*. For the winning of wealth, let him enjoy the gift of treasure. Sacrifice!

Agni, the divine Sviṣṭakṛt, the possessor of excellent wealth, the delightful sage, whose thoughts are true—the invoker, more skilled at sacrifice than any invoker—O Agni, those gods whom you have sacrificed to and whom you have gladdened, who have rejoiced in your office as invoker: for them, having shared in the sacrificial food, send this sacrifice, which goes to the gods, to heaven among the gods. And you, O Agni, being the Sviṣṭakṛt and the invoker, have become the one for the winning of wealth; in the utterance of homage, partake of the gift of wealth and sacrifice!

Anuvāka 14 {3.6.14.1} May the divine *barhis* (sacrificial grass) partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of bestowing wealth. May the divine doors partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of bestowing wealth. May the two divine goddesses, Dawn and Night, partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of bestowing wealth. May the two divine goddesses, the Delighters (*joṣṭrī*), partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of bestowing wealth. May the two divine goddesses, the Offerings of Strength (*ūrjāhuti*), partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of bestowing wealth.

The divine ones, the two divine Hotṛ-priests: let them partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of attaining wealth. The goddesses, the three goddesses: let them partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of attaining wealth. The god Narāśaṃsa: let him partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of attaining wealth. The god Vanaspati: let him partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of attaining wealth. The god Barhis of the waters: let it partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of attaining wealth.

Agni, the god who makes the sacrifice well-offered; the giver of good wealth, the delightful sage; the one whose thoughts are true, the sacrificing Hotṛ-priest—more skilled at sacrificing than every other Hotṛ. O Agni, those gods whom you have sacrificed to, those whom you have gratified, those who have rejoiced in your office as Hotṛ—to them, along with this sacrificial gift that has been won and goes to the gods, send this sacrifice to heaven among the gods. And you, O Agni, having become the Hotṛ who makes the sacrifice well-offered, partake in the invocation of homage for the granting of wealth and the bestowing of treasures.

Anuvāka 15 {3.6.15.1} Today this sacrificer has chosen Agni as the Hotṛ; cooking the cooked offerings, cooking the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*), and binding the goat for Indra and Agni. Today the divine Vanaspati has become well-established; with the goat for Indra and Agni, they have offered it from below; they have taken hold of it from the fat; they have increased it with the sacrificial cake. Today you, O seer, descendant of seers, grandson of seers, this sacrificer has chosen you from among many who have assembled; "This is my wealth among the gods."

"Water shall be poured out. Those divine gifts which the gods have bestowed, declare them to him, and pronounce the *guru* formula. O Hotṛ, being impelled for the auspicious recitation, you, the human one, being sent forth for the *sūktavāka*, speak the hymns.

Prapāṭhaka 7, Anuvāka 1 He who, having added fuel to the fires, undertakes the vow, causes all desires to enter into the fire. If he were to depart without having performed the sacrifice, his desires, not being gratified, would not follow him; he would be without splendor and without vigor. He should therefore offer an oblation with the verse: "To thee, O best of Aṅgiras, all well-settled dwellings have separately submitted for the sake of desire, O Agni.
Thus he places desires within himself.

Desires that are gratified follow after him; he becomes radiant and full of vigor. This is indeed the continuity of the sacrifice: when one who has added fuel to the fires enters upon the vow, if the fire goes out, that is a severance for him. Having drawn it out toward the east, he should worship it with his mind. Mind is Prajāpati, and the sacrifice belongs to Prajāpati.

{3.7.1.3} He continues the sacrifice by means of the mind alone. "Bhūḥ! he says. Prajāpati is indeed *bhūta* (existent/being). Verily, he attains prosperity (*bhūti*). He is indeed deprived of power and vigor whose consecrated fire (*āhitāgni*) goes out. As far as one could strike with a wooden pin (*śamyā*), for that distance the fire should go out; if it should go out for that duration, he should collect it again: "This is one [fire] for thee, and yonder is another."

"Enter with the third light; be pleasant for the body as you enter; in the dear, supreme birthplace of the gods. With this, he gathers it together by means of the *brahman*. That indeed is the atonement (*prāyaścitti*) for that. If it should go away further, he should follow after it and settle there; that indeed is the atonement for that. Indeed, the plants enter the milk of the cattle of one whose calves, having been driven away for the sake of the oblation, suckle [their mothers].

If he were to milk them, he would sacrifice with an exhausted oblation; if he were not to milk them, he would omit a limb of the sacrifice. He should offer a barley gruel to Vāyu. Vāyu is indeed the one who causes the milk to flow; he himself causes the milk to flow for him. Plants are indeed milk; milk is milk. By means of milk, he secures milk for himself.

{3.7.1.6} Now, one should drive away the calves for the subsequent oblation; that itself is the expiation for this. Indeed, he deprives one set of gods of their share—those who come to the house of the sacrificer in the evening—for him whose evening-milked oblation meets with misfortune. Having set aside rice for Indra, he should fast. For plants are milk; thus, having begun with and taken hold of milk, he fasts. Whatever [milk] there may be in the morning, he should have it boiled.

{3.7.1.7} Now, the other cake should be dedicated to Indra; thus he bestows upon him the two powers of sense together. Plants are indeed milk; milk is milk. By means of milk, he secures milk for him. Then he should drive away the calves for the subsequent oblation; that itself is the atonement for it. Indeed, he deprives both classes of gods of their share—those who come to the house of the sacrificer in the evening and those who come in the morning—for him whose two oblations both meet with ruin.

{3.7.1.8} He should offer a five-platter oblation of cooked rice to Indra. He should sacrifice to Agni first among the deities; thus he gratifies the deities with Agni as their mouth. For other deities follow after Agni, while others follow after Indra; he thus gratifies both these classes. Plants are indeed milk; milk is milk. By means of milk, he secures milk for him. Then he should drive away the calves for the subsequent oblation.

{3.7.1.9} That itself is the expiation for this: a half of this sacrifice is indeed lost for him whose wife becomes menstruating on the day of the vow. Having excluded her, he should perform the sacrifice; thus he performs the sacrifice with the sacrifice in its entirety. After having sacrificed, he should address her: "I am that man; you are she. I am heaven; you are earth. I am the Sāman; you are the Ṛc. Come, let us two unite; let us together deposit seed, so that we may obtain a male son."
"For the increase of wealth, for good offspring, and for heroic vigor"—with these words, he indeed invokes her back; that itself is the expiation for that.

If one were to offer with [the ladle] turned upside down, the sacrificer would be without offspring and without cattle. If he were to pour it out where there is no proper place, he would be without a proper place. He should pour it out into an anthill with a verse addressed to Prajāpati. For the anthill belongs to Prajāpati, and Prajāpati is the sacrifice. Thus, he establishes the sacrifice in Prajāpati himself. "Bhūḥ! he says; for Prajāpati is indeed *bhūta* (existent).

{3.7.2.2} He attains prosperity itself by performing that [rite]. Having done that, he should milk another cow and offer again; that indeed is the expiation for it. If he were to offer with [milk] into which an insect has fallen, the sacrificer would become childless and cattleless. If he were to pour it out where there is no proper place, he would be without a foundation. He should pour it out within the enclosing sticks with the middle leaf, using a verse addressed to Heaven and Earth; thus he establishes it in Heaven and Earth.

Having done that, one should milk another [cow] and offer again; that itself is the expiation for it. If he were to offer with rain falling, a deformity would arise in his body—he might become leprous or afflicted with hemorrhoids. If he were to go back [to the offering place], he would interrupt the sacrifice. He should offer: "Mitra, knowing, ordains people."

“Mitra has supported the earth and the sky; Mitra gazes upon the people with unblinking eyes. Offer the oblation, rich in ghee, to the True One!”—with this [verse], he makes it right through Mitra himself. Having done that, one must milk another cow and offer again; that indeed is the atonement for that. If, after the first oblation has been offered, the subsequent oblation should spill, the sacrificer would be deprived of two-footed animals. If he were to offer it again with the subsequent [verse], [the same fault would occur].

{3.7.2.5} The sacrificer may be deprived of his four-footed livestock. Having placed a fuel-stick with the verse addressed to the Lord of the Forest: "O Lord of the Forest, where you know the secret names of the gods, there bring the oblations," he should then offer another oblation silently. By means of the Lord of the Forest, he has indeed sustained both the afflicted and the unafflicted oblations of the sacrifice. Having done that, one should milk another cow and offer again; that itself is the expiation for that.
If a coal should fly out before the fore-offerings (prayājas), it would bring misfortune to both the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer.

If [he were to offer] toward the south, it would be sufficient for the Brahman priest and the sacrificer. If toward the west, it would be sufficient for the Hotṛ priest, the wife, and the sacrificer. If toward the north, it would be sufficient for the Āgnīdhra priest, the sacrificial animals, and the sacrificer. If he were to offer directly [toward the fire], Rudra might become a slayer of his cattle. If he were not to offer directly, the oblation would be cast forth unappeased.

{3.7.2.7} He should place [the vessel] down with the base of the *sruva* ladle, saying: "Let not darkness, let not the sacrifice, let not the sacrificer perish! Homage be to you as you come; homage, O Rudra, as you go away; homage where you sit down! Do not harm so-and-so; do not harm so-and-so! With whatever [liquid] it might spill, he should strike that [spot], saying: "The thousand-horned bull, Jātavedas, whose back is the *stoma*, who is rich in ghee and fair of count—do not abandon us, nor may we abandon you."

"Grant us prosperity through cattle and prosperity through heroes"—with these words he strikes it with the *brahman*. This indeed is the expiation for that. Anuvāka 3 {3.7.3.1}: He who, having established the sacred fires, finds his fire not produced when being churned, is deprived of power and vigor. Wherever he may see another [fire], he should fetch it from there and offer the oblation; thus his *agnihotra* becomes offered in the fire itself. If he cannot find another [fire], he should offer it in a she-goat; for the she-goat belongs to Agni. Thus his *agnihotra* becomes offered in the fire itself.

{3.7.3.2} One should not eat the goat. If one were to eat the goat, one would be eating that very oblation which one offers into the fire. Therefore, the goat is not to be eaten. If one should not find a goat, the offering should be made into the right hand of a Brāhmaṇa. For the Brāhmaṇa is indeed Agni Vaiśvānara; thus his Agnihotra becomes offered into the fire itself.

{3.7.3.3} One should not exclude a Brāhmaṇa from lodging. If one were to exclude a Brāhmaṇa from lodging, one would deprive that very fire into which one offers the oblation of its rightful portion. Therefore, a Brāhmaṇa must not be excluded from lodging. If one cannot find a Brāhmaṇa, the offering should be made into a clump of Darbha grass. A clump of Darbha grass is indeed possessed of fire; thus, his Agnihotra becomes offered into the fire itself. However, one must not sit upon the Darbha grass.

{3.7.3.4} If one were to sit upon *darbha* grass, he would be sitting upon whatever oblation he offers in the fire. Therefore, *darbha* grass must not be sat upon. If he should not find *darbha* grass, he should offer the oblation in water; for water is indeed all the deities. Thus his *agnihotra* becomes offered in the deities themselves. However, he should not despise the water; for if he were to despise the water...

Whatever oblation one might offer in the waters, that one should avoid; therefore, the waters are not to be avoided. For him whose consecrated fires are mixed with other fires, both his pure and impure bodies become intermingled. He should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Vivici; thus he separates his pure body from his impure body. He should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Vratapati.
He approaches Agni Vratapati with his own share; he alone causes him to undertake the vow.

"He has made the leaking embryo free from disease—Agni, Indra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Bṛhaspati; they have poured this down upon the earth; it reaches the navel and Nirṛti is cast far away. The *agnihotra* is indeed the potent seed of the one who has established the sacred fires. If that [milk] should leak, his potent seed would leak. By saying, "He has made the leaking embryo free from disease," he places the potent seed back into him.

"Agni," he says. Agni is indeed the depositor of seed; thus he deposits seed. "Indra," he says; he thereby bestows power upon him. "Tvaṣṭṛ," he says. Tvaṣṭṛ is indeed the fashioner of the forms of paired animals; he thereby bestows form upon the animals. "Bṛhaspati," he says. Bṛhaspati is indeed the sacred power (*brahman*) of the gods; by means of the sacred power, he causes offspring to be born for him. "Upon the earth, he has poured down this," he says.

He establishes this very [sacrifice] in this [earth]; he does not reach the navel; "May Nirṛti go away," he says, for the smiting away of the Rākṣasas. Anuvāka 4 {3.7.4.1}: Those [streams] which flow from the front, those from above, and those from all sides—with those [waters] purified by rays, I commence faith and the sacrifice. O gods who know the way, find the way for the sacrifice! By the divine Lord of the Mind, let the sacrifice be set in motion. From the third heaven, Soma has been brought down by means of the Gāyatrī.

{3.7.4.2} To prepare for the drinking of Soma, he takes the inner bark: "O divine waters, you are pure; purify these vessels for the gods' Upātaṅkya rite. Purify also the *parṇa*-bark! May there be milk in the houses, milk in the cows, and milk in the calves; O [Soma], be held firm as an oblation for Indra. By means of the *gāyatrī* verse and the *parṇa*-bark, may it turn this milk into Soma."

I seize Agni, the good chariot, who is the source of bliss; he who ascends the rising sun for the sake of the day, the Āditya, the highest light among lights. May he rest for the sacrifice tomorrow for the sake of the deities—the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas—those deities together with Indra. I first enclose them within my own abode through my wisdom. Those gods who have entered this fifteenth nourishment, those I first enclose.

{3.7.4.4} May Agni, the bearer of oblations, bring them here. This full-moon offering belongs to them; it is within me. This new-moon offering belongs to them; it is within me. Between the two fires are the cattle; they have come to the assembly of the gods. Those I first enclose within my own dwelling with my mind. Here let offspring of every form rejoice, dwelling together around Agni the lord of the house. Those I first enclose.

{3.7.4.5} In their own dwelling, through our inspired thought, may cattle of every form take delight here, dwelling together around Agni, the lord of the household; them I first enclose in their own dwelling through inspired thought. This is the fire of the ancestors; it has carried the oblations to the ancestors; him I first enclose. May he make our food free from poison; you, O guardians of the assembly, [serve] the eternal one.

{3.7.4.6} May they kindle the portion of victory! O Agni of the assembly hall, may you shine for me for a hundred autumns, for the sake of conquest! May I bring food fit for the dwelling for a hundred autumns! May Ahibudhnya bestow upon the dwelling glory and sacred power! Here, I announce this sacrifice to the Vasus, of whom Agni is the eldest; here, I announce it to those of whom Indra is the eldest.

{3.7.4.7} I proclaim the sacrifice to the Rudras; this, I declare, to those who have Varuṇa as their eldest. I proclaim the sacrifice to the Ādityas. The plants are full of milk; the milk of the creepers is full of milk. That which is the milk of the milk of the waters—with that, O Indra, unite me. O Agni, Lord of Vows, I shall perform the vow; may I be able to do it, may it be successful for me. O Vāyu, Lord of Vows; O Āditya, Lord of Vows.

{3.7.4.8} O Lord of Vows, I shall observe the vow of vows. May I be able to do it; may it be successful for me. This [branch], directed eastward and northward, prepared as nourishment and vigor—abounding in leaves and with unfaded tips—I bring forth as the protector of cattle. Since you, having assumed a black form, entered the lords of the forest, therefore I gather you together in twenty-one parts, well-prepared.

The three enclosing sticks, the three fuel-sticks, those that move along with the life of the sacrifice, the fire-cleanser, the stirring-spoon, and the fire-tongs—I gather these well-prepared. Of those plants that were born for the gods in the three ages of old, may I attain their joint as I bring the sacrificial strew. May the water, pure and fit for sacrifice, be divine and auspicious to me.

May I, who cut [the grass] for you, not come to harm; may I live for a hundred autumns. Of the immeasurable, these are measured. I gird myself for the sake of good deeds. May I not fall into any sin whatsoever. Rising again, may they become abundant. The sacrificial grass, once-cut, soft as wool—pleasant for the ancestors, I bring you here. May my ancestors, worthy of Soma, sit upon this: my grandfathers and great-grandfathers, together with their followers.

{3.7.4.11} Made of triple-stranded *palāśa* and *darbha* grass, this much in length, measured by a span (*prādeśa*), it is the most excellent purifier in the sacrifice. May it make my milk an offering. {F These two} {ānandā. These two} {BI These} {These two}, the out-breath and the in-breath, moving about while nourishing all the limbs of the sacrifice, are the two purifiers that cleanse the oblation. You two are the purifiers belonging to Viṣṇu; may Vāyu purify you both with his mind.

{3.7.4.12} This out-breath and this in-breath—let them both go unto the sacrificer. For in the sacrifice they were the two *potṛ* priests, the purifiers who cleanse the oblations. Through you, they found the altar and the earth; through you, the sacrifice is born, providing all gifts. As a knower, you seek out the flawless sacrifice; through you, the *hotṛ* priest extends the half-months. You are the thirty-third of the threads; come together with the filter.

O Śiva, this is the rope, the cord; may it serve the inviolable cow so that the sacrifice does not slip away. I place the two *ukhā* pots; may they support what has been brought together with the cattle—the boiled milk and curd for Indra. You are the *upaveṣa*; they have held you as a serving vessel while preparing the oblation for Indra. Be auspicious and helpful to us.

{3.7.4.14} This non-earth vessel is a divine cup; let it be employed for the longevity of the sacrifice. Having been led across the filter, may the waters not flow over. Purified by the god Savitṛ with the rays of the bright sun, O rope, purify the cow and all the vessels for milking. These cows come hither, yielding honey, prolific, glorious, and multiform.

Becoming many as they are born here, may Indra cause you, O cows, to delight in this place. You are Pūṣan’s [cows]. Free from disease, I unite you with offspring; becoming abundant through the increase of wealth, swelling with strength, milk, and ghee—may I, living, sit among you who are living. May Heaven and Earth together yield this sacrifice; may Dhātṛ along with Soma, and Vāyu with Vāta, bestow wealth upon the sacrificer.

They milk the fountain, the four-holed jar—the divine *iḍā*, honey-sweet and winner of the light. O Indra and Agni, quicken that which is full of truth; may it quicken [the sacrificer]. May that establish the sacrificer in immortality. Tell us what you have milked for us: the invigorating oblation for Indra. That in which the milk of the gods and of men is placed—may it yield much for Indra and for the gods; may the offering swell again.

For the calves, for men; may it be fit for milking again. You are the continuity of the sacrifice; I continue myself along with you, the continuity of the sacrifice. You are uninjured; for Viṣṇu, I place you for the sacrifice. With water, in a vessel not empty—those waters which lie purified around—having turned this milk into Soma, let it go back to its own source.

The bark of the *parṇa* tree is the purifier; it belongs to Soma, for it was fashioned from Soma. These two, the *parṇa* and the *darbha*, are the cleansers of the oblation for the gods. O Viṣṇu, for the morning service, you protect the oblation as its guardian. He spreads [the grass] over both fires: "May the deities dwell near me; I dwell near the domestic animals, for my sake as their protector. For the sake of the cattle-herd, [he seeks] the livestock.

Anuvāka 5 {3.7.5.1} O gods, exert your power among the gods! Let the first ones prevail over the second; let the second over the third. O you who are thrice eleven, protect me here! May I be able to accomplish this which I now do. Let the self act for the sake of the self. This I shall perform as a healing remedy. This is my universal medicine. O Aśvins, protect me both of you! This [I do] against the attacking army.

I wipe away the face. Shine forth with the light of the sun! For great sensory power! May he whose source is ghee swell; may Agni approve the oblations. Anoint the cavity; anoint the skin. You, of beautiful form, the finder of wealth—with the splendor of cattle, I sprinkle you, acceptable to Agni. I prepare for you a pleasant seat.

With a stream of clarified butter, I prepare a most gracious place. Sit upon it; take your stand in this immortal [place]. O essence of rice, be well-disposed! Moist, spreading, the guardian of the world—he, the cooked, emerges as the progenitor of thoughts. That self of yours which has entered into the cattle, which has extended through the station of the gods—having become possessed of self and endowed with clarity (*ghṛta*), go to the gods, O Soma; find the light of heaven for me, the sacrificer. May nourishment, prosperity, and the sap of the earth not depart from me.

The gods are the fathers, the fathers are the gods. Being who I am—{O Ānanda, being who I am}—as such I sacrifice. I do not pass between [the self] and him to whom I belong. My own is what is sacrificed; my own is what is given; my own is what is bestowed; my own is the toil; my own is the oblation. Of that mine, Agni is the witness, Vāyu is the listener, Āditya is the observer, and Dyaus is the father.

Earth is the mother; Prajāpati is the kinsman. Being who I am, I sacrifice. Do not fear, O Ānanda, do not tremble; may I not harm you. May your vital radiance (*tejas*) not depart. Lift up the offering; pour it out after [the fire]. I shall cut off portions for you from your own limbs. Homage be to you; do not harm me. If, while cutting off the portions for you, I have acted contrary to my own nature, [may that be forgiven].

{3.7.5.6} With clarified butter I anoint this back; may that part of yours swell again. Let there be no deficiency even by the measure of a barley grain. Let this [defect] be remedied from the wound. May we not cause injury to the sacrifice. This oblation is pure and well-offered. From the southern half, without breaking through, I cut off the single-faced portion, which was seen by Manu, whose foot is in ghee, and which was impelled by Mitra and Varuṇa.

O *iḍā*, enjoy our portion; quicken the cows, quicken the horses. May we be partakers of thee, with all our selves and all our groups. O radiant one (*bradhna*), swell! Let there be no depletion for me who gives; let there be no failure for me who acts. Thou art the ordainer of the quarters; may the quarters be favorable to me; may the quarters be favorable to me.

{3.7.5.8} May the divine and the human [powers] be favorable to me! May day and night be favorable to me! May the half-months be favorable to me! May the months be favorable to me! May the seasons be favorable to me! May the year be favorable to me! You are the arrangement; may there be arrangement for me! To you, from the guardians of the quarters—to the four immortals! To these overseers of what has come into being!

{ 3.7.5.9 } May we worship with this oblation. Let the one who has a share receive his portion; let no one be left without a share. We exclude the one who has no share. Make the waters swell; quicken the plants. Protect the bipeds; favor the quadrupeds. Send down rain from heaven. This oblation belongs to the Brahmins.

{3.7.5.10} Of those who are worthy of Soma and drinkers of Soma, the non-Brahmin is excluded. There is no share here for the non-Brahmin. Let the sacrificial grass be anointed with the oblation and with ghee; let it be anointed with the Ādityas, with the Vasus, and with the Maruts; let it be anointed with Indra and with all the gods. May that which is offered with *svāhā* go to the celestial realm. May I be like Indrāṇī, not widowed; may I be like Aditi, possessed of good sons. O Gārhapatya fire, do not leave me alone.

{ 3.7.5.11} For the sake of sitting down together and for the possession of good offspring: may the wife be united with her husband through their good deed. May they become the two yoke-oxen harnessed to the sacrifice; being in harmony, may they cast away all enemies. May they grasp the unaging light in heaven. O Sacrifice, ten are your bodies worthy of worship; may the sacrificer gratify them with clarified butter. Praising the instruction of the two *nāriṣṭha* oblations, the sacrificer has become immortal within the divine assembly of the gods. You whom the gods have fashioned—

{3.7.5.12} O you two of a hundred powers, [this is] your portion of strength; with this I gratify you both. With this, may you two be satisfied, O destroyers of distress! I am in the world of the gods who perform good deeds; may this sacrifice of mine not be in vain. Knowing this, I, as one skilled, perform the *anuyāja* for the two *Nāriṣṭhas*, since Indra assigned them their share. O divine Soma, do not flow away; O Maruts, be gracious to us at this sacrifice. Let no overwhelming calamity or curse find us.

{3.7.5.13} May he not deliver us to hostile enclosures. We sacrifice to the Bull, the vigorous one, to the Full Moon. May it yield for us abundance of heroic strength and thousandfold increase of wealth. To the out-breath, the bountiful; to the Full Moon, *svāhā*! The New Moon is fortunate and most gracious, swelling again like a milch-cow. May she yield for us abundance of heroic strength and thousandfold increase of wealth. To the in-breath, the bountiful; to the New Moon, *svāhā*!

Strew the grass; enclose the altar. Do not harm your kin as they lie there. These golden, bright-colored [bricks] are the Hotṛ’s seats; these are the gold neck-ornaments for the sacrificer, O radiant one.

Anuvāka 6 {3.7.6.1} Strew around [the altar] and enclose the fire! May the enclosed fire benefit the sacrificer. The essence of the waters, the gold of the plants—may these be the golden neck-ornaments for the sacrificer, yielding all his desires, in that world, in yonder world. O Lord of the Earth, Lord of the World, Lord of the Great Being, we choose you as our Brahman priest. I am the Lord of the Earth, I am the Lord of the World, I am the Lord of the Great Being.

Impelled by the god Savitṛ, I shall perform the office of the officiating priest. O god Savitṛ, they choose you here as Bṛhaspati, the divine Brahman. That I announce to the mind; the mind to the Gāyatrī; the Gāyatrī to the Triṣṭubh; the Triṣṭubh to the Jagatī; the Jagatī to the Anuṣṭubh; the Anuṣṭubh to the Paṅkti; the Paṅkti to Prajāpati.

Prajāpati [gave it] to the Viśvedevas; the Viśvedevas to Bṛhaspati; Bṛhaspati to the Brahman; the Brahman is Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Suvaḥ. Bṛhaspati is the Brahman of the gods; I am [the Brahman] of men. O Bṛhaspati, protect the sacrifice! For him who among you, O gods, practices the life of a student (brahmacarya)—who is wise, contemplative in mind, and ascetic—for him I prepare this dwelling.

A messenger moves among human women; a young woman with four tufts of hair, beautifully adorned, her face anointed with ghee, in the midst of the world. Being cleansed for great good fortune, milk for me, for the sacrificer, all his desires. Having become the earth, she has nourished her greatness; from there, the goddess increases her milks. The holy ones go apart and come together for the sacrifice—the plants, the waters, and the powerful verses here. Whoever [offends] me with heart, with mind, or with speech...

{3.7.6.5} O Gods, whoever hates the sacred word (*brahman*) through his actions, whoever [hates it] through his learning or his longing heart—his head I sever with the thunderbolt, O Indra! Soft as wool, spreading out, pleasant, the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) beloved by the gods for their seat; place the sacrificer indeed in the world of heaven, upon the back of the firmament, in the highest sky! The young woman with four tufts, well-adorned, whose face is ghee, clothes herself in the sacred ordinances (*vayunāni*). Being strewn for great good fortune...

{3.7.6.6} May you milk desires for me, the sacrificer. Be auspicious and helpful to me; be pleasant and a good seat for me; be full of vigor and full of milk for me. Make me swell with food and vigor; make me swell with sacred power and splendor; make me swell with dominion and force; make me swell with the common people and prosperity; make me swell with long life and the eating of food; make me swell with offspring and cattle.

{3.7.6.7} In this sacrifice, let there be even more for me now. For the sake of non-disturbance, I set up the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*). Agni, the supporter, the sustainer, the most firm—may he drive away hostilities from here. With the two separating-spans (*vidhṛti*), I cut asunder my rivals, those *bhrātṛvya* enemies who have been born and those who are yet to be born. With the two restraining-straps (*yantra*) of the people, I scatter them away. O Gods, may I be the highest among my own kin. While the two restraining-straps of the people drive away the enemy, [they drive away] every evil, lack of understanding, and the short-lived.

{3.7.6.8} Sit down, O Goddess, in the world of the well-performed deed! You two are supports, you two are sustainers, you two are self-sustained. Sustain the vital breaths within me; sustain offspring within me; sustain cattle within me. This sacrificial grass-bundle (*prastara*) is the supporter of both; it is the supporter of the *prayāja* offerings as well as the *anūyāja* offerings. It has supported the kindling-sticks of every form; upon it I place the offering-spoons. Ascend the paths leading to the gods, O *juhū* ladle!

{3.7.6.9} Where the seers who were first-born in ancient times dwell—those with golden wings, swift, and of well-formed limbs—there carry me, where the worlds of the righteous are. With the *upabhṛt* ladle I drive away my rivals: the kinsmen already born and those yet to be born. May I milk the sacrifice like a cow that yields easily; may I be superior, and may my rivals be inferior. O Agni, whoever, difficult to overcome, would attack me with word, mind, or heart, acting with hostility—[him I strike down].

This mind of his is lower than the *dhruvā* [ladle]. May I be higher. May my rivals be lower. You are the bull, belonging to the *śakvarī* meters; you are the son of the *ghṛtācī* [milch-cows]. Sit upon the dear seat with your dear name. Sit comfortably for me, easy to sit upon, on the earth. Spread yourself wide with offspring and cattle in the world of heaven. Sit in the sky, on the earth, and in the intermediate space. May I be higher.

{3.7.6.11} May my rivals be beneath me! This vessel is full of clarified butter; it is a fountain with a hundred streams, its flow unbroken. By the divine protection of the Maruts, you are the sacrifice, resting on all sides. Let the past and the future rest upon me from every side! May there be a hundred blessings for me; may there be a thousand pleasant truths for me—abounding in nourishment and rich in cattle. You are Prajāpati, resting on all sides.

{ 3.7.6.12} Let the past and the future rest upon me from every side. May there be a hundred blessings for me; may there be a thousand pleasant truths for me. Rich in nourishment, rich in cattle—this is the immortal power of the senses. By this, the animals offered healing to Indra. Through that, O gods, protect me! May I win here food, vigor, glory, strength, and force. Let the cooked [oblation] rest within me. That which moved upon the earth has entered therein.

{3.7.6.13} That with which Prajāpati sprinkled strength upon Indra—this is that bright, honeyed, and powerful draught; that with which he strengthened Mahendra from above—may curd nourish me! This Veda discovered the earth, hidden in secret, in the depths and in caverns; may it find a world for the sacrificer; may the performer of many rites make the sacrifice flawless! This sacrifice, rich in oblations, has been established through the Ṛg, the Sāman, the Yajus, and the deities.

By this may we conquer the sun-filled worlds; may I attain the friendship of Indra and immortality. Whoever here desires what is less for us—for me, the sacrificer at this sacrifice—may Indra and Agni drive him away from these worlds. May I obtain offspring rich in heroes. O Agni, winner of booty! You who are about to run for booty, you who are about to win booty—the vigorous one, the winner of booty!

I cleanse [thee] for the winning of strength; [I cleanse] Agni, the eater of food, for the sake of food. Father Heaven is invited; may Father Heaven invite me. Agni from the Āgnīdhra [is invited] for long life, for luster, for living, and for merit. Mother Earth is invited; may Mother Earth invite me. Agni from the Āgnīdhra [is invited].

For life, for splendor, for living, for merit—may the mind, as light, enjoy the clarified butter; may it join together this severed sacrifice. May Bṛhaspati extend this for us; may all the gods rejoice here. O Agni, that which I cut away from you, or which I, moving about, have cast off—that offspring and its root, O gods, cut down low.

O Agni, whoever seeks to harm us—whether he be an equal or a stranger—let nothing of him remain, as if he were wood being consumed by fire. O Jātavedas, whoever hates me, and whomsoever I hate, and whoever hates me—burn them all together, O Agni. And those whom I hate and those who hate me—O Agni, winner of booty, [consume] thee as thou hast sped toward the booty.

{3.7.6.18} Him who has won the prize; the vigorous one, the winner of the prize. For the winning of the prize, I cleanse thee. Agni, the eater of food, for the sake of eating food. The altar, the sacrificial grass, the cooked oblation; the fuel, the enclosing sticks, the offering-ladles; the clarified butter, the sacrifice, the *ṛc*-verses, the *yajus*-formulas; the invitatory verses and the *vaṣaṭ*-calls. May my convergences bow together. When the binding of the fuel is offered.

A wedge from heaven is extended; it has risen up from the earth. With that thousand-jointed [wedge], we cause our enemy to burn. May he who hates me burn intensely. O Herb, may I not suffer the pain of burning. O Sacrifice, homage to you, O Sacrifice! Homage, and yet again homage to you, O Sacrifice! Be established for me with auspiciousness; be established for me with comfort.

{3.7.6.20} Stand firm for me with prosperity; stand firm for me with Brahman-splendor; stand firm in accordance with the success of the sacrifice. Homage to you, O sacrifice! Homage to you! Homage to you! Of the three [portions] being husked, whatever husk remains—that is the portion of the Rakṣases. May the waters carry that away from here.

{3.7.6.21} Whatever [has stuck] in the mortar, in the pestle, and in the winnowing basket; whatever has adhered to the grinding stone and in the potsherd—those drops and splashes I offer together. May the All-Gods (Viśve Devāḥ) enjoy this oblation. Those many drops that exist in the sacrifice, all those I offer well-sacrificed and well-poured into the fire. Rising today, O thou of sun-like luster, thou hast destroyed my rivals. Strike them down from heaven with thy lightning. As thou settest, cast them downward.

Rising today, grant us our share, as a father grants his portion to his sons. For you, O Sūrya, possess long life; grant that to us. Rising today, O Sun of friendly luster, ascending to the highest heaven, O Sūrya, destroy my heart-disease and my jaundice. We transfer my jaundice onto the parrots and onto the thrushes.

{3.7.6.23} Now, moreover, we deposit my yellowness in the *hāridrava* birds. This Āditya has risen up with all his power, bringing my enemy under my control; may I not fall under the power of my enemy. He who curses us when we do not curse, and he who curses us when we do curse—may both Dawn and Night sweep away all that evil from him. {3.7.6.24} Whatever rival, whatever adversary, or mortal seeks to harm us, O Gods, let him be like kindling wood being consumed by fire.

Let nothing remain as a remnant of him. Being released, fly away! An arrow sharpened by sacred prayer (*brahman*), go forth and enter the enemies! Let not one of them escape. Anuvāka 7 {3.7.7.1} Sakṣa, behold this! Vidhartṛ, behold this! Nāka, behold this! The most praiseworthy delight is the highest *ṛta*, which they call immortal. Sūrya, the most excellent, shines with his rays; he follows heaven and earth, the two whose sons are the gods. You are consecration (*dīkṣā*), the womb of austerity (*tapas*). You are austerity, the womb of sacred knowledge (*brahman*).

{3.7.7.2} You are the Brahman, the source of the Kṣatra; you are the Kṣatra, the source of the Cosmic Order (Ṛta). You are the Cosmic Order, O Earth! I take hold of it. With the mind, I take hold of faith; with austerity, I take hold of consecration—the sovereign lady of the entire world. May all desires of the sacrificer be fulfilled. We take hold of the wind, the breath of the mind; [we take hold of] Prajāpati, who is the guardian of the world. May he protect us from death and save us from distress.

{3.7.7.3} May we live long and reach old age. O Indra Śākvara, I take refuge in the Gāyatrī; I yoke that for you. O Indra Śākvara, I take refuge in the Triṣṭubh; I yoke that for you. O Indra Śākvara, I take refuge in the Jagatī; I yoke that for you. O Indra Śākvara, I take refuge in the Anuṣṭubh; I yoke that for you. O Indra Śākvara, I take refuge in the Paṅkti.

{3.7.7.4} I yoke that for you. I have ascended to consecration (*dīkṣā*), the consort of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*), with the *gāyatrī* metre and with the sacred word (*brahman*). Cosmic Order has been established in Truth; Truth has been established in Cosmic Order. Both Cosmic Order and Truth have come into being for me. I have become light; I have gone to the sun. I have gone to the heavenly world, to the back of the firmament, to the summit of the radiant realm. Earth is consecration.

{3.7.7.5} By that consecration with which Agni was consecrated—by that very consecration I consecrate you. The intermediate space is consecration; by that consecration Vāyu was consecrated—by that very consecration I consecrate you. Heaven is consecration; by that consecration Āditya was consecrated—by that very consecration [I consecrate you].

{3.7.7.6} By that consecration I consecrate you. The quarters are consecration; by that consecration the moon is consecrated. By that consecration by which the moon is consecrated, by that consecration I consecrate you. Water is consecration; by that consecration King Varuṇa is consecrated. By that consecration by which King Varuṇa is consecrated, by that consecration I consecrate you. Plants are consecration.

By that consecration King Soma was consecrated; by that same consecration by which King Soma was consecrated, I consecrate you. Speech is the consecration; by that consecration Prāṇa was consecrated; by that same consecration by which Prāṇa was consecrated, I consecrate you. May the earth consecrate you as you are being consecrated; may the intermediate space consecrate you as you are being consecrated; may the sky consecrate you as you are being consecrated.

{3.7.7.8} May the quarters consecrate you as you are being consecrated. May the waters consecrate you as you are being consecrated. May the plants consecrate you as you are being consecrated. May speech consecrate you as you are being consecrated. May the *ṛc*-verses consecrate you as you are being consecrated. May the *sāman*-chants consecrate you as you are being consecrated. May the *yajus*-formulas consecrate you as you are being consecrated. Day and night; plowing and rain; brilliance and honor.

The waters and the plants; strength and truth—may these consecrate you as you undergo consecration. Sit here in your own skill, O father of skill! In the favor of the gods, for great delight; settle yourself well in this comfortable seat with your body. Be like a father to your son, most gracious; as one auspicious, enter me auspiciously. Truth is my self; faith is my imperishability.

Austerity is my foundation. May the quarters, impelled by Savitṛ, consecrate me. I am truth. I am yours; you are mine; this [is our bond]. You are my womb; I am your womb. Being mine alone, O Agni, carry the oblations, you who create the world for your father, O Jātavedas. Being invoked, fair-faced in the east, O Agni, sit upon your own womb, the Sādhya seat, in this higher assembly-place.

O All-Gods and Sacrificer, sit down! May Viṣṇu follow you for the sake of food—one step. May Viṣṇu follow you for the sake of strength—two steps. May Viṣṇu follow you for the sake of the sacred vow—three steps. May Viṣṇu follow you for the sake of well-being—four steps. May Viṣṇu follow you for the sake of cattle—five steps. May Viṣṇu follow you for the sake of the increase of wealth—six steps. May Viṣṇu follow you for the sake of the seven priestly offices—seven steps. We have become friends through these seven steps; may I attain your friendship.

{3.7.7.12} Through friendship may I not be separated from you; through friendship may you not be separated from me. You are the Subrahmaṇyā. Of you, the earth is one foot. You are the Subrahmaṇyā. Of you, the intermediate space is one foot. You are the Subrahmaṇyā. Of you, the sky is one foot. You are the Subrahmaṇyā. Of you, the quarters are one foot.

{3.7.7.13} Beyond the dust is your fifth foot. May you milk for us food and vigor, splendor, sensory power, holy luster, and the eating of food. I measure you out, the one rich in milk—the well-milking cow of the gods, who does not kick back. Let Indra drink the Soma; may there be security for us. O men, come and prepare this altar, which is possessed of the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas.

{3.7.7.14} At the height of the sky, at the navel of the earth, so that this sacrificer may not come to harm, by the impulse of the god Savitṛ. The young woman with four crests, well-formed, with ghee as her face, in the midst of the world; upon her are seated two birds of beautiful wings. Of those two, the gods have their share. Drive away the fear of the people; turn back the wheels!

Go to the home of Soma! Indeed, you do not die here, nor do you suffer harm; you go to the gods by easy paths, where the doers of good deeds go, and not the doers of evil. There may the god Savitṛ establish you.

That brilliant light which was born beyond this region—may that carry us across our enemies. O Agni Vaiśvānara, Svāhā! From whatever you were afraid and stood back from, grant us safety from that; be gracious to all our offspring. Homage to Rudra, the bountiful! From whatever you were afraid and sat down from, grant us safety from that.

Be gracious to all creatures! Homage to Rudra, the bountiful! Rise up, O Dawn; stand firm, do not perish! Do not harm this sacrifice nor the sacrificer! Place the sacrificer in the world of heaven! Be auspicious to our bipeds, be auspicious to our quadrupeds! From whatever you were terrified, fled, or took refuge, from that grant us fearlessness! Be gracious to all creatures! Homage to Rudra, the bountiful!

{3.7.8.3} Homage to him who has done this! To him, svāhā! Indeed, you do not die here. You, the hopes; all the quarters. For you two are the seasonal ones of the sacrifice, Indra and Agni, of consciousness. Be satisfied with what is offered and what is unoffered; with the unoffered and the offered; with the offered and the unoffered; with the unoffered and the offered. O Indra and Agni, enjoy and drink of this soma; take pleasure in it! Let darkness not find the sacrificer.

Not the priests, nor these creatures; not he who would drink this Soma. Both [the priest and the drinker] have been made to mingle. Anuvāka 9 {3.7.9.1} We, being sinless, approach you, sent by Indra. May Vāyu be your portion; may Mitra be your portion; may Varuṇa be your portion.
