Kāma said to him: "O Prajāpati, you are indeed toiling because of Kāma. I am indeed Kāma. Sacrifice to me; then your desire will become true, and you shall find the heavenly world. He offered this cake on eight potsherds to Agni Kāma, a pap to Kāma, and a pap to Anumati. Thereupon his desire became true, and he found the heavenly world.

Truly, his desire becomes fulfilled; he finds the heavenly world—whoever sacrifices with this oblation and whoever knows it thus. He offers here: "To Agni, the Desire, svāhā! To Desire, svāhā! To Anumati, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To the heavenly world, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā!"

Brahmā said to him: "O Prajāpati, you are indeed toiling for the sake of the *brahman*. I am truly the *brahman*; worship me now. Then your sacrifice will be accompanied by the *brahman*, and you shall find the heavenly world. He then offered this cake on eight potsherds to Agni Kāma, a pap to Brahmā, and a pap to Anumati. Thereupon his sacrifice became accompanied by the *brahman*, and he found the heavenly world.

The sacrifice of one who performs this oblation becomes possessed of the *brahman*, and he finds the heavenly world—both he who sacrifices with this oblation and he who knows it thus. He offers here: "To Agni Kāma, svāhā! To the *brahman*, svāhā! To Anumati, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To the heavenly world, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā!"

{3.12.2.5} Sacrifice said to him: "O Prajāpati, you are indeed wearying yourself with sacrifice. I am truly the sacrifice; worship me now, and then your sacrifice will become effective; you shall attain the heavenly world. He then offered this cake on eight potsherds to Agni Kāma, a pap to Yajña, and a pap to Anumati. Thereupon, his sacrifice became effective, and he attained the heavenly world.

Truly, the sacrifice of one who performs this oblation becomes successful; he finds the heavenly world, both he who sacrifices with this oblation and he who knows it thus. He offers here: "To Agni Kāma, svāhā! To the Sacrifice, svāhā! To Anumati, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To the heavenly world, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā!"

The Waters said to him: "O Prajāpati, all desires are indeed supported in the waters; we are the Waters. Sacrifice to us, and then all desires will take refuge in you, and you shall find the world of heaven. He offered this cake on eight potsherds to Agni Kāma, a pap to the Waters, and a pap to Anumati. Then, indeed, all desires took refuge in him, and he found the world of heaven.

Verily, all desires rest upon this; he who sacrifices with this oblation, and he who knows it thus, finds the heavenly world. He offers here as follows: "To Agni, the desire, svāhā! To the waters, svāhā! To Anumati, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To the heavenly world, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā!"

Agni Balimān said to him: "O Prajāpati, all beings bring tribute to Agni Balimān. I indeed am Agni Balimān; worship me now, and then all beings will bring tribute to you, and you shall attain the heavenly world. He then offered this cake on eight potsherds to Agni Kāma, a pap to Agni Balimān, and a pap to Anumati.

Then indeed all beings brought him tribute; he found the world of heaven. Verily, all beings bring tribute to him who sacrifices with this oblation and who knows it thus. He offers here: "To Agni Kāma, svāhā! To Agni Balimat, svāhā! To Anumati, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To the world of heaven, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā!"

{3.12.2.8} Anuvitti said to him: "O Prajāpati, you indeed desire to find out the heavenly world. I am Anuvitti; worship me now, and then your finding out will become true; you shall find out the heavenly world. He then offered this cake on eight potsherds to Agni Kāma, a pap to Anuvitti, and a pap to Anumati. Thereupon, his finding out became true.

He discovered the heavenly world. Truly, his discovery becomes real; he who sacrifices with this oblation, and he who knows it thus, discovers the heavenly world. He offers here: "To Agni Kāma, svāhā! To Anuvitti, svāhā! To Anumati, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To the heavenly world, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā!"

{3.12.2.9} These, indeed, are the seven doors to the heavenly world, the paths of the sky known as the *diva-śyenas*. Hope guards the first; Desire, the second; the Brahman, the third; the Sacrifice, the fourth; the Waters, the fifth; Agni, the possessor of strength, the sixth; and Anuvitti, the seventh. Verily, he who performs these sacrifices, or he who knows them thus, finds the heavenly world for himself; he possesses free movement in the heavenly world.
In those [sacrifices], there is a search. One should give a four-year-old cow as the sacrificial fee, and a bronze vessel; and for a woman, a load-bearer for the sake of prosperity.

Anuvāka 3: The Cāturhotra Fire-altar Piling; The Vaiśvasṛja Fire-altar Piling {3.12.3.1} By austerity, the gods attained divinity in the beginning. By austerity, the seers found the heavenly light. By austerity, may we drive away our rivals and enemies. With that by which this entire universe is encompassed—whatever exists—we shall worship the first-born god with an oblation. That which is self-existent, the supreme Brahman, is austerity; he alone is the son, he is the father, he is the mother. Austerity indeed was the first miracle to come into being.
Through faith, a god attains godhood; faith is the goddess who is the foundation of the world.

{3.12.3.2} May she, being pleased, come to our sacrifice, yielding immortal nectar according to our desire—the goddess Śraddhā, the first-born of Cosmic Order (Ṛta), the sustainer of all, the foundation of the world. We worship that Śraddhā with an oblation; may she establish for us the immortal realm. The sovereign goddess, the mistress of the universe, has come, accepting this true oblation—from whom all the gods and the entire world were born—to him we pay homage with an oblation of clarified butter.

{3.12.3.3} So that we may rejoice in a feast together with the gods—He whose foundation is the wide mid-air, from whom the gods and all the worlds were born; that Truth has come to our sacrifice, shining forth, delighting in the offerings of prayer (*brahmāhutīḥ*). Under the control of the Mind, all this has come to be; it has not followed the control of another. For He is the formidable god, mightier than might; may He, being pleased, come to our sacrifice—the Lord of intentions and of thoughts.

Increasing here King Manas, the god Vipaschit, whose impetus is volition—we would abide in his invocation and in his good favor. The ancient, wide-spread, purifying path, by which the purified one crosses over evil deeds—purified by that pure purifier, may we cross over sin and hostility. The radiant door of the world, the purifier, full of light, shining, and glorious, yielding in many ways the stream of immortality.

May he establish for us a firm footing in the world, well-placed. Agni is the head of the earth. May Anumati follow us today; O Anumati, do thou indeed grant thy approval. [To thee] the bearer of oblations, the well-sacrificed.

Anuvāka 4: The Cāturhotra Fire-piling and the Vaiśvasṛja Fire-piling {3.12.4.1} The heavenly world, indeed, became hidden from the gods. They said to Prajāpati: "O Prajāpati, the heavenly world has become hidden from us; seek it out! He sought it by means of sacrificial rites (*yajñakratu*). He did not find it by means of sacrificial rites. He sought it by means of *iṣṭi* offerings. He found it by means of *iṣṭi* offerings. That is the reason for the name *iṣṭi* of the *iṣṭis*.
They are indeed called *iṣṭayas*; they are referred to as *iṣṭayas* cryptically, for the gods, as it were, love the cryptic.

Tapaḥ said to him: "O Prajāpati, you are indeed wearying yourself with ascetic toil (tapas). I am indeed Tapaḥ; worship me now, and then your ascetic toil will become true; you shall find the heavenly world. He offered this oblation: a cake on eight potsherds for Agni, a pap for Tapaḥ, and a pap for Anumati. Thereupon his ascetic toil became true, and he found the heavenly world. Truly, his ascetic toil becomes true.

He who sacrifices with this oblation, and he who knows it thus, finds the heavenly world. He offers here as follows: "To Agni, svāhā! To Tapas, svāhā! To Anumati, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To the heavenly world, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā!"

Faith said to him: "O Prajāpati, you toil indeed with faith. I am Faith; sacrifice to me, and then your faith will become true, and you will find the heavenly world. He offered this oblation: a cake on eight potsherds for Agni, a pap for Faith, and a pap for Anumati. Thereupon, his faith became true, and he found the heavenly world.

Truly, his faith becomes established; he finds the heavenly world—whoever sacrifices with this oblation and whoever knows it thus. He offers here: "To Agni, svāhā! To Faith, svāhā! To Anumati, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To the heavenly world, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā!"

He said to Satya: "O Prajāpati, you indeed toil for the sake of truth; I too am truth. Sacrifice to me now! Then your truth will become true, and you shall find the heavenly world. He offered this oblation of eight potsherds to Agni, a pap to Satya, and a pap to Anumati. Thereupon, his truth became true, and he found the heavenly world.

Truly, his truth becomes established; he finds the heavenly world—he who sacrifices with this oblation and he who knows it thus. He offers here: "To Agni, svāhā! To Truth, svāhā! To Anumati, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To the heavenly world, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā!"

Mind spoke to him: "O Prajāpati, you are indeed wearying yourself with the mind. I am Mind; sacrifice to me now, and then your mind will become true; you shall find the heavenly world. He offered this oblation: a cake on eight potsherds for Agni, a pap for Mind, and a pap for Anumati. Thereupon his mind became true, and he found the heavenly world. Truly, his mind becomes true.

He who sacrifices with this oblation, and he who knows it thus, finds the heavenly world. He offers here as follows: "To Agni, svāhā! To Manas, svāhā! To Anumati, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To the heavenly world, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā!"

He said to Caraṇa: "O Prajāpati, you are indeed wearying yourself with Caraṇa. I am truly Caraṇa; sacrifice to me now, and then your Caraṇa will become true; you shall find the heavenly world. He offered this oblation: a cake on eight potsherds to Agni, a pap to Caraṇa, and a pap to Anumati. Thereupon, his Caraṇa became true, and he found the heavenly world.

Truly, his conduct becomes truthful; he finds the heavenly world, whoever sacrifices with this oblation and whoever knows it thus. He offers here: "To Agni, svāhā! To Conduct, svāhā! To Anumati, svāhā! To Prajāpati, svāhā! To the heavenly world, svāhā! To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā!"

These, indeed, are the five gates to the heavenly world, known as the *apāghā* and *anuvittayaḥ*. Austerity guards the first; faith, the second; truth, the third; the mind, the fourth; and conduct, the fifth. Verily, he who sacrifices with these offerings finds the heavenly world; for him there is freedom of movement in the heavenly world, both he who sacrifices with these offerings and he who knows them thus.
In connection with these offerings, one should give a four-year-old cow and a bronze vessel, and also a load for a woman, for the sake of prosperity.

Anuvāka 5: The Cāturhotrā Agnicayana and the Vaiśvasṛja Agnicayana {3.12.5.1} The *caturhotṛ* formulas are indeed the Brahman. From the *caturhotṛ* formulas the sacrifice was fashioned. Neither a curse nor sorcery reaches him who knows this. He who truly knows the "four-hotṛ-ness" of the *caturhotṛ* formulas, as well as their "five-hotṛ-ness"—all the quarters become favorable to him. Vācaspati is the Hotṛ of the ten *hotṛ* formulas; Pṛthivī is the Hotṛ of the four *hotṛ* formulas.

Agni is the Hotṛ of the five Hotṛs; Speech is the Hotṛ of the six Hotṛs; Mahāhavis is the Hotṛ of the seven Hotṛs. This indeed is the "four-hotṛ-ness" of the four-hotṛ formulas, as well as their "five-hotṛ-ness. For him who knows this, all the quarters become favorable. This is indeed all knowledge; this is the remedy; this is the fivefold path, the direct way, the track leading to the heavenly world.

He who studies these [hymns], even if he lacks a roof over his head, goes to heaven as far as his strength permits, provided he does not speak ill of others; he reaches a full lifespan, obtains offspring, and gains abundance of wealth and lordship over cattle. He becomes endowed with the splendor of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcas*). He who studies these protects himself, his offspring, and his ancestors. Indeed, Aruṇa Aupaveśi discovered these.

{3.12.5.4} By means of these, he overcame censure and, moreover, all evil; he went to the heavenly world. Whoever studies these [hymns] overcomes censure and, moreover, all evil; he goes to the heavenly world. One desiring heaven should pile the fire-altar with these; one desiring long life, or one desiring offspring and cattle, should do so with these.

{3.12.5.5} To the east, he places the Daśahotṛ facing north for as many steps as there are; [he places] the Hṛdaya, the Yajus-formulas, and the two Patnīs. To the south, the Caturhotṛ facing east. To the west, the Pañcahotṛ facing north. To the north, the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ facing east. Above, the Saptahotṛ facing east; [he places] the Hṛdaya, the Yajus-formulas, and the Patnīs. He places the Grahas according to available space, the Pratigrahas according to available space, and the Lokampṛṇās.
Indeed, all these deities become pleased and gratified for him.

One piles the fire-altar together with the gods. It should be piled commensurate with a chariot; for the chariot is indeed the thunderbolt. By means of the thunderbolt, he strikes down evil and the rival. It should be piled commensurate with a wing; for the chariot is only as large as its wing. Thus, he piles it commensurate with a chariot. By means of the animal sacrifice (*paśubandha*), he conquers this very world; and also by means of the *agniṣṭoma*.

He wins the intermediate space by the Ukthya; heaven by the Atirātra; all the worlds by the Ahīna, and also by the Sattra. The sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) is a boon (*vara*); by means of a boon he wins a boon, for the self is indeed the boon. He gives twenty-one sacrificial fees; the heavenly world from here is the twenty-first; he attains the heavenly world.

That sun is the twenty-first. He attains that very sun. He gives a hundred; man has a lifespan of a hundred years and a hundredfold power. He thus establishes himself in life and power. He gives a thousand; the heavenly world is commensurate with a thousand. It is for the conquest of the heavenly world. He gives sacrificial gifts (dakṣiṇā) for every brick; [thereby he obtains] all ages.

{3.12.5.9} For the attainment of everything; for the securing of everything. If he should not find [a suitable gift], he should give as many stirred-drinks (mantha) or cooked rice (odana) as there would be [cows]. He attains that desire for which the fire-altar is built. However, he should give a pregnant four-year-old cow (ṣaṣṭhauhī), for she indeed contains all ages. It is for the attainment of everything; for the securing of everything.

He gives gold; verily, with gold as his light, he goes to the heavenly world. He gives a garment; by that he prolongs his life. One should sacrifice on the third layer of the altar; for the gods are threefold in truth. He piles the fire-altar in accordance with truth. One should state this Brāhmaṇa in connection with the animal sacrifice (Paśubandha), but not in other sacrifices. Verily, he who knows the four Hotṛ-priests who are to be satisfied at each pressing (anusavana) [attains success].

He prospers with offspring and cattle; the drinking of Soma inclines toward him. These indeed are the *caturhotṛ* formulas that must be satisfied at each pressing. As for those Brahmins who are learned in many [Vedic] sciences—if one were not to bring sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*) to them, the sacrifice would be ill-performed; they would seize his fire. To them he should give according to his faith; thus the sacrifice is made well-performed, and they do not seize his fire.

{3.12.5.12} There is a golden brick. It is as large as the highest finger-joint, commensurate with the joints of the sacrifice. Gold is brilliance. If one should not find gold, one should place pebbles smeared with ghee; ghee is brilliance. Thus, he piles the fire-altar endowed with brilliance. Having piled the fire-altar, one should sacrifice with the Sautrāmaṇī or with the Maitrāvaruṇī [offering]. For he who piles the fire-altar is deprived of his virility.

{3.12.5.13} He bestows upon him whatever vigor there is. He attains union with Brahman and residence in the same world as Brahman. He who piles this fire, and he who knows it thus, attains union with these very deities, equal power, and residence in the same world. This indeed is the Brāhmaṇa for the Sāvitra [fire], and likewise for the Nāciketa.

Anuvāka 6: The Cāturhotra Fire-piling and the Vaiśvasṛja Fire-piling {3.12.6.1} That which is immortal and that which is mortal; that which breathes and that which does not—having made all these into bricks, I place them upon the wish-fulfilling cow. By that seer, by that sacred formulation (brahman), by that deity—sit firm like Aṅgiras! All women, all men, and whatever is neither woman nor man—all those [are the bricks]. As many as are the particles of dust of the earth, so many are they.

{3.12.6.2} All those [grains] have been numbered by divine power. As many as there are grains of salt for cattle, all those are established as the prosperity upon the earth. All those [grains] are as many as all the sands, and those which are contained within the waters—all those are as many as the pebbles for the sake of stability upon this earth.

All those [stones], as many stones as there are on this earth, established in their foundations—all those. All those plants, as many as all the plants are, spread over the earth—all those. All those herbs, as many as all the herbs are, spread over the earth—all those.

As many trees as there are upon this earth—all those; as many domestic animals as there are, and all those that are wild—all those; those that are two-footed, four-footed, footless, or those that crawl on their bellies—all those; as much as is called ointment.

Whatever belongs to the gods and whatever belongs to humans—all those [are yours], as far as all iron; whatever belongs to the gods and whatever belongs to humans—all those [are yours], as far as all bronze; whatever belongs to the gods and whatever belongs to humans—all those [are yours], all lead, and all tin; whatever belongs to the gods and whatever belongs to humans.

All of them—every piece of gold and silver, whether belonging to the gods or to humans—all of them; every piece of gold and bronze, whether belonging to the gods or to humans—all of them, having made these into bricks, he placed them near the wish-fulfilling cow. With that seer, with that sacred formulation (*brahman*), with that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras!

Anuvāka 7: The Cāturhotra Fire-piling and the Vaiśvasṛja Fire-piling {3.12.7.1} All the quarters and that which exists established within the quarters—all these, having made them into bricks, I place here as wish-fulfilling cows. With that seer, with that sacred formulation (brahman), with that deity—sit firm like Aṅgiras! And the intermediate space alone, and whatever is deposited within it—all those, and the creatures belonging to the intermediate space.

And those who are the Gandharvas and Apsarases—all of them; all the noble waters established in the intermediate space—all of them; all the noble waters; those which are stationary and those which are migratory—all of them; all the roaring rivers, all the torrents; and the cold that falls as snow.

All those [streams], all the spreading rays of light, and the mist that falls—all those; all the lightning flashes, all the thunders, and the hailstones that fall—all those; all the flowing rivers and whatever moves within the waters—all those.

Those waters that are from wells, those from rivers, those from the ocean, those from ponds, and those from springs—all of them; those clouds that rise up, and those rains that fall—all of them; heat, brilliance, and space, and whatever is established in space—all of them; the wind and all birds.

And that which moves in the intermediate space—all those [beings], Agni, Sūrya, Candramas, Mitra, Varuṇa, and Bhaga—all those; truth, faith, austerity, self-control, and the name and form of all beings—all those, having made them into bricks, he places near the wish-fulfilling cow. With that seer, with that Brahman, with that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras!

Anuvāka 8: The Cāturhotra Fire-altar Piling, the Vaiśvasṛja Fire-altar Piling {3.12.8.1} The entire sky, all the gods in heaven, and whatever being is established within [the earth]—having made all these into bricks, I place them upon the wish-fulfilling cow. With that seer, with that sacred formulation (brahman), with that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras! As many stars as there are, all spread out in the luminous realm of heaven—all those are the Ṛg-verses, the Yajus-formulas, and the Sāman-chants.

Whatever belongs to the Atharvans and Aṅgirasas—all those; and the Itihāsas and Purāṇas—all those; and whatever serpents and divine beings—all those; and whatever worlds and non-worlds—contained within, established in the Earth—all those; and whatever is Brahman and whatever is non-Brahman—contained within, established in Brahman.

All those—every day and night, and all the half-months; all those—all the seasons, all the months, and the entire year; all those—all that has been (O Ānanda, that which has been) and all that is to be, and whatever shall come after this—having made all these into bricks, he placed them upon the wish-fulfilling cow. With that seer, with that Brahman, with that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras!

Anuvāka 9: The Cāturhotra Fire-piling and the Vaiśvasṛja Fire-piling {3.12.9.1} The eastern direction is said to be the great domain of the *ṛc* verses; they say the southern direction is the boundless domain of the *yajus* formulas; the western direction is that of the *Atharvans* and *Aṅgirases*; the northern direction is said to be the great domain of the *sāmans*. By means of the *ṛcs*, the God moves in the sky in the forenoon; he stands upon the *Yajurveda* at midday; he is magnified by the *Sāmaveda* at sunset. The Sun goes forth never empty of the three Vedas.
They say that form is born in every way from the *Ṛg* verses; indeed, all movement is eternally of the nature of the *Yajus*.

All splendor is indeed eternal in its form; bliss is indeed eternal. All this was created by Brahman alone. They say the Vaiśya caste was born from the *Ṛgveda*; they say the *Yajurveda* is the source of the Kṣatriya; the *Sāmaveda* is the progenitor of the Brāhmaṇas. Those of old spoke these words to those before them as they were building the fire-altar like a mirror. The ancient world-creators, the immortals, remained consecrated for a sacrificial session (*sattra*) for a hundred thousand years.

Austerity was the Gṛhapati priest; the Brahman itself became the Brahman priest. Truth indeed was their Hotṛ priest when they sat as the creators of the universe. Immortality sang the Udgītha for them for a thousand years. The past was their Prastotṛ priest; he brought forward the future. Breath became the Adhvaryu priest for those desiring to win all this.

The wise apāna, being encompassed, stood firm at the sacrifice. The seasons were the singers; the ṛtu-sacrificers became the members of the assembly (sadasya). The half-months and the months became the cup-bearers (camasādhvaryu). The splendor of the Brahman was the reciter (acchāvāka); glory became the acchāvāka. Truth was their praśāstṛ when the creators of the universe sat down.

Sustenance bore the King; he became the protector of the firm foundation through power. Vital force praised the pressing-stones when the creators of the universe sat down. Honor performed the sacrifice for the office of the *potṛ*; Splendor performed the sacrifice for the office of the *neṣṭṛ*. From the office of the *āgnīdh*, the knowing one [performed] the truth. Faith herself indeed performed the sacrifice. *Irā* was the wife of the creators of the universe; Intention bound the oblation.

Hunger and thirst brought the sacrificial fuel for them, both of them fierce. Speech was their *subrahmaṇyā* priest, knowing the application of the meters and weaving the ritual manuals (*kalpatantrāṇi*) and the terminations of the days in every respect. Day and night were the two guardians of the cattle; the moments (*muhūrtas*) became the attendants. Death was the Ordainer (*dhātṛ*); the fierce Lord of the People was the immolator (*śamitṛ*).

The first creators of the universe performed a sacrificial session (*sattra*), proceeding with a thousand-fold libation. From that was born the guardian of the world, the golden bird named Brahman, by whom the sun shines, kindled with splendor. Father possessing a son through a son, [he exists] in womb after womb. One who does not know the Veda does not comprehend that Great One, the Self who pervades all, in the hereafter. This is the eternal majesty of the Brahmin: he increases not by action, nor does he diminish.

{3.12.9.8} His very self is the knower of the path; having known him, one is not smeared by evil action. There are five sets of fifty threefold years, five sets of fifty fifteenfold years, five sets of fifty seventeenfold years, and five sets of fifty twenty-one-fold years. This is the thousand-year sacrifice of the creators of the universe (*viśvasṛj*). By means of this, indeed, the creators of the universe created this entire universe. Because they created the universe, they are called the "creators of the universe."

The universe is born after them. They attain union with Brahman and residence in the same world as Brahman; they attain union with these very deities, equal power, and residence in the same world as those deities—those who practice this, those who proclaim it, and those to whom they proclaim it.
